column3: The word that answers 什么颜色 and takes 深 or 浅 for a shade (颜色很深). A named color adds 色: 红色, 蓝色, 绿色. 色 began as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was only later borrowed for its sound to mean color.
column7: What color do you like?
column9: The word that answers 什麼顏色 and takes 深 or 淺 for a shade (顏色很深). A named color adds 色: 紅色, 藍色, 綠色. 色 began as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was only later borrowed for its sound to mean color.

column3: The color named as a noun (我最喜欢白色); before another noun it takes 的 (白色的衣服), though 白 alone also works (白衬衫). It has a political sense too: 白色恐怖 is the "White Terror" of harsh repression. Alone, 白 also means in vain or free of charge, as in "to come for nothing".
column6: Wǒmen jiā de qiáng shì báisè de.
column7: The walls of our home are white.
column9: The color named as a noun (我最喜歡白色); before another noun it takes 的 (白色的衣服), though 白 alone also works (白襯衫). It has a political sense too: 白色恐怖 is the "White Terror" of harsh repression. Alone, 白 also means in vain or free of charge, as in "to come for nothing".

column3: Works as an adjective by itself (头发很黑), and 天黑了 is the everyday way to say night is falling, with 了 marking the change. The color noun is 黑色, and 黑 leads words such as 黑板 and 黑夜. The computing sense, as in 黑客, matches both the meaning and the sound of English "hack".
column6: Tiān hēi le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.
column7: It's dark, let's go home.
column9: Works as an adjective by itself (頭髮很黑), and 天黑了 is the everyday way to say night is falling, with 了 marking the change. The color noun is 黑色, and 黑 leads words such as 黑板 and 黑夜. The computing sense, as in 黑客, matches both the meaning and the sound of English "hack".

column3: The color as a noun (我喜欢黑色); before a noun it takes 的 (黑色的包) or is shortened to 黑 (黑头发). In fixed phrases it can be figurative: 黑色幽默 is "black humor" and 黑色星期五 is "Black Friday". 色 began as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was only later borrowed for its sound to mean color.
column4: 她穿了一件黑色的外套。
column5: 她穿了一件黑色的外套。
column6: Tā chuān le yī jiàn hēisè de wàitào.
column7: She put on a black coat.
column9: The color as a noun (我喜歡黑色); before a noun it takes 的 (黑色的包) or is shortened to 黑 (黑頭髮). In fixed phrases it can be figurative: 黑色幽默 is "black humor" and 黑色星期五 is "Black Friday". 色 began as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was only later borrowed for its sound to mean color.

column3: An adjective that takes 很 and 了 (她的脸红了 "she blushed"). Red means luck and celebration, so 红包 is the cash gift in a red envelope; but 红茶 is black tea, not "red tea". It first meant lighter shades of red and only gradually replaced 赤 as the basic color word.
column7: Her face turned red.
column9: An adjective that takes 很 and 了 (她的臉紅了 "she blushed"). Red means luck and celebration, so 紅包 is the cash gift in a red envelope; but 紅茶 is black tea, not "red tea". It first meant lighter shades of red and only gradually replaced 赤 as the basic color word.

column3: The color as a noun (我喜欢红色) or before a noun with 的 (红色的车). Red is the color of luck and joy, so it fills 春节 decorations and weddings; the "revolutionary" sense appears in 红色经典, a name for classic mainland works. 色 has a colloquial second reading, shǎi, when it means color.
column6: Hóngsè de chē shì wǒ de.
column7: The red car is mine.
column9: The color as a noun (我喜歡紅色) or before a noun with 的 (紅色的車). Red is the color of luck and joy, so it fills 春節 decorations and weddings; the "revolutionary" sense appears in 紅色經典, a name for classic mainland works. 色 has a colloquial second reading, shǎi, when it means color.

column3: An adjective that changes state with 了 (香蕉黄了 "the bananas have ripened"). Some compounds are not what they seem: 黄瓜 is a cucumber, 黄油 is butter, and 黄牛 is an ox or a ticket scalper. The river is 黄河. One scholar proposes that 黄 began as a picture of a semicircular jade (璜) and came to mean yellow by borrowing.
column7: In autumn the leaves have all turned yellow.
column9: An adjective that changes state with 了 (香蕉黃了 "the bananas have ripened"). Some compounds are not what they seem: 黃瓜 is a cucumber, 黃油 is butter, and 黃牛 is an ox or a ticket scalper. The river is 黃河. One scholar proposes that 黃 began as a picture of a semicircular jade (璜) and came to mean yellow by borrowing.

column3: Often with 的 before a noun (黄色的花), though it is as often left out (黄色衣服). The word has a second, slangy sense: 黄色网站 or 黄色电影 is not yellow but pornographic.
column6: Tā yǒu yī zhī huángsè de māo.
column7: He has a yellow cat.
column9: Often with 的 before a noun (黃色的花), though it is as often left out (黃色衣服). The word has a second, slangy sense: 黃色網站 or 黃色電影 is not yellow but pornographic.

column3: Describes things directly (天很蓝) and fills fixed words: 蓝天 for a clear blue sky, 蓝牙 for Bluetooth, 蓝莓 for blueberries. The color noun is 蓝色.
column7: The sky is especially blue today.
column9: Describes things directly (天很藍) and fills fixed words: 藍天 for a clear blue sky, 藍牙 for Bluetooth, 藍莓 for blueberries. The color noun is 藍色.

column3: The color as a noun (我喜欢蓝色) or before a noun with 的 (蓝色的鞋). A shade goes in front: 浅蓝色 light blue, 深蓝色 dark blue, 天蓝色 sky blue.
column6: Tā de xīn shūbāo shì lánsè de.
column7: His new school bag is blue.
column9: The color as a noun (我喜歡藍色) or before a noun with 的 (藍色的鞋). A shade goes in front: 淺藍色 light blue, 深藍色 dark blue, 天藍色 sky blue.

column3: Typed lv on most keyboards. Used for traffic lights (绿灯) and for things turning green (树都绿了). Careful with 绿帽子: giving someone a "green hat" says that their partner is cheating. In modern times it gave rise to 氯, the character for chlorine.
column6: Chūntiān lái le, shù dōu lǜ le.
column7: Spring has come and the trees have all turned green.
column9: Typed lv on most keyboards. Used for traffic lights (綠燈) and for things turning green (樹都綠了). Careful with 綠帽子: giving someone a "green hat" says that their partner is cheating. In modern times it gave rise to 氯, the character for chlorine.

column3: Beyond the color, it means environmentally friendly or pollution-free: 绿色食品, 绿色出行. Before a plain noun it takes 的 (绿色的树) or is shortened to 绿 (绿叶). 色 began as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was only later borrowed for its sound to mean color.
column6: Tā de chē shì lǜsè de.
column7: His car is green.
column9: Beyond the color, it means environmentally friendly or pollution-free: 綠色食品, 綠色出行. Before a plain noun it takes 的 (綠色的樹) or is shortened to 綠 (綠葉). 色 began as a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was only later borrowed for its sound to mean color.

column3: The everyday word for spring. A season word works like a time word, before the verb (春天去公园) or at the start of a sentence; 春季 is the written term, and 春 alone appears in 春节, 春风 and 青春. The grass 艸 at the top of 春 has merged with 屯; the older form 萅 still keeps the grass clear.
column6: Chūntiān lái le, huā kāi le.
column7: Spring has come and the flowers are out.
column9: The everyday word for spring. A season word works like a time word, before the verb (春天去公園) or at the start of a sentence; 春季 is the written term, and 春 alone appears in 春節, 春風 and 青春. The grass 艸 at the top of 春 has merged with 屯; the older form 萅 still keeps the grass clear.

column3: The everyday word for summer. Like other time words it goes before the verb (夏天我常去游泳); 夏季 is the written term, and 夏 alone appears in 初夏 and 夏令营, a summer camp. 夏 is also the name of the Xia dynasty and a surname. Some scholars read an old form with 日 and 頁 as a man under the scorching sun, though that is uncertain.
column7: In summer I often go swimming.
column9: The everyday word for summer. Like other time words it goes before the verb (夏天我常去游泳); 夏季 is the written term, and 夏 alone appears in 初夏 and 夏令營, a summer camp. 夏 is also the name of the Xia dynasty and a surname. Some scholars read an old form with 日 and 頁 as a man under the scorching sun, though that is uncertain.

column3: The everyday word; 秋 alone shows up in set phrases such as 秋风 and 中秋, and 秋季 is the formal one for schedules and forecasts. Like other time words it goes before the verb: 秋天去爬山. The oldest forms of 秋 show a cricket or a locust.
column7: The weather is nice in autumn.
column9: The everyday word; 秋 alone shows up in set phrases such as 秋風 and 中秋, and 秋季 is the formal one for schedules and forecasts. Like other time words it goes before the verb: 秋天去爬山. The oldest forms of 秋 show a cricket or a locust.

column3: The everyday word for winter, used before the verb like other time words (冬天下雪). 冬季 is the written term (冬季运动 for winter sports), and 冬 alone appears in 冬至, the winter solstice. 冬 is possibly related to 终, to end. 冬 can also stand for 鼕, which imitates the sound of beating a drum.
column6: Dōngtiān hěn lěng, yào duō chuān yīfu.
column7: Winter is cold, so wear more clothes.
column9: The everyday word for winter, used before the verb like other time words (冬天下雪). 冬季 is the written term (冬季運動 for winter sports), and 冬 alone appears in 冬至, the winter solstice. 冬 is possibly related to 終, to end. 冬 can also stand for 鼕, which imitates the sound of beating a drum.

column3: The official name of the Lunar New Year holiday, more exact than 新年, which can also mean January 1. People say 过年 for celebrating it, and greet each other with 春节快乐. 节 is also the word for the solar terms, the 24 divisions of the traditional calendar year, besides seasonal festivals.
column6: Chūnjié wǒ xiǎng huí lǎojiā kànkan.
column7: At Spring Festival I want to go back to my hometown.
column9: The official name of the Lunar New Year holiday, more exact than 新年, which can also mean January 1. People say 過年 for celebrating it, and greet each other with 春節快樂. 節 is also the word for the solar terms, the 24 divisions of the traditional calendar year, besides seasonal festivals.

column3: A verb and its object, so 过年 takes no object of its own; 过年好 is the greeting and 过年了 says the holiday is here. 过 means to spend a holiday in a pattern of its own: 过生日, 过节, 过年. 过 is also the light particle guo for past experience (吃过), unlike the guò of this word.
column4: 过年的时候，我们吃饺子。
column5: 過年的時候，我們吃餃子。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, wǒmen chī jiǎozi.
column7: At New Year we eat dumplings.
column9: A verb and its object, so 過年 takes no object of its own; 過年好 is the greeting and 過年了 says the holiday is here. 過 means to spend a holiday in a pattern of its own: 過生日, 過節, 過年. 過 is also the light particle guo for past experience (吃過), unlike the guò of this word.

column3: The general word for a festival or holiday, while 节 follows each name (春节, 中秋节, 母亲节). Use 节日快乐 to greet someone on any of them. A 节日 is not always a day off: days off are 假日. 日 is a picture of the sun, with a line in the middle added to tell it from 口.
column4: 春节是中国最重要的节日。
column5: 春節是中國最重要的節日。
column6: Chūnjié shì Zhōngguó zuì zhòngyào de jiérì.
column7: Spring Festival is the most important festival in China.
column9: The general word for a festival or holiday, while 節 follows each name (春節, 中秋節, 母親節). Use 節日快樂 to greet someone on any of them. A 節日 is not always a day off: days off are 假日. 日 is a picture of the sun, with a line in the middle added to tell it from 口.

column3: Three jobs: the last syllable of a festival's name (中秋节, 母亲节); a measure word for class periods and sections (一节课, 一节车厢); and "saving", as in 节约 and 节水. A show or program is 节目.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu liǎng jié kè.
column7: I have two classes today.
column9: Three jobs: the last syllable of a festival's name (中秋節, 母親節); a measure word for class periods and sections (一節課, 一節車廂); and "saving", as in 節約 and 節水. A show or program is 節目.

column3: Falling snow takes 下: 下雪, and the amount goes before it (雪下得很大). Also 雪人 for a snowman, 滑雪 for skiing, and in writing 雪耻 for wiping out a disgrace. 雪 is an ancient simplification of 䨮, whose sound part was 彗.
column7: The snow is coming down hard.
column9: Falling snow takes 下: 下雪, and the amount goes before it (雪下得很大). Also 雪人 for a snowman, 滑雪 for skiing, and in writing 雪恥 for wiping out a disgrace. 雪 is an ancient simplification of 䨮, whose sound part was 彗.

column3: Weather that falls takes 下: 下雨, 下雪. 了 marks that it has begun (下雪了), and the amount goes before 雪: 下大雪, 下小雪. The snow already lying on the ground is just 雪, as in 雪很厚. 下 is thought to go back to an old word meaning to fall.
column7: It snowed last night.
column9: Weather that falls takes 下: 下雨, 下雪. 了 marks that it has begun (下雪了), and the amount goes before 雪: 下大雪, 下小雪. The snow already lying on the ground is just 雪, as in 雪很厚. 下 is thought to go back to an old word meaning to fall.

column3: Clouds are counted with 朵: 一朵云. 白云 is white clouds and 乌云 dark storm clouds. Today 云 also means cloud computing, as in 云端 and 云盘. 云 was the original character for cloud; 雨 was added on top, making 雲, to tell it apart from the borrowed sense, to speak.
column7: There are a lot of clouds in the sky.
column9: Clouds are counted with 朵: 一朵雲. 白雲 is white clouds and 烏雲 dark storm clouds. Today 雲 also means cloud computing, as in 雲端. 云 was the original character for cloud; 雨 was added on top to tell it apart from the borrowed sense, to speak.

column3: A forecast word between 晴 and 阴: sunny, cloudy, overcast. Forecasts string them together: 多云转晴 "cloudy turning sunny", 晴转多云 the reverse. 多 began as two pieces of meat, which later turned into two 夕.
column7: Tomorrow will be cloudy, with no rain.
column9: A forecast word between 晴 and 陰: sunny, cloudy, overcast. Forecasts string them together: 多雲轉晴 "cloudy turning sunny", 晴轉多雲 the reverse. 多 began as two pieces of meat, which later turned into two 夕.

column3: A weather word (天阴了 "it has clouded over", the opposite of 晴) that also pairs with 阳 as yin and yang, shade and sun. It marks the hidden or dark side in words such as 阴谋 "plot". The 月 in 阴 is not the moon: it replaced the part 侌 of the older form.
column6: Tiān yīn le, kěnéng yào xià yǔ.
column7: It has turned overcast, and it may rain.
column9: A weather word (天陰了 "it has clouded over", the opposite of 晴) that also pairs with 陽 as yin and yang, shade and sun. It marks the hidden or dark side in words such as 陰謀 "plot".

column3: 天 here means the day's weather. The pattern is 晴天, 阴天, 雨天, 雪天; say 今天是阴天 or just 今天阴天. In forecasts 阴 is fully covered, while 多云 is partly cloudy. 天 began as a front-facing standing man (大), drawn with different marks for the head.
column4: 阴天的时候，我不太想出门。
column5: 陰天的時候，我不太想出門。
column6: Yīntiān de shíhou, wǒ bù tài xiǎng chūmén.
column7: On overcast days I don't much feel like going out.
column9: 天 here means the day's weather. The pattern is 晴天, 陰天, 雨天, 雪天; say 今天是陰天 or just 今天陰天. In forecasts 陰 is fully covered, while 多雲 is partly cloudy. 天 began as a front-facing standing man (大), drawn with different marks for the head.

column3: Said of weather and the sky, never of people: 天晴了, 放晴 "clear up" (雨停了，天放晴了). 晴朗 is the written "clear and bright", and 雨过天晴 the idiom for the sky clearing after rain. The Classic of Poetry writes 晴 as 星, and one scholar thinks it comes from 星: becoming starry, then clearing.
column6: Yǔ tíng le, tiān qíng le.
column7: The rain stopped and the sky cleared.
column9: Said of weather and the sky, never of people: 天晴了, 放晴 "clear up" (雨停了，天放晴了). 晴朗 is the written "clear and bright", and 雨過天晴 the idiom for the sky clearing after rain. The Classic of Poetry writes 晴 as 星, and one scholar thinks it comes from 星: becoming starry, then clearing.

column3: The standard forecast word, the opposite of 阴天; 明天是晴天 is a typical line. 晴天霹雳 is the idiom for a bolt from the blue, a sudden shock.
column4: 明天是晴天，我们去爬山。
column5: 明天是晴天，我們去爬山。
column6: Míngtiān shì qíngtiān, wǒmen qù páshān.
column7: Tomorrow will be sunny, so let's go hiking.
column9: The standard forecast word, the opposite of 陰天; 明天是晴天 is a typical line. 晴天霹靂 is the idiom for a bolt from the blue, a sudden shock.

column3: Mildly cold, often pleasant, and less cold than 冷. 凉快 is "nicely cool", and 饭凉了 means the food has gone cold. 凉 and 冷 are related words that differ mainly in their vowel.
column4: 天气凉了，多穿一件衣服。
column5: 天氣涼了，多穿一件衣服。
column6: Tiānqì liáng le, duō chuān yī jiàn yīfu.
column7: The weather has turned cool, so put on another layer.
column9: Mildly cold, often pleasant, and less cold than 冷. 涼快 is "nicely cool", and 飯涼了 means the food has gone cold. 涼 and 冷 are related words that differ mainly in their vowel.

column3: Cool in the comfortable way, like shade or an evening breeze after a hot day; 冷 is cold you do not want. As a verb it doubles up, 凉快凉快 "cool off a bit", and 一边凉快去 is a rude "go stay out of it".
column4: 晚上很凉快，我们出去走走吧。
column5: 晚上很涼快，我們出去走走吧。
column6: Wǎnshang hěn liángkuai, wǒmen chūqù zǒuzou ba.
column7: It's nice and cool in the evening; let's go for a walk.
column9: Cool in the comfortable way, like shade or an evening breeze after a hot day; 冷 is cold you do not want. As a verb it doubles up, 涼快涼快 "cool off a bit", and 一邊涼快去 is a rude "go stay out of it".

column3: The number goes between 零下 and 度: 零下五度. Forecasts also say 负五度 or 零下五摄氏度, and 零上 "above zero" is rarely needed, since people just give the number. 零 first meant a little bit of rain, and in 1248 a mathematician used it as a placeholder, as in 三百零二, which led to its meaning zero.
column6: Jīntiān língxià wǔ dù, tài lěng le.
column7: It's five below zero today, which is too cold.
column9: The number goes between 零下 and 度: 零下五度. Forecasts also say 負五度 or 零下五攝氏度, and 零上 "above zero" is rarely needed, since people just give the number. 零 first meant a little bit of rain, and in 1248 a mathematician used it as a placeholder, as in 三百零二, which led to its meaning zero.

column3: The forecast word for the air outside: 最高气温 and 最低气温, which rise or fall (气温下降). For water, a room or a body use 温度 (body temperature is 体温), not 气温. 温 also means to review a lesson.
column7: The temperature will drop tomorrow.
column9: The forecast word for the air outside: 最高氣溫 and 最低氣溫, which rise or fall (氣溫下降). For water, a room or a body use 溫度 (body temperature is 體溫), not 氣溫. 溫 also means to review a lesson.

column3: Temperature of anything: the air, water, a room (房间的温度). It goes with 高 and 低 or 升 and 降, and a thermometer is 温度计. 气温 is for the outdoor air only. 度 is read duó in the verb meaning to estimate (duò in Taiwan).
column7: The temperature in this room is just right.
column9: Temperature of anything: the air, water, a room (房間的溫度). It goes with 高 and 低 or 升 and 降, and a thermometer is 溫度計. 氣溫 is for the outdoor air only. 度 is read duó in the verb meaning to estimate (duò in Taiwan).

column3: The everyday word for the sun and its light: 太阳出来了, and 晒太阳 means to bask in the sun. 阳 is light in speech (tàiyang), and 阳光 is "sunlight" (阳光很好). 太 is just 大 with a dot added, to say "too big".
column7: The sun comes up from the east.
column9: The everyday word for the sun and its light: 太陽出來了, and 曬太陽 means to bask in the sun. 陽 is light in speech (tàiyang), and 陽光 is "sunlight" (陽光很好). 太 is just 大 with a dot added, to say "too big".

column3: 月 alone can mean the moon or a month (一个月), so 月亮 is the clear word for the moon itself. The second syllable is light (yuèliang). Moonlight is 月光, and the moon is full when it is 圆. 月 pictures a crescent moon, but in 有 it stands for a piece of meat.
column4: 今天晚上的月亮又大又圆。
column5: 今天晚上的月亮又大又圓。
column6: Jīntiān wǎnshang de yuèliang yòu dà yòu yuán.
column7: The moon is big and round tonight.
column9: 月 alone can mean the moon or a month (一個月), so 月亮 is the clear word for the moon itself. The second syllable is light (yuèliang). Moonlight is 月光, and the moon is full when it is 圓. 月 pictures a crescent moon, but in 有 it stands for a piece of meat.

column3: The word for stars in speech, with a light second syllable (xīngxing). Counted with 颗: 一颗星星. 星 alone appears in compounds such as 星期 and 星空, and 明星 means a celebrity. The old character for this word was 晶; 生 was added later as a sound part.
column7: You can see the stars at night.
column9: The word for stars in speech, with a light second syllable (xīngxing). Counted with 顆: 一顆星星. 星 alone appears in compounds such as 星期 and 星空, and 明星 means a celebrity. The old character for this word was 晶; 生 was added later as a sound part.

column3: Says where something is in the sky: 天上有云, 天上飞着一只鸟. It is also heaven, and 天上掉馅饼 "pie falling from the sky" is the saying for a windfall. The sky as an expanse you look at is 天空.
column7: There is a bird in the sky.
column9: Says where something is in the sky: 天上有雲, 天上飛著一隻鳥. It is also heaven, and 天上掉餡餅 "pie falling from the sky" is the saying for a windfall. The sky as an expanse you look at is 天空.

column3: Goes with 好, 新鲜 and 污染: 空气很好, 空气污染, and 呼吸新鲜空气 is a common phrase for stepping outside. 气 alone is not "air" in everyday speech; it is used inside words. 空 is read kòng, not kōng, when it means vacant or free time.
column7: The air is very good here.
column9: Goes with 好, 新鮮 and 污染: 空氣很好, 空氣污染, and 呼吸新鮮空氣 is a common phrase for stepping outside. 氣 alone is not "air" in everyday speech; it is used inside words. 空 is read kòng, not kōng, when it means vacant or free time.

column3: Mostly found inside words, and a pattern that opens many: 天气, 空气, 生气, 客气, 力气, 运气. On its own it is often "angry": 气死我了 "it makes me furious".
column7: I'm furious!
column9: Mostly found inside words, and a pattern that opens many: 天氣, 空氣, 生氣, 客氣, 力氣, 運氣. On its own it is often "angry": 氣死我了 "it makes me furious".

column3: Earth as a planet and as our home: 地球上, 保护地球, 地球村. 球 is every ball (足球, 篮球), and 打球 means to play ball. 球 first named a kind of jade; a ball was written 毬 until 球 became the usual form.
column6: Wǒmen dōu zhù zài dìqiú shang.
column7: We all live on Earth.
column9: Earth as a planet and as our home: 地球上, 保護地球, 地球村. 球 is every ball (足球, 籃球), and 打球 means to play ball. 球 first named a kind of jade; a ball was written 毬 until 球 became the usual form.

column3: Nature as the world outside: 亲近大自然, 走进大自然, 热爱大自然, 保护大自然. It is never human nature, and 自然 alone means natural or naturally (很自然). 然 first meant to burn, as its fire part 火 shows, and 燃 later took over that meaning.
column7: I like nature.
column9: Nature as the world outside: 親近大自然, 走進大自然, 熱愛大自然, 保護大自然. It is never human nature, and 自然 alone means natural or naturally (很自然). 然 first meant to burn, as its fire part 火 shows, and 燃 later took over that meaning.

column3: The everyday word, leading many compounds: 海边, 海鲜 seafood, 海外 overseas, 海关 customs, 上海. 大海 stresses the vastness; 海洋 is the formal "ocean" of textbooks. 海 is probably related to 晦, dark, and Zhou texts describe the sea as 晦.
column6: Wǒ jiā lí hǎi hěn jìn.
column7: My home is close to the sea.
column9: The everyday word, leading many compounds: 海邊, 海鮮 seafood, 海外 overseas, 海關 customs, 上海. 大海 stresses the vastness; 海洋 is the formal "ocean" of textbooks. 海 is probably related to 晦, dark, and Zhou texts describe the sea as 晦.

column3: A place word for the beach or seaside: 去海边, 在海边散步. 海滩 is the sandy beach itself. People go there for a day out, so it is often paired with 玩 or 度假. 边 also has a light reading, bian, as a suffix of a noun of locality.
column7: Let's go to the seaside.
column9: A place word for the beach or seaside: 去海邊, 在海邊散步. 海灘 is the sandy beach itself. People go there for a day out, so it is often paired with 玩 or 度假. 邊 also has a light reading, bian, as a suffix of a noun of locality.

column3: Picks the sea out as something vast and open, to look at or be moved by: 看大海, 大海边. Practical compounds drop the 大: 海边, 海水, 海鲜. 大海捞针, "fishing a needle out of the sea", is the idiom for a hopeless search. 海 is probably related to 晦, "dark".
column7: The sea is very blue.
column9: Picks the sea out as something vast and open, to look at or be moved by: 看大海, 大海邊. Practical compounds drop the 大: 海邊, 海水, 海鮮. 大海撈針, "fishing a needle out of the sea", is the idiom for a hopeless search. 海 is probably related to 晦, "dark".

column3: Counted with 条: 一条河. 河 names most rivers (黄河), while 江 names the great rivers of the south, such as 长江. 河水 is river water and 河边 the bank. 河 originally named only the Yellow River; other rivers were called 水.
column6: Hé lǐ yǒu hěn duō yú.
column7: There are many fish in the river.
column9: Counted with 條: 一條河. 河 names most rivers (黃河), while 江 names the great rivers of the south, such as 長江. 河水 is river water and 河邊 the bank. 河 originally named only the Yellow River; other rivers were called 水.

column3: Lakes are named with it: 西湖, 太湖, 洞庭湖. The provinces 湖北 and 湖南 are "north" and "south" of a lake, the Dongting Lake. 湖边 is the typical place word for the shore.
column6: Zhège hú yòu dà yòu měi.
column7: This lake is big and beautiful.
column9: Lakes are named with it: 西湖, 太湖, 洞庭湖. The provinces 湖北 and 湖南 are "north" and "south" of a lake, the Dongting Lake. 湖邊 is the typical place word for the shore.

column3: 吃草 is what cows and horses do. The character leads 草地 lawn, 草原 grassland, 草莓 strawberry and 草稿 a draft; it can also mean rough or careless, as in 草率. 草, a picture of blades of grass, was the old character for grass; 草 was borrowed to replace it.
column7: The horse is eating grass.
column9: 吃草 is what cows and horses do. The character leads 草地 lawn, 草原 grassland, 草莓 strawberry and 草稿 a draft; it can also mean rough or careless, as in 草率. 艸, a picture of blades of grass, was the old character for grass; 草 was borrowed to replace it.

column3: Grass growing on the ground: 在草地上 "on the grass". A tended lawn in a park or yard is more often 草坪. Say 坐在草地上 for sitting on it. 地 is read dì here; the same character is the light particle de that goes before a verb. An early form of 地 shows a hill, a pig and a mound of earth.
column7: The children are playing on the grass.
column9: Grass growing on the ground: 在草地上 "on the grass". A tended lawn in a park or yard is more often 草坪. Say 坐在草地上 for sitting on it. 地 is read dì here; the same character is the light particle de that goes before a verb. An early form of 地 shows a hill, a pig and a mound of earth.

column3: Counted with 只: 一只鸟. 鸟 is any bird; it leads 小鸟 and 鸟笼. 鸟 is the bird part of other bird names, such as 鸭. 鳥 began as a picture of a bird with a dangling tail. In many dialects the old t- sound changed to n-, to avoid sounding like a vulgar word.
column6: Shù shang yǒu liǎng zhī niǎo.
column7: There are two birds in the tree.
column9: Counted with 隻: 一隻鳥. 鳥 is any bird; it leads 小鳥 and 鳥籠. 鳥 is the bird part of other bird names, such as 鴨. 鳥 began as a picture of a bird with a dangling tail. In many dialects the old t- sound changed to n-, to avoid sounding like a vulgar word.

column3: Counted with 条: 一条鱼. It is both the animal and the food, so 我不吃鱼 and a menu use the same word. At New Year a whole fish is served, since 鱼 sounds like 余 "surplus" (年年有余). 鱼 is cognate with 渔, the verb "to fish".
column7: Do you like to eat fish?
column9: Counted with 條: 一條魚. It is both the animal and the food, so 我不吃魚 and a menu use the same word. At New Year a whole fish is served, since 魚 sounds like 餘 "surplus" (年年有餘). 魚 is cognate with 漁, the verb "to fish".

column3: Counted with 只: 一只猫. 小猫 is a kitten and 熊猫 a panda, literally "bear cat". In northern speech 猫 also means to hide away or stay in: 猫在家里 "stay holed up at home". 猫 is onomatopoeic: in its earliest records it may have imitated the call of the Asian golden cat or clouded leopard.
column6: Wǒ de māo xǐhuan shuì zài chuāngbiān.
column7: My cat likes to sleep by the window.
column9: Counted with 隻: 一隻貓. 小貓 is a kitten and 熊貓 a panda, literally "bear cat". In northern speech 貓 also means to hide away or stay in: 貓在家裡 "stay holed up at home". 貓 is onomatopoeic: in its earliest records it may have imitated the call of the Asian golden cat or clouded leopard.

column3: The everyday word for dog, counted with 只 or 条 (一只狗, 一条狗). 犬 is the literary one, kept in set words such as 警犬. 狗 also turns up in insults, so be careful calling a person one. Early excavated texts hint that 狗 could also denote a young animal or cub.
column6: Tā měitiān dài gǒu qù gōngyuán.
column7: He takes the dog to the park every day.
column9: The everyday word for dog, counted with 隻 or 條 (一隻狗, 一條狗). 犬 is the literary one, kept in set words such as 警犬. 狗 also turns up in insults, so be careful calling a person one. Early excavated texts hint that 狗 could also denote a young animal or cub.

column3: Counted with 只. 公鸡 is a rooster, 母鸡 a hen and 小鸡 a chick, with 公 and 母 marking male and female animals (公牛, 母牛). The meat is 鸡肉. One scholar considers the word onomatopoeic.
column6: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǒu hěn duō jī.
column7: There are a lot of chickens on the farm.
column9: Counted with 隻. 公雞 is a rooster, 母雞 a hen and 小雞 a chick, with 公 and 母 marking male and female animals (公牛, 母牛). The meat is 雞肉. One scholar considers the word onomatopoeic.

column3: Animals in general (野生动物, 小动物), as opposed to 植物. 物 builds many category words: 动物, 植物, 食物, 礼物, and 宠物 for pets. 物 is a bound form: it appears inside words and does not stand alone for "thing".
column7: What animals do you like?
column9: Animals in general (野生動物, 小動物), as opposed to 植物. 物 builds many category words: 動物, 植物, 食物, 禮物, and 寵物 for pets. 物 is a bound form: it appears inside words and does not stand alone for "thing".

column3: 去动物园 is the everyday phrase. 园 marks a place for plants or public enjoyment: 动物园, 植物园, 公园, 花园, and 幼儿园 for a kindergarten.
column7: We go to the zoo on Saturday.
column9: 去動物園 is the everyday phrase. 園 marks a place for plants or public enjoyment: 動物園, 植物園, 公園, 花園, and 幼兒園 for a kindergarten.

column3: A garden of flowers and ornamental plants, often a shared one inside a housing complex (小区花园); 后花园 is a back garden. A yard that belongs to a house is 院子, and a vegetable plot is 菜园. 花 also means to spend money or time (花钱, 花时间).
column6: Huāyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō huā.
column7: There are many flowers in the garden.
column9: A garden of flowers and ornamental plants, often a shared one inside a housing complex (小區花園); 後花園 is a back garden. A yard that belongs to a house is 院子, and a vegetable plot is 菜園. 花 also means to spend money or time (花錢, 花時間).

column3: The place for a walk, tai chi or a run: 去公园散步. 公 is "public" here, as in 公共 and 公司 "company", so a 公园 is open to all, unlike a private 花园. 公 also marks a male animal, as in 公鸡.
column4: 周末我常常去公园跑步。
column5: 週末我常常去公園跑步。
column6: Zhōumò wǒ chángcháng qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
column7: At weekends I often go running in the park.
column9: The place for a walk, tai chi or a run: 去公園散步. 公 is "public" here, as in 公共 and 公司 "company", so a 公園 is open to all, unlike a private 花園. 公 also marks a male animal, as in 公雞.

column3: The open ground of a house: a small 小院子 beside it, or the traditional courtyard home, 四合院. A planted garden is more specifically 花园. 子 is a light noun suffix here (yuànzi), as in 椅子. 院 on its own means a courtyard and also an institution, as in 医院.
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu yī ge xiǎo yuànzi.
column7: Our home has a small yard.
column9: The open ground of a house: a small 小院子 beside it, or the traditional courtyard home, 四合院. A planted garden is more specifically 花園. 子 is a light noun suffix here (yuànzi), as in 椅子. 院 on its own means a courtyard and also an institution, as in 醫院.

column3: Moving up or along with hands and feet, so it suits babies, insects and hikers alike: 爬山 is the normal word for hiking up a mountain, and 爬楼梯, 爬树 follow. 爬虫 is both a reptile and a web crawler.
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù pá shān ba.
column7: Let's go hiking this weekend.
column9: Moving up or along with hands and feet, so it suits babies, insects and hikers alike: 爬山 is the normal word for hiking up a mountain, and 爬樓梯, 爬樹 follow. 爬蟲 is both a reptile and a web crawler.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 爬了一座山, 爬过几次山. 爬 alone means to climb or crawl, which is why stairs and ladders are 爬楼梯 and 爬梯子. A more formal word for mountaineering is 登山, as in 登山队. In oracle bone script the peaks of 山 were drawn as triangles rather than vertical strokes.
column7: We are going hiking this weekend.
column9: A verb plus object, so it splits: 爬了一座山, 爬過幾次山. 爬 alone means to climb or crawl, which is why stairs and ladders are 爬樓梯 and 爬梯子. A more formal word for mountaineering is 登山, as in 登山隊. In oracle bone script the peaks of 山 were drawn as triangles rather than vertical strokes.

column3: Besides the head, 头 is the top or end of something (山头, a hilltop) and the measure word for livestock: 一头牛, 两头猪. Light tou ends many nouns: 石头, 木头, 舌头, 骨头. The older word for head was 首, which gave way to 头 because it sounded like 手, hand.
column7: I have a headache and want to sleep.
column9: Besides the head, 頭 is the top or end of something (山頭, a hilltop) and the measure word for livestock: 一頭牛, 兩頭豬. Light tou ends many nouns: 石頭, 木頭, 舌頭, 骨頭. The older word for head was 首, which gave way to 頭 because it sounded like 手, hand.

column3: Hair as a mass takes no measure word: 头发很长. One strand is 一根头发. A haircut is 剪头发 or 理发, and washing it is 洗头发 or just 洗头. The 发 is light: tóufa. 发 stands for two characters: fā, to send out (發), and fà, hair (髮).
column6: Wǒ míngtiān yào qù jiǎn tóufa.
column7: I am going to get a haircut tomorrow.
column9: Hair as a mass takes no measure word: 頭髮很長. One strand is 一根頭髮. A haircut is 剪頭髮 or 理髮, and washing it is 洗頭髮 or just 洗頭. The 髮 is light: tóufa.

column3: Besides the face itself, 脸 is face in the sense of dignity: 丢脸 is to lose face and 不要脸 is shameless. 脸红 is to blush and 洗脸 is to wash your face. The word goes back to an old root meaning cheek or face.
column6: Tā yī tīng jiù liǎn hóng le.
column7: He blushed as soon as he heard it.
column9: Besides the face itself, 臉 is face in the sense of dignity: 丟臉 is to lose face and 不要臉 is shameless. 臉紅 is to blush and 洗臉 is to wash your face. The word goes back to an old root meaning cheek or face.

column3: As a measure word 眼 counts glances: 看一眼, 瞪一眼. The eye as an organ is mostly 眼睛, while bare 眼 turns up in compounds such as 眼镜, 眼泪 and 眼科. 目 lives on in written words like 目光. It displaced 目, the old Sino-Tibetan word for eye, in many dialects.
column7: Let me take a look.
column9: As a measure word 眼 counts glances: 看一眼, 瞪一眼. The eye as an organ is mostly 眼睛, while bare 眼 turns up in compounds such as 眼鏡, 眼淚 and 眼科. 目 lives on in written words like 目光. It displaced 目, the old Sino-Tibetan word for eye, in many dialects.

column3: 睛 hardly appears outside this word (a rare exception is the idiom 画龙点睛), so the eye is 眼睛: 闭上眼睛, 睁开眼睛, and 一双眼睛 for a pair. Bare 眼 is for glances and compounds. The 睛 is light: yǎnjing.
column6: Bì shàng yǎnjing, wǒ shǔ dào sān.
column7: Close your eyes and I will count to three.
column9: 睛 hardly appears outside this word (a rare exception is the idiom 畫龍點睛), so the eye is 眼睛: 閉上眼睛, 睜開眼睛, and 一雙眼睛 for a pair. Bare 眼 is for glances and compounds. The 睛 is light: yǎnjing.

column3: Also stands for what comes out of it: 嘴甜 is sweet-talking, 多嘴 speaking out of turn, and 闭嘴 "shut up" is rude. A kettle has a 壶嘴 (spout) and a bird a 鸟嘴 (beak).
column7: Please open your mouth.
column9: Also stands for what comes out of it: 嘴甜 is sweet-talking, 多嘴 speaking out of turn, and 閉嘴 "shut up" is rude. A kettle has a 壺嘴 (spout) and a bird a 鳥嘴 (beak).

column3: 腿 is the whole leg, so the thigh is 大腿 and the calf 小腿. It is also the leg of a table or chair, 桌子腿, and a cooked leg: 鸡腿, a drumstick. The foot is 脚. It was originally written 骽, a character that also means hip bone.
column6: Pǎo le yī tiān, wǒ de tuǐ hěn suān.
column7: After running all day, my legs are sore.
column9: 腿 is the whole leg, so the thigh is 大腿 and the calf 小腿. It is also the leg of a table or chair, 桌子腿, and a cooked leg: 雞腿, a drumstick. The foot is 腳. It was originally written 骽, a character that also means hip bone.

column3: 脚 is the foot, and also the bottom of a thing: 山脚 is the foot of a mountain. It counts kicks, 踢了一脚, and 光脚 is barefoot. 脚步 is a footstep.
column6: Tā tī le wǒ yī jiǎo.
column7: He kicked me.
column9: 腳 is the foot, and also the bottom of a thing: 山腳 is the foot of a mountain. It counts kicks, 踢了一腳, and 光腳 is barefoot. 腳步 is a footstep.

column3: 全 before a noun means all of: 全家, 全校. 全身 is all over the body: 全身都湿了. As a modifier it means full-body: 全身检查 is a full checkup and 全身照 a full-length photo. 身 also counts outfits: 一身西装. 全 began as 入 plus 玉, a whole piece of jade, pure jade.
column6: Pǎo wán bù, wǒ quánshēn dōu shī le.
column7: After the run, I was wet all over.
column9: 全 before a noun means all of: 全家, 全校. 全身 is all over the body: 全身都溼了. As a modifier it means full-body: 全身檢查 is a full checkup and 全身照 a full-length photo. 身 also counts outfits: 一身西裝. 全 began as 入 plus 玉, a whole piece of jade, pure jade.

column3: It says how tall or big someone looks, not an exact figure: 大个子 is a big, tall person and 小个子 a small one. A number goes with 身高 instead: 身高一米八. The 子 is light: gèzi. 个 is a variant of 箇, a bamboo stalk, and looks like half of 竹.
column4: 他个子很高，打篮球很合适。
column5: 他個子很高，打籃球很合適。
column6: Tā gèzi hěn gāo, dǎ lánqiú hěn héshì.
column7: He is tall, so he is well suited to basketball.
column9: It says how tall or big someone looks, not an exact figure: 大個子 is a big, tall person and 小個子 a small one. A number goes with 身高 instead: 身高一米八. The 子 is light: gèzi. 個 is a variant of 箇, a bamboo stalk.

column3: A verb plus object: 点点头 is a small nod and 点了点头 a nod already given. It means yes, agreement or a greeting; the opposite is 摇头, shaking the head. 老板点头了 means the boss approved. 点 alone can already mean to nod in agreement.
column7: He smiled and nodded at me.
column9: A verb plus object: 點點頭 is a small nod and 點了點頭 a nod already given. It means yes, agreement or a greeting; the opposite is 搖頭, shaking the head. 老板點頭了 means the boss approved. 點 alone can already mean to nod in agreement.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 举起手, 举了手. It is the classroom signal for a question or answer. 举 also means to hold or to cite, as in 举行 (to hold an event) and 举例 (to give an example). The top stroke of 手 is the bent middle finger, and each horizontal stroke stands for two fingers.
column7: If you have a question, please raise your hand.
column9: A verb plus object, so it splits: 舉起手, 舉了手. It is the classroom signal for a question or answer. 舉 also means to hold or to cite, as in 舉行 (to hold an event) and 舉例 (to give an example). The top stroke of 手 is the bent middle finger, and each horizontal stroke stands for two fingers.

column3: Dirty in the sense of grimy or unclean: 弄脏 gets something dirty (衣服弄脏了), 脏话 is swearing, and the opposite is 干净. Simplified 脏 also writes a second word, the organ read zàng.
column7: Your hands are dirty.
column9: Dirty in the sense of grimy or unclean: 弄髒 gets something dirty (衣服弄髒了), 髒話 is swearing, and the opposite is 乾淨.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 洗了澡, 洗个澡, 洗完澡. 澡 does not stand alone. It covers both shower and bath: 冲澡 is a quick shower and 泡澡 a long soak. 洗 is the general wash: 洗手, 洗碗, and 洗牌 for shuffling cards.
column6: Nǐ xiān xǐzǎo, háishi xiān chī fàn?
column7: Do you want to shower first or eat first?
column9: A verb plus object, so it splits: 洗了澡, 洗個澡, 洗完澡. 澡 does not stand alone. It covers both shower and bath: 沖澡 is a quick shower and 泡澡 a long soak. 洗 is the general wash: 洗手, 洗碗, and 洗牌 for shuffling cards.

column3: Full from eating, so it follows a verb: 吃饱, and 我吃饱了 is the way to decline more food. 没吃饱 means you have not had enough. A full glass or room is 满, not 饱; the opposite of 饱 is 饿.
column7: I'm full, thank you.
column9: Full from eating, so it follows a verb: 吃飽, and 我吃飽了 is the way to decline more food. 沒吃飽 means you have not had enough. A full glass or room is 滿, not 飽; the opposite of 飽 is 餓.

column3: 疼 is the everyday word for physical pain in the north and in standard mainland speech: 头疼, 肚子疼, 疼死了. 痛 is usual in the south and in Taiwan (好痛), and it is the written word everywhere, as in 疼痛. 疼 also means to love dearly, said of children.
column7: Where does it hurt?
column9: 疼 is the everyday word for physical pain in the north and in standard mainland speech: 頭疼, 肚子疼, 疼死了. 痛 is usual in the south and in Taiwan (好痛), and it is the written word everywhere, as in 疼痛. 疼 also means to love dearly, said of children.

column3: It describes things (a sofa, a bed) and your own body. 我不舒服 is a polite way to say you are unwell without naming the illness. 舒适 is the more formal word for comfortable conditions: 舒适的环境. The 月 in 服 is a corrupted 舟, itself a corrupted 凡, a tray.
column7: I don't feel very well today.
column9: It describes things (a sofa, a bed) and your own body. 我不舒服 is a polite way to say you are unwell without naming the illness. 舒適 is the more formal word for comfortable conditions: 舒適的環境. The 月 in 服 is a corrupted 舟, itself a corrupted 凡, a tray.

column3: What blows goes before it, 风吹, and what is blown comes after: 吹蜡烛, 吹气. It also covers wind instruments (吹笛子) and the hair dryer 吹风机. As slang it means to boast: 吹牛. 吹了 says a plan or relationship fell through.
column7: The wind is blowing over; it is a bit cold.
column9: What blows goes before it, 風吹, and what is blown comes after: 吹蠟燭, 吹氣. It also covers wind instruments (吹笛子) and the hair dryer 吹風機. As slang it means to boast: 吹牛. 吹了 says a plan or relationship fell through.

column3: Door signs say 拉 and 推, opposites. 拉 has many uses: 拉小提琴 plays the violin, 拉肚子 is to have diarrhea, 拉面 is hand-pulled noodles and 拉链 a zipper.
column6: Zhè shàn mén yào lā, bù yào tuī.
column7: This door is pull, not push.
column9: Door signs say 拉 and 推, opposites. 拉 has many uses: 拉小提琴 plays the violin, 拉肚子 is to have diarrhea, 拉麵 is hand-pulled noodles and 拉鏈 a zipper.

column3: It takes a result: 推开 pushes open, 推倒 pushes over. It also means pushing something back or away: 推迟 is to postpone and 推辞 to decline politely. A separate sense is to put forward: 推荐 is to recommend. Middle Chinese kept two readings apart: one for to push, the other for to proceed, promote or deduce.
column6: Mén hěn zhòng, nǐ bāng wǒ tuī yīxià.
column7: The door is heavy; give it a push for me.
column9: It takes a result: 推開 pushes open, 推倒 pushes over. It also means pushing something back or away: 推遲 is to postpone and 推辭 to decline politely. A separate sense is to put forward: 推薦 is to recommend. Middle Chinese kept two readings apart: one for to push, the other for to proceed, promote or deduce.

column3: The word of hotel signs, menus and writing; on the mainland speech prefers 早饭, while in Taiwan 早餐 is the everyday word too. It pairs with 午餐 and 晚餐, and the verb is 吃: 吃早餐. In early bronze inscriptions 早 was a picture of an acorn, later borrowed for its sound to write morning.
column7: I eat breakfast at seven.
column9: The word of hotel signs, menus and writing; on the mainland speech prefers 早飯, while in Taiwan 早餐 is the everyday word too. It pairs with 午餐 and 晚餐, and the verb is 吃: 吃早餐. In early bronze inscriptions 早 was a picture of an acorn, later borrowed for its sound to write morning.

column3: In Taiwan 午餐 is the ordinary word for lunch; on the mainland it sounds more formal, as on menus and at hotels, and 午饭 or 中饭 is the spoken one. With 早餐 and 晚餐 it makes the three meals. 午 began as a picture of a pestle, and it is unrelated to 干.
column7: We eat lunch at one.
column9: In Taiwan 午餐 is the ordinary word for lunch; on the mainland it sounds more formal, as on menus and at hotels, and 午飯 or 中飯 is the spoken one. With 早餐 and 晚餐 it makes the three meals. 午 began as a picture of a pestle, and it is unrelated to 干.

column3: In Taiwan 晚餐 is the ordinary word for dinner; on the mainland it sounds more formal, as in 烛光晚餐, a candlelit dinner, and 晚饭 is the spoken one. 晚 means late as well as evening: 来晚了. The 餐 first meant to swallow.
column7: What do you want for dinner?
column9: In Taiwan 晚餐 is the ordinary word for dinner; on the mainland it sounds more formal, as in 燭光晚餐, a candlelit dinner, and 晚飯 is the spoken one. 晚 means late as well as evening: 來晚了. The 餐 first meant to swallow.

column3: 中 here means Chinese, as in 中国 and 中文, so 中餐 is Chinese-style food, set against 西餐: 吃中餐, 中餐厅. It can also mean a midday meal, so context decides; 午餐 is the clear word for lunch. Read zhòng, 中 means to hit a target or to win a prize.
column7: We are having Chinese food tonight.
column9: 中 here means Chinese, as in 中國 and 中文, so 中餐 is Chinese-style food, set against 西餐: 吃中餐, 中餐廳. It can also mean a midday meal, so context decides; 午餐 is the clear word for lunch. Read zhòng, 中 means to hit a target or to win a prize.

column3: It covers steak, pasta, bread and the like, eaten with a knife and fork (刀叉) rather than chopsticks. A 西餐厅 is a Western-style restaurant, and 中餐还是西餐 is the usual pair of choices. 餐 itself counts meals.
column6: Nǐ xiǎng chī zhōngcān háishi xīcān?
column7: Do you want Chinese or Western food?
column9: It covers steak, pasta, bread and the like, eaten with a knife and fork (刀叉) rather than chopsticks. A 西餐廳 is a Western-style restaurant, and 中餐還是西餐 is the usual pair of choices. 餐 itself counts meals.

column3: The speed is in the service, not the eating: 快餐店 is a fast-food restaurant. On the mainland 洋快餐 names foreign chains such as 麦当劳 and 肯德基. 餐 counts meals: 一天三餐. 快 can also mean sharp, as of a knife or of wits.
column7: I don't often eat fast food.
column9: The speed is in the service, not the eating: 快餐店 is a fast-food restaurant. On the mainland 洋快餐 names foreign chains such as 麥當勞 and 肯德基. 餐 counts meals: 一天三餐. 快 can also mean sharp, as of a knife or of wits.

column3: The general, rather written word for food as a substance: 食物中毒 is food poisoning, 食物链 the food chain. In speech people say 吃的 or 东西; a dish is 菜 and cooked rice 饭. Kinds are counted with 种: 这种食物. Read sì, 食 means to feed a person or an animal.
column4: 这些食物都要放进冰箱。
column5: 這些食物都要放進冰箱。
column6: Zhèxiē shíwù dōu yào fàng jìn bīngxiāng.
column7: All this food has to go into the fridge.
column9: The general, rather written word for food as a substance: 食物中毒 is food poisoning, 食物鏈 the food chain. In speech people say 吃的 or 東西; a dish is 菜 and cooked rice 飯. Kinds are counted with 種: 這種食物. Read sì, 食 means to feed a person or an animal.

column3: Count them one by one with 个, or by the plate: 一盘饺子. 包饺子 is wrapping them, often a family job at New Year; 水饺 are boiled, 蒸饺 steamed and 煎饺 pan-fried. 饺 is said to take its name from 角, "horn", for its horn-like shape.
column7: Let's make dumplings.
column9: Count them one by one with 個, or by the plate: 一盤餃子. 包餃子 is wrapping them, often a family job at New Year; 水餃 are boiled, 蒸餃 steamed and 煎餃 pan-fried. 餃 is said to take its name from 角, "horn", for its horn-like shape.

column3: A packet is 一包方便面, a bowl 一碗. You make it by 泡, soaking it in hot water, which is why Taiwan calls it 泡面. On the mainland 方便面 is the usual name. 面 also stands in for 麵, noodles, with 麥 dropped.
column4: 没时间做饭，就吃了一包方便面。
column5: 沒時間做飯，就吃了一包方便麵。
column6: Méi shíjiān zuòfàn, jiù chī le yī bāo fāngbiànmiàn.
column7: I had no time to cook, so I ate a packet of instant noodles.
column9: A packet is 一包方便麵, a bowl 一碗. You make it by 泡, soaking it in hot water, which is why Taiwan calls it 泡麵. On the mainland 方便麵 is the usual name.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 鸡蛋 is the everyday egg, 蛋糕 cake, 蛋黄 yolk, 煎蛋 a fried egg. 蛋 also names round things and, rudely, people: 脸蛋 is a cheek, 笨蛋 a fool and 坏蛋 a villain. It was coined late, for egg with particular reference to snake eggs.
column6: Wǒ zǎoshang chī le liǎng ge dàn.
column7: I had two eggs this morning.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 雞蛋 is the everyday egg, 蛋糕 cake, 蛋黃 yolk, 煎蛋 a fried egg. 蛋 also names round things and, rudely, people: 臉蛋 is a cheek, 笨蛋 a fool and 壞蛋 a villain. It was coined late, for egg with particular reference to snake eggs.

column3: Uncooked rice; the cooked kind is 米饭. It also names other small grains and kernels: 小米 is millet, 玉米 corn, and 花生米 a peanut kernel. As the unit it is the meter: 一米八 is a typical way to give a height. One scholar suggests the horizontal stroke of 米 is a bamboo sieve.
column4: 家里没有米了，我去买一袋。
column5: 家裡沒有米了，我去買一袋。
column6: Jiālǐ méiyǒu mǐ le, wǒ qù mǎi yī dài.
column7: We are out of rice; I'll go buy a bag.
column9: Uncooked rice; the cooked kind is 米飯. It also names other small grains and kernels: 小米 is millet, 玉米 corn, and 花生米 a peanut kernel. As the unit it is the meter: 一米八 is a typical way to give a height. One scholar suggests the horizontal stroke of 米 is a bamboo sieve.

column3: Cooking oil, but also fat, grease and fuel: 汽油 is gasoline, 石油 petroleum and 酱油 soy sauce. Of food it means greasy: 太油了. 加油 is to fill up at 加油站 and also a shout of encouragement, like "go for it".
column7: This dish is too greasy.
column9: Cooking oil, but also fat, grease and fuel: 汽油 is gasoline, 石油 petroleum and 醬油 soy sauce. Of food it means greasy: 太油了. 加油 is to fill up at 加油站 and also a shout of encouragement, like "go for it".

column3: It means any alcohol, not only wine, so the kind comes first: 啤酒 beer, 白酒 grain liquor, 红酒 red wine. It forms 酒吧 (a bar) and 酒量 (how much someone can drink). 酉, a wine vessel, was itself the original character for this word; water was added later to tell them apart.
column7: I don't drink alcohol.
column9: It means any alcohol, not only wine, so the kind comes first: 啤酒 beer, 白酒 grain liquor, 紅酒 red wine. It forms 酒吧 (a bar) and 酒量 (how much someone can drink). 酉, a wine vessel, was itself the original character for this word; water was added later to tell them apart.

column3: 味道 is neutral, so you ask 味道怎么样?, while 好吃 already says it is good. It also means a feel or hint: 有过年的味道 feels like the New Year. 道 counts the courses of a meal, so a dish is 一道菜.
column7: This soup tastes a bit bland.
column9: 味道 is neutral, so you ask 味道怎麼樣?, while 好吃 already says it is good. It also means a feel or hint: 有過年的味道 feels like the New Year. 道 counts the courses of a meal, so a dish is 一道菜.

column3: One word for being done through: food is cooked (饭熟了), fruit is ripe, and a person or place is familiar (我和他不熟, 熟人 "an acquaintance"). 生 is the opposite in all three: raw, unripe, a stranger.
column6: Wǒ hé tā bù tài shú.
column7: I don't know him very well.
column9: One word for being done through: food is cooked (飯熟了), fruit is ripe, and a person or place is familiar (我和他不熟, 熟人 "an acquaintance"). 生 is the opposite in all three: raw, unripe, a stranger.

column3: Ask 请给我菜单 at a restaurant; then 点菜 to order. 菜单 is also a software menu. 单 is a slip or list, as in 账单 (a bill), 订单 (an order) and 名单 (a name list). 單 began as a picture of a Y-shaped hunting weapon with two stones on top.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ kàn yīxià càidān.
column7: Please let me see the menu.
column9: Ask 請給我菜單 at a restaurant; then 點菜 to order. 菜單 is also a software menu. 單 is a slip or list, as in 帳單 (a bill), 訂單 (an order) and 名單 (a name list). 單 began as a picture of a Y-shaped hunting weapon with two stones on top.

column3: A casual place to eat, less formal than 餐厅; 餐馆 is much the same. It is counted with 家: 一家饭馆. 馆 marks a place offering a service: 图书馆, 咖啡馆, 博物馆. 馆 also names an embassy or consulate.
column6: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is delicious.
column9: A casual place to eat, less formal than 餐廳; 餐館 is much the same. It is counted with 家: 一家飯館. 館 marks a place offering a service: 圖書館, 咖啡館, 博物館. 館 also names an embassy or consulate.

column3: On the mainland 外卖 covers both takeout and delivery: 点外卖 is to order in, 送外卖 to deliver, and 外卖员 is a delivery rider. Taiwan says 外带 for takeout and 外送 for delivery. 卖 comes from 賣, which was built from 出, go out, and 買, buy; the 出 was later reduced to 士.
column6: Tài lèi le, wǎnshang diǎn wàimài ba.
column7: I'm too tired; let's order in tonight.
column9: On the mainland 外賣 covers both takeout and delivery: 點外賣 is to order in, 送外賣 to deliver, and 外賣員 is a delivery rider. Taiwan says 外帶 for takeout and 外送 for delivery. 賣 was built from 出, go out, and 買, buy; the 出 was later reduced to 士.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 做了饭, 做好饭, 做顿饭. It is the whole task of getting a meal ready; one dish is 做菜. Taiwan more often says 煮饭 for cooking in general. 做 began as a vulgar variant of 作. 作 rather than 做 is fixed in many set words: 工作, 作业, 作文.
column7: I'll cook tonight.
column9: A verb plus object, so it splits: 做了飯, 做好飯, 做頓飯. It is the whole task of getting a meal ready; one dish is 做菜. Taiwan more often says 煮飯 for cooking in general. 做 began as a vulgar variant of 作. 作 rather than 做 is fixed in many set words: 工作, 作業, 作文.

column3: Literally to drain the cup, so it asks everyone to empty their glass; 随意 means drink as much as you like. Name the toast with 为: 为我们的友谊干杯. 杯 also counts drinks: 一杯咖啡. 干 began as a picture of a shield and was later borrowed to simplify both 乾, dry, and 幹.
column7: To our friendship!
column9: Literally to drain the cup, so it asks everyone to empty their glass; 隨意 means drink as much as you like. Name the toast with 為: 為我們的友誼乾杯. 杯 also counts drinks: 一杯咖啡.

column3: Counted with 双: 一双筷子; you 用筷子 and 夹菜 with them. The light 子 ends many tableware nouns: 勺子 a spoon, 叉子 a fork, 盘子 a plate. 筷 comes from 快 and was originally a euphemism for 箸, which sounded like 住, to stay or stop.
column7: Can you use chopsticks?
column9: Counted with 雙: 一雙筷子; you 用筷子 and 夾菜 with them. The light 子 ends many tableware nouns: 勺子 a spoon, 叉子 a fork, 盤子 a plate. 筷 comes from 快 and was originally a euphemism for 箸, which sounded like 住, to stay or stop.

column3: It counts a bowlful of what it holds: 一碗面, 一碗米饭. 饭碗 is a rice bowl and also one's livelihood: 铁饭碗 is a secure job. 洗碗 is to do the dishes.
column7: Boss, a bowl of noodles!
column9: It counts a bowlful of what it holds: 一碗麵, 一碗米飯. 飯碗 is a rice bowl and also one's livelihood: 鐵飯碗 is a secure job. 洗碗 is to do the dishes.

column3: On its own it is mostly a measure word (一瓶水); the bottle itself is 瓶子. It also ends compounds for containers: 花瓶 vase, 酒瓶, 奶瓶 baby bottle. The 瓦 in it means earthenware, because a 瓶 was first a clay vessel, not a glass one.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng yào yī píng shuǐ.
column7: I would like a bottle of water.
column9: On its own it is mostly a measure word (一瓶水); the bottle itself is 瓶子. It also ends compounds for containers: 花瓶 vase, 酒瓶, 奶瓶 baby bottle. The 瓦 in it means earthenware, because a 瓶 was first a clay vessel, not a glass one.

column3: 瓶子 is the bottle itself. Bare 瓶 counts what it holds, 一瓶水, or ends a compound: 花瓶 is a vase and 酒瓶 a liquor bottle. The 子 is light: píngzi. 瓶 first meant an earthenware vessel, not a glass bottle, and now covers bottles of any kind and size.
column7: There is water in the bottle.
column9: 瓶子 is the bottle itself. Bare 瓶 counts what it holds, 一瓶水, or ends a compound: 花瓶 is a vase and 酒瓶 a liquor bottle. The 子 is light: píngzi. 瓶 first meant an earthenware vessel, not a glass bottle, and now covers bottles of any kind and size.

column3: 闻 smells with the nose: 闻一闻 is to have a sniff, 闻到 to smell something, 好闻 smells nice. Hearing survives in 新闻, news, and in the saying 百闻不如一见, hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once. 问, to ask, is a related word: literally "let (me) hear".
column6: Nǐ wén yī wén, xiāng bu xiāng?
column7: Take a sniff; does it smell good?
column9: 聞 smells with the nose: 聞一聞 is to have a sniff, 聞到 to smell something, 好聞 smells nice. Hearing survives in 新聞, news, and in the saying 百聞不如一見, hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once. 問, to ask, is a related word: literally "let (me) hear".

column3: A spoken word for being in a good mood right now; 高兴 is its near twin. 玩得开心 is how you wish someone a good time, and the opposite is 不开心. 拿我开心 means to make fun of me.
column6: Jīntiān jiàndào nǐ, wǒ hěn kāixīn.
column7: I'm very happy to see you today.
column9: A spoken word for being in a good mood right now; 高興 is its near twin. 玩得開心 is how you wish someone a good time, and the opposite is 不開心. 拿我開心 means to make fun of me.

column3: Fixed in greetings: 生日快乐, 新年快乐, and 祝你快乐. As a lasting state it is a little more written than 开心, which is for a mood of the moment: you say 玩得开心, not 玩得快乐. 乐 is lè for happy but yuè for music, as in 音乐.
column7: Happy birthday to you!
column9: Fixed in greetings: 生日快樂, 新年快樂, and 祝你快樂. As a lasting state it is a little more written than 開心, which is for a mood of the moment: you say 玩得開心, not 玩得快樂. 樂 is lè for happy but yuè for music, as in 音樂.

column3: Said of babies, pets, toys and lovable personalities. 可 before a verb makes an adjective: 可爱, 可怕 (scary), 可笑 (funny), 可惜 (a pity), 可靠 (reliable).
column7: This kitten is very cute.
column9: Said of babies, pets, toys and lovable personalities. 可 before a verb makes an adjective: 可愛, 可怕 (scary), 可笑 (funny), 可惜 (a pity), 可靠 (reliable).

column3: 可怕 describes the thing that frightens; 怕 says the person is afraid: 这条狗很可怕 but 我怕狗. It also makes an intensifier: 安静得可怕 is frighteningly quiet. 怕 can also mean perhaps.
column4: 这部电影太可怕了，我不敢看。
column5: 這部電影太可怕了，我不敢看。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng tài kěpà le, wǒ bù gǎn kàn.
column7: This film is too scary; I don't dare watch it.
column9: 可怕 describes the thing that frightens; 怕 says the person is afraid: 這條狗很可怕 but 我怕狗. It also makes an intensifier: 安靜得可怕 is frighteningly quiet. 怕 can also mean perhaps.

column3: Takes an object (怕狗) or a whole clause (我怕他不来, "I am afraid he will not come"). Before a verb or adjective it means dread or be sensitive to: 怕冷 feels the cold easily, 怕麻烦 dislikes trouble, 别怕 "don't be afraid".
column7: I am afraid of the dark.
column9: Takes an object (怕狗) or a whole clause (我怕他不來, "I am afraid he will not come"). Before a verb or adjective it means dread or be sensitive to: 怕冷 feels the cold easily, 怕麻煩 dislikes trouble, 別怕 "don't be afraid".

column3: 急 is a pressure feeling when you are late, waiting or worried: 别急 is don't worry, there is time. 着急 is the common verb for getting anxious: 我很着急. It also fits an urgent matter, 急事, and a swift current: 水流很急. 急诊 is the emergency room.
column7: Don't rush, take it slowly.
column9: 急 is a pressure feeling when you are late, waiting or worried: 別急 is don't worry, there is time. 著急 is the common verb for getting anxious: 我很著急. It also fits an urgent matter, 急事, and a swift current: 水流很急. 急診 is the emergency room.

column3: 哭 is crying with sound, weeping or wailing; tears without a sound are 流泪 or 掉眼泪. 别哭 is don't cry, and what you cry over follows 为: 为这件事哭了. The 犬 in 哭 is not a dog: it was a long-haired person, beside two mouths for loudly.
column7: Don't cry, it's all right.
column9: 哭 is crying with sound, weeping or wailing; tears without a sound are 流淚 or 掉眼淚. 別哭 is don't cry, and what you cry over follows 為: 為這件事哭了. The 犬 in 哭 is not a dog: it was a long-haired person, beside two mouths for loudly.

column3: The thing you are pleased with follows 对: 我对这里很满意. Customers give a 满意度, a satisfaction rating. 满足 is different: it means to meet a need or to be content with what you have, 满足需求. The top of 意 looks like 音 but is etymologically unrelated to it.
column7: I'm very satisfied with this.
column9: The thing you are pleased with follows 對: 我對這裡很滿意. Customers give a 滿意度, a satisfaction rating. 滿足 is different: it means to meet a need or to be content with what you have, 滿足需求. The top of 意 looks like 音 but is etymologically unrelated to it.

column3: It is a complaint or grudge, stronger than 不满意: 他对工资不满, and 表示不满 is to voice discontent. Before a number it means under: 不满十岁 is not yet ten, since 满十岁 is to have turned ten. 不 began as a picture of a flower's calyx; the meaning 'not' came back to it from 否, which is 不 plus 口.
column7: He is not yet ten years old.
column9: It is a complaint or grudge, stronger than 不滿意: 他對工資不滿, and 表示不滿 is to voice discontent. Before a number it means under: 不滿十歲 is not yet ten, since 滿十歲 is to have turned ten. 不 began as a picture of a flower's calyx; the meaning 'not' came back to it from 否, which is 不 plus 口.

column3: It works both ways: 我很感动 (I am moved) and 他的话感动了我 (his words moved me). The result is added with 得: 感动得哭了, so moved I cried. 感 ending a word means sense of: 责任感, 幸福感.
column6: Tīng le tā de huà, wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
column7: After hearing his words, I was very moved.
column9: It works both ways: 我很感動 (I am moved) and 他的話感動了我 (his words moved me). The result is added with 得: 感動得哭了, so moved I cried. 感 ending a word means sense of: 責任感, 幸福感.

column3: The feeling follows directly: 感到高兴, 感到很累, 感到有点奇怪. It reports a feeling or sensation, not an opinion: 我觉得他说得对 takes 觉得, not 感到. 感到 is a little more formal than 觉得. 到 can also mean considerate or thorough.
column4: 听到这个消息，我感到很高兴。
column5: 聽到這個消息，我感到很高興。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, wǒ gǎndào hěn gāoxìng.
column7: I was very happy to hear this news.
column9: The feeling follows directly: 感到高興, 感到很累, 感到有點奇怪. It reports a feeling or sensation, not an opinion: 我覺得他說得對 takes 覺得, not 感到. 感到 is a little more formal than 覺得. 到 can also mean considerate or thorough.

column3: Works as verb and noun. As a verb it is close to 觉得, but it speaks of an impression you sense (感觉有点冷), while 觉得 also states an opinion. As a noun, 有感觉 means something moves you or feels right, and 没感觉 means it leaves you cold.
column7: I feel a bit cold.
column9: Works as verb and noun. As a verb it is close to 覺得, but it speaks of an impression you sense (感覺有點冷), while 覺得 also states an opinion. As a noun, 有感覺 means something moves you or feels right, and 沒感覺 means it leaves you cold.

column3: Mood: 心情好 "in a good mood", 心情不好 "in a bad mood". It is what is in your heart (心) at a given time. 情 has 青 as sound part, as in 请 and 晴.
column7: She is in a very good mood today.
column9: Mood: 心情好 "in a good mood", 心情不好 "in a bad mood". It is what is in your heart (心) at a given time. 情 has 青 as sound part, as in 請 and 晴.

column3: In the heart, in one's mind: 心里想 "think to oneself", 心里很高兴 "happy inside". Said xīnli, with a light 里. 心中 means the same but is more written.
column7: I am happy inside.
column9: In the heart, in one's mind: 心裡想 "think to oneself", 心裡很高興 "happy inside". Said xīnli, with a light 裡. 心中 means the same but is more written.

column3: In the heart, a more written way to say 心里. It sits in expressions such as 心中的想法 "the thoughts in one's heart". 中 here means "within", not "middle".
column7: He is very sad inside.
column9: In the heart, a more written way to say 心裡. It sits in expressions such as 心中的想法 "the thoughts in one's heart". 中 here means "within", not "middle".

column3: Rest at ease, not worry: 放 ("put down") plus 心 ("heart"), so putting your heart down. 请放心 and 你放心 reassure someone. 放心不下 is the opposite, "cannot stop worrying".
column6: Nǐ fàngxīn, wǒ bù huì wàng.
column7: Don't worry, I won't forget.
column9: Rest at ease, not worry: 放 ("put down") plus 心 ("heart"), so putting your heart down. 請放心 and 你放心 reassure someone. 放心不下 is the opposite, "cannot stop worrying".

column3: Careful, watch out: 小心！ is a warning, and 小心 + verb gives advice: 小心路滑 "watch for the slippery road". 路上小心 is said to someone setting off. Literally "small heart".
column7: Take care on the way.
column9: Careful, watch out: 小心！ is a warning, and 小心 + verb gives advice: 小心路滑 "watch for the slippery road". 路上小心 is said to someone setting off. Literally "small heart".

column3: Sad, upset, a feeling: 我很难过. With 难 read nán, it also exists as "hard to get through". 难受 is close, but covers physical discomfort too.
column6: Tīngshuō tā zǒu le, wǒ hěn nánguò.
column7: I heard he left, and I'm sad.
column9: Sad, upset, a feeling: 我很難過. With 難 read nán, it also exists as "hard to get through". 難受 is close, but covers physical discomfort too.

column3: Covers bodily misery (头疼得很难受) and emotional pain (听到这个消息很难受). 难过 leans toward sadness, and 不舒服 is the milder "unwell". A stuffy room makes you 难受 too (屋里太闷了，很难受). One view is that 受 shows a hand, a boat and another hand, something handed over.
column7: I feel awful today.
column9: Covers bodily misery (頭疼得很難受) and emotional pain (聽到這個消息很難受). 難過 leans toward sadness, and 不舒服 is the milder "unwell". A stuffy room makes you 難受 too (屋裡太悶了，很難受). One view is that 受 shows a hand, a boat and another hand, something handed over.

column3: Ugly, unsightly, the opposite of 好看. 难 in front of a verb makes "hard to V", and here the meaning is "unpleasant to look at". It also describes an awkward moment or a bad look on a face.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài nánkàn le.
column7: This piece of clothing is so ugly.
column9: Ugly, unsightly, the opposite of 好看. 難 in front of a verb makes "hard to V", and here the meaning is "unpleasant to look at". It also describes an awkward moment or a bad look on a face.

column3: Unpleasant to hear, of a sound, a song or words. The opposite is 好听. The pattern 难 + verb is the same as in 难看: it says a thing is not pleasant to do.
column7: He sings badly.
column9: Unpleasant to hear, of a sound, a song or words. The opposite is 好聽. The pattern 難 + verb is the same as in 難看: it says a thing is not pleasant to do.

column3: Be willing to: 愿意 + verb, as in 你愿意来吗？ It states a wish that comes from the person, unlike 要, which can be a need. The 原 gives the sound.
column6: Nǐ yuànyì hé wǒ qù ma?
column7: Are you willing to go with me?
column9: Be willing to: 願意 + verb, as in 你願意來嗎？ It states a wish that comes from the person, unlike 要, which can be a need. The 原 gives the sound.

column3: Confidence: 有信心 "be confident". The person or thing you are confident about follows 对: 对自己有信心 "have confidence in oneself". 信 ("trust") plus 心 ("heart").
column7: I have confidence in myself.
column9: Confidence: 有信心 "be confident". The person or thing you are confident about follows 對: 對自己有信心 "have confidence in oneself". 信 ("trust") plus 心 ("heart").

column3: Care about, be concerned for: 关心 + person, as in 关心他. 谢谢你的关心 is the usual thanks for a kind word. It is about caring in the heart, not about taking care of a thing.
column7: Thank you for your concern.
column9: Care about, be concerned for: 關心 + person, as in 關心他. 謝謝你的關心 is the usual thanks for a kind word. It is about caring in the heart, not about taking care of a thing.

column3: Thank, a more formal word than 谢谢. It takes the person or the help directly: 感谢你的帮助, 感谢大家. It is used in speeches and writing, and in everyday talk 谢谢 is enough.
column7: Thank you for your help.
column9: Thank, a more formal word than 謝謝. It takes the person or the help directly: 感謝你的幫助, 感謝大家. It is used in speeches and writing, and in everyday talk 謝謝 is enough.

column3: Welcome: 欢迎你 "welcome, you". The shop greeting is 欢迎光临. It is also a verb: 欢迎你来我家 "you are welcome to come to my home".
column7: You are welcome at my home.
column9: Welcome: 歡迎你 "welcome, you". The shop greeting is 歡迎光臨. It is also a verb: 歡迎你來我家 "you are welcome to come to my home".

column3: A soft "excuse me" before a request or a small apology (不好意思，我来晚了); for a real wrong say 对不起. About yourself it means "I feel embarrassed", and in 你还好意思说？ the 好意思 half is "have the nerve". 思 may show the soft spot of the head 囟 over the heart 心.
column7: Sorry, I'm late.
column9: A soft "excuse me" before a request or a small apology (不好意思，我來晚了); for a real wrong say 對不起. About yourself it means "I feel embarrassed", and in 你還好意思說？ the 好意思 half is "have the nerve". 思 may show the soft spot of the head 囟 over the heart 心.

column3: Treat someone, pay for the meal: a verb and its object, 请 ("invite") plus 客 ("guest"). 我请客 means "my treat". The guest is the one who is invited.
column7: It's my treat today.
column9: Treat someone, pay for the meal: a verb and its object, 請 ("invite") plus 客 ("guest"). 我請客 means "my treat". The guest is the one who is invited.

column3: Request, ask for: more formal than 请. 请求 + person + verb: 他请求我帮忙. It is also a noun, "a request": 同意他的请求.
column7: He asked me for help.
column9: Request, ask for: more formal than 請. 請求 + person + verb: 他請求我幫忙. It is also a noun, "a request": 同意他的請求.

column3: Beg, ask for earnestly: 求你了 "please, I'm begging you". 求 + person + verb: 求你帮我一下. It is stronger than 请, and also means "seek": 求学 "study".
column7: Please, help me out.
column9: Beg, ask for earnestly: 求你了 "please, I'm begging you". 求 + person + verb: 求你幫我一下. It is stronger than 請, and also means "seek": 求學 "study".

column3: Agree, promise: 答应 + verb, as in 他答应来. It also means "answer, reply" to a call: 答应一声. 答 is read dā here, and 应 is light: dāying.
column7: He promised to help me.
column9: Agree, promise: 答應 + verb, as in 他答應來. It also means "answer, reply" to a call: 答應一聲. 答 is read dā here, and 應 is light: dāying.

column3: Hello? or "Hey!", used to answer the phone or to call to someone: 喂，你好. It is read wèi in the fourth tone. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part, as in other calling and speaking sounds.
column7: Hello, where are you?
column9: Hello? or "Hey!", used to answer the phone or to call to someone: 喂，你好. It is read wèi in the fourth tone. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part, as in other calling and speaking sounds.

column3: A sentence-ending particle that warms up a sentence: 好啊 "sure!", 你好啊. The tone is light a5, and after a vowel sound it blends into ya and is often written 呀. It does not carry meaning on its own.
column7: The weather is really nice today!
column9: A sentence-ending particle that warms up a sentence: 好啊 "sure!", 你好啊. The tone is light a5, and after a vowel sound it blends into ya and is often written 呀. It does not carry meaning on its own.

column3: Goes beyond single people: 友好关系, 友好访问 and 友好城市 "sister city" are standard in news and diplomacy. Of a person it means well-disposed (他对我很友好); 友善 stresses kindness and 热情 warmth. In the old explanation 友 is two hands, so friendship.
column6: Zhèlǐ de rén dōu hěn yǒuhǎo.
column7: The people here are all friendly.
column9: Goes beyond single people: 友好關係, 友好訪問 and 友好城市 "sister city" are standard in news and diplomacy. Of a person it means well-disposed (他對我很友好); 友善 stresses kindness and 熱情 warmth. In the old explanation 友 is two hands, so friendship.

column3: Warm, enthusiastic, of a person who welcomes you: 热 ("hot") plus 情 ("feeling"). 他很热情 "he is very warm". With 地 it turns into an adverb: 热情地欢迎.
column7: The teacher is very warm to us.
column9: Warm, enthusiastic, of a person who welcomes you: 熱 ("hot") plus 情 ("feeling"). 他很熱情 "he is very warm". With 地 it turns into an adverb: 熱情地歡迎.

column3: Good night, said when someone goes to bed or you part late. Not "good evening", which is 晚上好. 晚 ("late") plus 安 ("peaceful"). A typical pair is 晚安，明天见.
column7: Good night, see you tomorrow.
column9: Good night, said when someone goes to bed or you part late. Not "good evening", which is 晚上好. 晚 ("late") plus 安 ("peaceful"). A typical pair is 晚安，明天見.

column3: Literally "add oil", a cheer: "Go for it!" "Come on!" It is shouted at sports, or said to someone who has a hard task. It also means "fill up with gas".
column7: Come on, you can do it!
column9: Literally "add oil", a cheer: "Go for it!" "Come on!" It is shouted at sports, or said to someone who has a hard task. It also means "fill up with gas".

column3: A fixed wish to someone who sets off: "have a safe trip". 一路 ("the whole way") plus 平安 ("safe and sound"). Say it as 祝你一路平安.
column7: Have a safe trip!
column9: A fixed wish to someone who sets off: "have a safe trip". 一路 ("the whole way") plus 平安 ("safe and sound"). Say it as 祝你一路平安.

column3: A fixed wish to someone who is leaving: "bon voyage". Literally "may the wind be smooth the whole way": 一路 plus 顺风 ("with a following wind"). Often paired with 一路平安.
column7: Bon voyage!
column9: A fixed wish to someone who is leaving: "bon voyage". Literally "may the wind be smooth the whole way": 一路 plus 順風 ("with a following wind"). Often paired with 一路平安.

column3: Early morning: 早 ("early") plus 晨 ("morning"). It sounds a little more written than 早上, and it is the stretch just after sunrise: 早晨的空气 "the morning air". 晨 hardly occurs on its own.
column7: The morning air is good.
column9: Early morning: 早 ("early") plus 晨 ("morning"). It sounds a little more written than 早上, and it is the stretch just after sunrise: 早晨的空氣 "the morning air". 晨 hardly occurs on its own.

column3: Any time in the dead of night, not an exact hour. It goes before the verb like other time words: 半夜醒来, 半夜才回家. 半夜三更 is the idiom for "in the dead of night". 半 was built as 八 "to divide" and a cow 牛: cutting a cow into two halves.
column7: He didn't come home until the middle of the night.
column9: Any time in the dead of night, not an exact hour. It goes before the verb like other time words: 半夜醒來, 半夜才回家. 半夜三更 is the idiom for "in the dead of night". 半 was built as 八 "to divide" and a cow 牛: cutting a cow into two halves.

column3: Night: 夜里 and 半夜 use it. Alone it feels more written than 晚上 and appears in set phrases and compounds: 夜深了 "the night is late". Compare 晚上 "evening", the common spoken word.
column6: Yè shēn le, kuài shuì ba.
column7: It's late at night, go to sleep.
column9: Night: 夜裡 and 半夜 use it. Alone it feels more written than 晚上 and appears in set phrases and compounds: 夜深了 "the night is late". Compare 晚上 "evening", the common spoken word.

column3: At night: 夜 ("night") plus 里 ("inside"). Used like 晚上, it is a time word and goes before the verb. 里 is light: yèli.
column7: It is cold at night.
column9: At night: 夜 ("night") plus 裡 ("inside"). Used like 晚上, it is a time word and goes before the verb. 裡 is light: yèli.

column3: Nap after lunch: 午 ("noon") plus 睡 ("sleep"). The phrase 睡午觉 means the same, with 觉 read jiào. Both the habit and the act: 我每天午睡 "I nap every day".
column7: I take a nap every day.
column9: Nap after lunch: 午 ("noon") plus 睡 ("sleep"). The phrase 睡午覺 means the same, with 覺 read jiào. Both the habit and the act: 我每天午睡 "I nap every day".

column3: Evening party, evening show: 晚 ("evening") plus 会 ("gathering"). The famous 春节晚会 is a New Year's Eve television show. Here 会 means "gathering", not "can".
column7: There is a party this evening.
column9: Evening party, evening show: 晚 ("evening") plus 會 ("gathering"). The famous 春節晚會 is a New Year's Eve television show. Here 會 means "gathering", not "can".

column3: Week, as a measure: 一周, 三周 "three weeks". Also a surname, and the name of an old dynasty. It is also in 周末 "weekend", 上周 "last week" and 下周 "next week".
column6: Wǒ xué le sān zhōu Hànyǔ.
column7: I have studied Chinese for three weeks.
column9: Week, as a measure: 一週, 三週 "three weeks". Also a surname, and the name of an old dynasty. It is also in 週末 "weekend", 上週 "last week" and 下週 "next week".

column3: Weekend: 周 ("week") plus 末 ("end"). 周末 is a time word, put before the verb: 周末我去爬山.
column7: Are you free at the weekend?
column9: Weekend: 週 ("week") plus 末 ("end"). 週末 is a time word, put before the verb: 週末我去爬山.

column3: Last week: 上 ("above, previous") plus 周. 上周三 is "last Wednesday". The matching word for next week is 下周. As a time word it goes before the verb, or at the start of the sentence.
column7: Last week I went to Beijing.
column9: Last week: 上 ("above, previous") plus 週. 上週三 is "last Wednesday". The matching word for next week is 下週. As a time word it goes before the verb, or at the start of the sentence.

column3: A time word, so it sits before the verb or the subject: 下周见, 下周三 "next Wednesday". Speech often says 下个星期 or 下礼拜; the pair is 上周 last week and 这周 this week. 周 began as a picture of a jade ornament with carved patterns.
column7: We have an exam next week.
column9: A time word, so it sits before the verb or the subject: 下週見, 下週三 "next Wednesday". Speech often says 下個星期 or 下禮拜; the pair is 上周 last week and 這週 this week. 週 began as a picture of a jade ornament with carved patterns.

column3: Month, as a named month of the year: 三月份 "the month of March", 哪个月份 "which month". For a length of time use 个月: 三个月. 份 is read fèn here, with 分 as the sound part.
column7: In which month are you coming?
column9: Month, as a named month of the year: 三月份 "the month of March", 哪個月份 "which month". For a length of time use 個月: 三個月. 份 is read fèn here, with 分 as the sound part.

column3: Day, days and "life": 日子 is a particular day (好日子 "a good day") and the days of one's life: 日子过得很好 "life is going well". The 子 is light: rìzi. 天 is used to count days.
column7: Today is a good day.
column9: Day, days and "life": 日子 is a particular day (好日子 "a good day") and the days of one's life: 日子過得很好 "life is going well". The 子 is light: rìzi. 天 is used to count days.

column3: The year before last: 前 ("before") plus 年. It follows 今年 and 去年, going back in the same pattern. It is used as a time word before the verb. 前天 "the day before yesterday" works the same way.
column7: I went to Beijing the year before last.
column9: The year before last: 前 ("before") plus 年. It follows 今年 and 去年, going back in the same pattern. It is used as a time word before the verb. 前天 "the day before yesterday" works the same way.

column3: The whole year: 全 ("whole") plus 年. Often with 都: 全年都很热 "hot all year". 全年 has the same pattern as 全家 and 全身.
column7: It is hot here all year.
column9: The whole year: 全 ("whole") plus 年. Often with 都: 全年都很熱 "hot all year". 全年 has the same pattern as 全家 and 全身.

column3: Minute as a length of time: 十分钟 "ten minutes". For the minute on the clock, 分 is used alone: 三点十分. Do not put 个 before 分钟.
column7: I waited ten minutes.
column9: Minute as a length of time: 十分鐘 "ten minutes". For the minute on the clock, 分 is used alone: 三點十分. Do not put 個 before 分鐘.

column3: Holiday period, vacation: 假 ("leave") plus 期 ("period"). 假 is read jià here, but jiǎ in 假 "fake". 放假 is "to be on vacation". 暑假 is the summer vacation.
column7: Where do you want to go in the holidays?
column9: Holiday period, vacation: 假 ("leave") plus 期 ("period"). 假 is read jià here, but jiǎ in 假 "fake". 放假 is "to be on vacation". 暑假 is the summer vacation.

column3: Time off you take as an employee: 休年假, 休了三天假. A holiday given to everyone, such as a school break, is 放假; asking for leave is 请假, and a vacation trip is 度假. 假 is read jià here, meaning vacation; read jiǎ it means fake.
column7: I am on leave next week.
column9: Time off you take as an employee: 休年假, 休了三天假. A holiday given to everyone, such as a school break, is 放假; asking for leave is 請假, and a vacation trip is 度假. 假 is read jià here, meaning vacation; read jiǎ it means fake.

column3: The school term begins: 开 ("open") plus 学 ("school"), a verb and its object. 开学了 says classes have started again. 开学第一天 is "the first day of term".
column7: School starts again next week.
column9: The school term begins: 開 ("open") plus 學 ("school"), a verb and its object. 開學了 says classes have started again. 開學第一天 is "the first day of term".

column3: School term, semester: 上学期 "last term", 这学期 "this term", 下学期 "next term". 学 ("study") plus 期 ("period"). A term is not a school year; that is学年.
column7: I am very busy this term.
column9: School term, semester: 上學期 "last term", 這學期 "this term", 下學期 "next term". 學 ("study") plus 期 ("period"). A term is not a school year; that is學年.

column3: When I was little (or "when one was little"): 小 plus 时候 ("time"). The phrase usually stands at the start of the sentence and sets the time. The light 候 gives xiǎoshíhou.
column7: When I was little, I lived in Beijing.
column9: When I was little (or "when one was little"): 小 plus 時候 ("time"). The phrase usually stands at the start of the sentence and sets the time. The light 候 gives xiǎoshíhou.

column3: From childhood: 从 ("from") plus 小 ("small, young"). It sits before the verb and is often followed by 就: 从小就学汉语 "has learned Chinese since childhood".
column7: He has studied Chinese since he was little.
column9: From childhood: 從 ("from") plus 小 ("small, young"). It sits before the verb and is often followed by 就: 從小就學漢語 "has learned Chinese since childhood".
