column3: Have free time, with the spoken ending 儿 that makes kòngr. 有空 means the same thing. Asking it invites someone: 你明天有空儿吗？ 空 is read kòng here, but kōng in 空气.
column7: Are you free tomorrow?
column9: Have free time, with the spoken ending 兒 that makes kòngr. 有空 means the same thing. Asking it invites someone: 你明天有空兒嗎？ 空 is read kòng here, but kōng in 空氣.

column3: Anniversary: the number goes before it, as in 十周年 "tenth anniversary". It is also used for institutions and schools.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn shí zhōunián le.
column7: This shop has reached its tenth anniversary.
column9: Anniversary: the number goes before it, as in 十週年 "tenth anniversary". It is also used for institutions and schools.

column3: What children call grown-ups: 大人 and 小孩 together cover everyone, as in 大人说话，小孩别插嘴. On tickets and in law the formal word is 成人 (成人票). In historical dramas 大人 is also how you address an official, "Your Excellency".
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng dàren yě xǐhuan.
column7: Adults like this film too.
column9: What children call grown-ups: 大人 and 小孩 together cover everyone, as in 大人說話，小孩別插嘴. On tickets and in law the formal word is 成人 (成人票). In historical dramas 大人 is also how you address an official, "Your Excellency".

column3: Good person: 好 plus 人. 他是个好人 says he is a kind, decent person. It is the opposite of 坏人. It is a noun, with no 的 between 好 and 人.
column7: He is a good person.
column9: Good person: 好 plus 人. 他是個好人 says he is a kind, decent person. It is the opposite of 壞人. It is a noun, with no 的 between 好 and 人.

column3: Bad person, villain in stories and films: 坏 ("bad") plus 人. 坏 also means "broken": 手机坏了. The opposite is 好人 "good person".
column4: 电影里有好人，也有坏人。
column5: 電影裡有好人，也有壞人。
column6: Diànyǐng lǐ yǒu hǎorén, yě yǒu huàirén.
column7: In the film there are good people and bad people.
column9: Bad person, villain in stories and films: 壞 ("bad") plus 人. 壞 also means "broken": 手機壞了. The opposite is 好人 "good person".

column3: Guest, visitor: 来客人了 "guests have come". Its opposite is 主人, the host. 客 has 宀 (roof) on top, and the 各 below gives the sound. 客人 is also a customer in a shop or restaurant.
column7: Guests have come to our home.
column9: Guest, visitor: 來客人了 "guests have come". Its opposite is 主人, the host. 客 has 宀 (roof) on top, and the 各 below gives the sound. 客人 is also a customer in a shop or restaurant.

column3: Host, owner, as against 客人. The owner of a house, or a pet: 小狗的主人. 主 on its own means "main, chief", as in 主要. 主人 is the one who receives guests.
column7: The puppy is waiting for its owner.
column9: Host, owner, as against 客人. The owner of a house, or a pet: 小狗的主人. 主 on its own means "main, chief", as in 主要. 主人 is the one who receives guests.

column3: Pedestrian, passer-by: 行 here is read xíng and means "walk, go", and 人 is "person". It is the word used on signs, like 行人请走人行道. In 银行 the same 行 is read háng.
column7: There are no pedestrians on the road.
column9: Pedestrian, passer-by: 行 here is read xíng and means "walk, go", and 人 is "person". It is the word used on signs, like 行人請走人行道. In 銀行 the same 行 is read háng.

column3: Someone, there is someone: 有人 + verb: 有人在敲门 "someone is knocking". As a question, 有人吗？ asks "is anyone there?" The opposite is 没有人, "nobody". The noun is not marked with 一个.
column7: Someone is waiting for you outside.
column9: Someone, there is someone: 有人 + verb: 有人在敲門 "someone is knocking". As a question, 有人嗎？ asks "is anyone there?" The opposite is 沒有人, "nobody". The noun is not marked with 一個.

column3: A general "people", never a counted group: no numbers (三个人, not 三个人们). Unlike 大家 "everyone here", it does not include the speaker. 们 attaches to other people-words too: 孩子们, 同学们, 朋友们. 们 is a late character, first attested in the Song dynasty.
column4: 春节的时候，人们都回家过年。
column5: 春節的時候，人們都回家過年。
column6: Chūnjié de shíhou, rénmen dōu huí jiā guò nián.
column7: At Spring Festival people all go home.
column9: A general "people", never a counted group: no numbers (三個人, not 三個人們). Unlike 大家 "everyone here", it does not include the speaker. 們 attaches to other people-words too: 孩子們, 同學們, 朋友們. 們 is a late character, first attested in the Song dynasty.

column3: Everyone, all of us: 大家好 is how you greet a group. 大家 can include the speaker, and it is followed by 都 when the group does something together: 大家都来了.
column7: Has everyone come?
column9: Everyone, all of us: 大家好 is how you greet a group. 大家 can include the speaker, and it is followed by 都 when the group does something together: 大家都來了.

column3: We, including the person you speak to: "you and I". It is a spoken word, and it is mostly met as 咱们. Pair it with a suggestion: 咱走吧 "let's go". Compare 我们, which may leave the listener out.
column7: Let's go.
column9: We, including the person you speak to: "you and I". It is a spoken word, and it is mostly met as 咱們. Pair it with a suggestion: 咱走吧 "let's go". Compare 我們, which may leave the listener out.

column3: We including the listener: 咱们一起去吧 "let's go together". 我们 may or may not include the person you talk to, but 咱们 always does. It is a spoken word.
column7: Let's go together.
column9: We including the listener: 咱們一起去吧 "let's go together". 我們 may or may not include the person you talk to, but 咱們 always does. It is a spoken word.

column3: It, for things and animals but not people: 我喜欢它 "I like it". The subject is often left out in Chinese, so 它 appears mostly where the thing needs to be named again.
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn hǎo, wǒ xǐhuan tā.
column7: This book is good, I like it.
column9: It, for things and animals but not people: 我喜歡它 "I like it". The subject is often left out in Chinese, so 它 appears mostly where the thing needs to be named again. In Taiwan 牠 is also used for an animal.

column3: They or "them", for things and animals, never for people: 我喜欢它们. The plural ending 们 is added to 它. People are 他们 and 她们.
column4: 这些书很好，我都喜欢它们。
column5: 這些書很好，我都喜歡它們。
column6: Zhèxiē shū hěn hǎo, wǒ dōu xǐhuan tāmen.
column7: These books are good, I like them all.
column9: They or "them", for things and animals, never for people: 我喜歡它們. The plural ending 們 is added to 它. People are 他們 and 她們. In Taiwan animals may be written 牠們.

column3: Oneself, repeated for emphasis: 我自己 "myself", 自己做 "do it oneself". It follows the person: 他自己, 你自己. Take care with the shape of 己: it is open at the top, 已 (yǐ, in 已经) is half closed and 巳 is closed.
column7: I cook for myself.
column9: Oneself, repeated for emphasis: 我自己 "myself", 自己做 "do it oneself". It follows the person: 他自己, 你自己. Take care with the shape of 己: it is open at the top, 已 (yǐ, in 已經) is half closed and 巳 is closed.

column3: Wife or "Mrs", a married woman. 他太太 is "his wife", and 王太太 is "Mrs Wang". The second 太 is light: tàitai. When a man speaks of his own wife he can say 我太太. It is for a married woman, not a girlfriend.
column7: His wife is a doctor.
column9: Wife or "Mrs", a married woman. 他太太 is "his wife", and 王太太 is "Mrs Wang". The second 太 is light: tàitai. When a man speaks of his own wife he can say 我太太. It is for a married woman, not a girlfriend.

column3: Spouse (husband or wife) in 我爱人 "my husband/wife", said of the person you are married to; a rather formal way to refer to them. 爱 ("love") plus 人. It does not mean "lover": that is 情人, which in everyday speech usually means a partner in an affair.
column7: My spouse works at a bank.
column9: Spouse (husband or wife) in 我愛人 "my husband/wife", said of the person you are married to; a rather formal way to refer to them. 愛 ("love") plus 人. It does not mean "lover": that is 情人, which in everyday speech usually means a partner in an affair.

column3: Romantic love only, as a subject: 爱情故事, 爱情电影. Love among family is 亲情 and among friends 友情, and the three go together in the phrase 亲情、友情、爱情.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge àiqíng gùshi.
column7: This is a love story.
column9: Romantic love only, as a subject: 愛情故事, 愛情電影. Love among family is 親情 and among friends 友情, and the three go together in the phrase 親情、友情、愛情.

column3: Family, household as a unit: 家庭 is more formal than 家. It goes with 成员 "member" and with 幸福 "happy": 家庭成员 "family member". 庭 on its own means "yard".
column7: My family is big.
column9: Family, household as a unit: 家庭 is more formal than 家. It goes with 成員 "member" and with 幸福 "happy": 家庭成員 "family member". 庭 on its own means "yard".

column3: Parent, guardian of a student: 家长会 is a parents' meeting at school. 长 is read zhǎng.
column7: The teacher asks the parents to come to school.
column9: Parent, guardian of a student: 家長會 is a parents' meeting at school. 長 is read zhǎng.

column3: The whole family: 全 ("whole") plus 家. Often 全家人, with 人. With 都 it means all of them: 全家都在北京 "the whole family is in Beijing". The same pattern as 全身 and 全年.
column7: The whole family is in Beijing.
column9: The whole family: 全 ("whole") plus 家. Often 全家人, with 人. With 都 it means all of them: 全家都在北京 "the whole family is in Beijing". The same pattern as 全身 and 全年.

column3: Make friends: 交 ("hand over, associate with") plus 朋友, a verb and its object. 交朋友 means to form a friendship, and 交了一个朋友 "made a friend". 交 appears in 交通 and 交流 too.
column7: I want to make friends here.
column9: Make friends: 交 ("hand over, associate with") plus 朋友, a verb and its object. 交朋友 means to form a friendship, and 交了一個朋友 "made a friend". 交 appears in 交通 and 交流 too.

column3: Old friend: 老 here means "long-standing", not "aged". The old friend is one you have known a long time. 老 is also a friendly prefix in 老师. The light ending gives lǎopéngyou.
column7: He is an old friend of mine.
column9: Old friend: 老 here means "long-standing", not "aged". The old friend is one you have known a long time. 老 is also a friendly prefix in 老師. The light ending gives lǎopéngyou.

column3: Colleague, co-worker: 同 ("same") plus 事 ("work, matter"), someone who shares the same work. Compare 同学, "classmate". 事 on its own means "matter, thing". The two words are 同事 and 同学.
column7: He is my colleague.
column9: Colleague, co-worker: 同 ("same") plus 事 ("work, matter"), someone who shares the same work. Compare 同學, "classmate". 事 on its own means "matter, thing". The two words are 同事 and 同學.

column3: Surname, and as a verb "be surnamed": 你姓什么？ asks for the surname only. The surname goes after 姓: 我姓王. To give a full name, use 叫: 我叫王明.
column7: My surname is Wang.
column9: Surname, and as a verb "be surnamed": 你姓什麼？ asks for the surname only. The surname goes after 姓: 我姓王. To give a full name, use 叫: 我叫王明.

column3: The word on forms and official lists (姓名：), for family name and given name together. In conversation you ask 你叫什么名字？, and 你姓什么？ asks only the family name.
column7: Please write your full name.
column9: The word on forms and official lists (姓名：), for family name and given name together. In conversation you ask 你叫什麼名字？, and 你姓什麼？ asks only the family name.

column3: Because. 因为 starts the reason clause, and 所以 often starts the result clause: 因为下雨，所以我没去. Chinese can use both, though English uses only one.
column6: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒ méi qù.
column7: Because it rained, I didn't go.
column9: Because. 因為 starts the reason clause, and 所以 often starts the result clause: 因為下雨，所以我沒去. Chinese can use both, though English uses only one.

column3: So, therefore: it opens the result clause. It often follows 因为: 因为…，所以… . It can be used without 因为: 我累了，所以想睡觉.
column6: Wǒ lèi le, suǒyǐ xiǎng shuìjiào.
column7: I'm tired, so I want to sleep.
column9: So, therefore: it opens the result clause. It often follows 因為: 因為…，所以… . It can be used without 因為: 我累了，所以想睡覺.

column3: But, the shortest of the group: 但 starts the second clause, which goes against the first. 但是 is the usual form, and 但 is somewhat more written.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dàn méiyǒu shíjiān.
column7: I want to go, but I have no time.
column9: But, the shortest of the group: 但 starts the second clause, which goes against the first. 但是 is the usual form, and 但 is somewhat more written.

column3: But, however, the standard word. It starts the second clause: 这个很好，但是太贵了. It pairs with 虽然: 虽然…，但是… . 可是 and 不过 do the same job, in a more spoken way.
column6: Zhège hěn hǎo, dànshì tài guì le.
column7: This one is good, but too expensive.
column9: But, however, the standard word. It starts the second clause: 這個很好，但是太貴了. It pairs with 雖然: 雖然…，但是… . 可是 and 不過 do the same job, in a more spoken way.

column3: But, the same job as 但是 and a more spoken one. It starts a clause that goes against the one before: 他很累，可是还想工作. 可 on its own is not "but".
column6: Tā hěn lèi, kěshì hái xiǎng gōngzuò.
column7: He is tired, but he still wants to work.
column9: But, the same job as 但是 and a more spoken one. It starts a clause that goes against the one before: 他很累，可是還想工作. 可 on its own is not "but".

column3: But, however, softer than 但是: it adds a note that limits what was said before. 菜很好吃，不过有点贵. Spoken more than written. Dictionaries write the tone of 不 as bù here, though people say bú before the fourth tone.
column6: Cài hěn hǎochī, bùguò yǒudiǎn guì.
column7: The food is tasty, but a bit pricey.
column9: But, however, softer than 但是: it adds a note that limits what was said before. 菜很好吃，不過有點貴. Spoken more than written. Dictionaries write the tone of 不 as bù here, though people say bú before the fourth tone.

column3: Although: 虽然…，但是… . Chinese puts 但是 or 可是 in the second clause, where English has no "but". 虽然 comes before the subject or the verb.
column4: 虽然很累，但是我很开心。
column5: 雖然很累，但是我很開心。
column6: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì wǒ hěn kāixīn.
column7: Although I'm tired, I'm very happy.
column9: Although: 雖然…，但是… . Chinese puts 但是 or 可是 in the second clause, where English has no "but". 雖然 comes before the subject or the verb.

column3: Adds a further point in the same direction, between clauses or adjectives: 这家店很便宜，而且很好吃. It can open a new sentence, and 不但…而且… pairs it with "not only". 并且 does the same job but sounds more written. 而 began as a picture of a beard.
column6: Cài hěn hǎochī, érqiě bù guì.
column7: The food is tasty, and not expensive too.
column9: Adds a further point in the same direction, between clauses or adjectives: 這家店很便宜，而且很好吃. It can open a new sentence, and 不但…而且… pairs it with "not only". 並且 does the same job but sounds more written. 而 began as a picture of a beard.

column3: Not only: 不但…，而且… . 不但 stands before the verb if the subject is the same: 他不但会说，而且会写. If the subjects differ, put it before the first subject.
column6: Tā bùdàn huì shuō, érqiě huì xiě.
column7: He can not only speak but also write.
column9: Not only: 不但…，而且… . 不但 stands before the verb if the subject is the same: 他不但會說，而且會寫. If the subjects differ, put it before the first subject.

column3: If: 如果…，就… . The result clause usually has 就 or 会. 如果 starts the "if" clause: 如果明天下雨，我就不去. It can be followed by 的话 at the end, to say the same thing again.
column4: 如果明天下雨，我就不去。
column5: 如果明天下雨，我就不去。
column6: Rúguǒ míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒ jiù bù qù.
column7: If it rains tomorrow, I won't go.
column9: If: 如果…，就… . The result clause usually has 就 or 會. 如果 starts the "if" clause: 如果明天下雨，我就不去. It can be followed by 的話 at the end, to say the same thing again.

column3: If, put at the end of the "if" clause: 你有空的话，请来. It can team up with 如果 at the front. 话 is a "word", so it is literally "in the words of…". The 的 and 话 are said light: dehuà.
column6: Nǐ yǒu kòng dehuà, qǐng lái.
column7: If you are free, please come.
column9: If, put at the end of the "if" clause: 你有空的話，請來. It can team up with 如果 at the front. 話 is a "word", so it is literally "in the words of…". The 的 and 話 are said light: dehuà.

column3: As long as, a condition that is enough: 只要…，就… . 只要你来，我就高兴 "as long as you come, I'm happy". The first clause gives the condition and the second begins with 就.
column6: Zhǐyào nǐ lái, wǒ jiù gāoxìng.
column7: As long as you come, I'll be happy.
column9: As long as, a condition that is enough: 只要…，就… . 只要你來，我就高興 "as long as you come, I'm happy". The first clause gives the condition and the second begins with 就.

column3: Or, for offering choices in statements. It is a bit more written than 或者. Both names two options: 你可以走路或坐车. Questions use 还是 instead.
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zǒulù huò zuò chē.
column7: You can walk or take a car.
column9: Or, for offering choices in statements. It is a bit more written than 或者. Both names two options: 你可以走路或坐車. Questions use 還是 instead.

column3: Or in a statement: 我喝茶或者咖啡都可以. In a question, "or" is 还是: 你喝茶还是咖啡？ The two words are not interchangeable. 或者 can also mean "perhaps" at the start of a sentence.
column4: 我喝茶或者咖啡都可以。
column5: 我喝茶或者咖啡都可以。
column6: Wǒ hē chá huòzhě kāfēi dōu kěyǐ.
column7: I'm fine with tea or coffee.
column9: Or in a statement: 我喝茶或者咖啡都可以. In a question, "or" is 還是: 你喝茶還是咖啡？ The two words are not interchangeable. 或者 can also mean "perhaps" at the start of a sentence.

column3: For example, followed by what you give: 比如苹果. 比 ("compare") plus 如 ("be like"). It leads a list or a single example.
column7: I like fruit, for example apples.
column9: For example, followed by what you give: 比如蘋果. 比 ("compare") plus 如 ("be like"). It leads a list or a single example.

column3: Comes after a pause, like English "say,": 比如说，你可以去北京. Put after a category it lists items: 水果，比如说苹果和香蕉. 比如 is the shorter form, and 例如 the more formal written one.
column4: 我喜欢很多水果，比如说苹果、香蕉和西瓜。
column5: 我喜歡很多水果，比如說蘋果、香蕉和西瓜。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan hěn duō shuǐguǒ, bǐrúshuō píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo hé xīguā.
column7: I like many fruits, for example apples, bananas and watermelon.
column9: Comes after a pause, like English "say,": 比如說，你可以去北京. Put after a category it lists items: 水果，比如說蘋果和香蕉. 比如 is the shorter form, and 例如 the more formal written one.

column3: For example, the written form, more formal than 比如. It is followed by examples: 例如北京和上海. 例 means "example" and 如 "like". It tends to appear in reports and textbooks.
column4: 我去过很多地方，例如北京和上海。
column5: 我去過很多地方，例如北京和上海。
column6: Wǒ qù guo hěn duō dìfang, lìrú Běijīng hé Shànghǎi.
column7: I have been to many places, for example Beijing and Shanghai.
column9: For example, the written form, more formal than 比如. It is followed by examples: 例如北京和上海. 例 means "example" and 如 "like". It tends to appear in reports and textbooks.

column3: Example: 举个例子 or 举一个例子 "give an example". It follows 举 ("raise"), as in 举手. 例 is made of 亻 (person) and 列 as the sound part (liè). The 子 is light: lìzi.
column7: Please give an example.
column9: Example: 舉個例子 or 舉一個例子 "give an example". It follows 舉 ("raise"), as in 舉手. 例 is made of 亻 (person) and 列 as the sound part (liè). The 子 is light: lìzi.

column3: Classroom: 教 ("teach") plus 室 ("room"). It is the room itself, so 在教室里 "in the classroom". 室 is also in other rooms, such as 办公室 "office". Compare 课堂, which is the class as an event.
column7: We study in the classroom.
column9: Classroom: 教 ("teach") plus 室 ("room"). It is the room itself, so 在教室裡 "in the classroom". 室 is also in other rooms, such as 辦公室 "office". Compare 課堂, which is the class as an event.

column3: Class, lesson time, the setting of a lesson: 课堂上 "in class". Where 教室 is the room, 课堂 is what happens in it.
column7: Please don't talk in class.
column9: Class, lesson time, the setting of a lesson: 課堂上 "in class". Where 教室 is the room, 課堂 is what happens in it.

column3: Blackboard: 黑 ("black") plus 板 ("board"). 请看黑板 is what a teacher says. 擦黑板 is "wipe the board". 板 has 木 ("wood") on the left, and the sound part 反 is read fǎn.
column7: Please look at the blackboard.
column9: Blackboard: 黑 ("black") plus 板 ("board"). 請看黑板 is what a teacher says. 擦黑板 is "wipe the board". 板 has 木 ("wood") on the left, and the sound part 反 is read fǎn.

column3: Pen, pencil in general: any writing tool, with 支 as the measure word: 一支笔. 笔 is 竹 ("bamboo") over 毛 ("hair"), like a brush. Kinds of pen: 铅笔 "pencil", 钢笔 "fountain pen", 毛笔 "brush".
column7: Do you have a pen?
column9: Pen, pencil in general: any writing tool, with 支 as the measure word: 一支筆. 筆 is 竹 ("bamboo") over 聿. Kinds of pen: 鉛筆 "pencil", 鋼筆 "fountain pen", 毛筆 "brush".

column3: 记笔记 or 做笔记 is to take notes, and the notes themselves are 笔记 (借笔记 "borrow someone's notes"). 笔记本 is a notebook, and 笔记本电脑 a laptop, which people shorten to 笔记本.
column6: Wǒ zài kè shang jì bǐjì.
column7: I take notes in class.
column9: 記筆記 or 做筆記 is to take notes, and the notes themselves are 筆記 (借筆記 "borrow someone's notes"). 筆記本 is a notebook, and 筆記本電腦 a laptop, which people shorten to 筆記本.

column3: Notebook, the paper kind, and also a laptop when it is used with 电脑: 笔记本电脑. In speech 笔记本 on its own can mean the laptop too, so the context decides.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī ge bǐjìběn.
column7: I bought a notebook.
column9: Notebook, the paper kind, and also a laptop when it is used with 電腦: 筆記本電腦. In speech 筆記本 on its own can mean the laptop too, so the context decides.

column3: Homework: 做作业 or 写作业 "do homework". 作业 is not counted with 个; use 份 or 项. It can also be assigned work in general, as in 布置作业 "assign homework".
column6: Wǒ de zuòyè hái méi xiě wán.
column7: I haven't finished my homework.
column9: Homework: 做作業 or 寫作業 "do homework". 作業 is not counted with 個; use 份 or 項. It can also be assigned work in general, as in 佈置作業 "assign homework".

column3: Composition, essay written at school or in an exam: 写作文 "write an essay". 作 ("make") plus 文 ("writing"). A short piece of writing for class is 作文, not a research paper.
column7: The teacher has us write an essay.
column9: Composition, essay written at school or in an exam: 寫作文 "write an essay". 作 ("make") plus 文 ("writing"). A short piece of writing for class is 作文, not a research paper.

column3: Question, problem on a test or exercise: 这道题 "this question", with 道 as the measure word. Compare 问题, which is any question or issue. 题 is also "title, topic": 题目.
column7: This question is very hard.
column9: Question, problem on a test or exercise: 這道題 "this question", with 道 as the measure word. Compare 問題, which is any question or issue. 題 is also "title, topic": 題目.

column3: Hard problem, difficult question: 难 ("hard") plus 题 ("problem"). 一个难题 "a tough problem". 解决难题 is "solve a hard problem".
column7: This is a hard problem.
column9: Hard problem, difficult question: 難 ("hard") plus 題 ("problem"). 一個難題 "a tough problem". 解決難題 is "solve a hard problem".

column3: Score, mark in an exam: 分 ("point") plus 数 ("number"). 分数高 "a high score". Compare 成绩, which means results more broadly.
column7: What is your score?
column9: Score, mark in an exam: 分 ("point") plus 數 ("number"). 分數高 "a high score". Compare 成績, which means results more broadly.

column3: Results of study, sport or work measured against a standard: 成绩好, 考试成绩, and a school report is 成绩单. 分数 is the number on one test. For work, 取得好成绩 is "achieve good results". 绩 itself means to spin hemp, as well as merit.
column7: His grades are very good.
column9: Results of study, sport or work measured against a standard: 成績好, 考試成績, and a school report is 成績單. 分數 is the number on one test. For work, 取得好成績 is "achieve good results". 績 itself means to spin hemp, as well as merit.

column3: Examinee, test taker: 考 ("test") plus 生 ("student"). It is for people taking a formal exam, such as the 高考 college entrance exam. 考生 also appears on exam notices.
column7: Examinees, please take your seats.
column9: Examinee, test taker: 考 ("test") plus 生 ("student"). It is for people taking a formal exam, such as the 高考 college entrance exam. 考生 also appears on exam notices.

column3: Review, revise what was learned before: 复习课文 "review the text". The first character 复 means "repeat". It is the opposite of 预习 "preview".
column4: 我明天考试，现在要复习。
column5: 我明天考試，現在要複習。
column6: Wǒ míngtiān kǎoshì, xiànzài yào fùxí.
column7: I have an exam tomorrow, so I must review now.
column9: Review, revise what was learned before: 複習課文 "review the text". The first character 複 means "repeat". It is the opposite of 預習 "preview".

column3: Practice, exercise: a verb (练习写汉字) and a noun (做练习 "do exercises"). 练 ("train") plus 习 ("practice"). Used for skills you improve by repeating them.
column7: I practice writing characters every day.
column9: Practice, exercise: a verb (練習寫漢字) and a noun (做練習 "do exercises"). 練 ("train") plus 習 ("practice"). Used for skills you improve by repeating them.

column3: Practice, train, often before the thing practiced: 练字 "practice handwriting", 练球 "practice a ball game". It also stands in 练习 "practice".
column7: He practices handwriting every day.
column9: Practice, train, often before the thing practiced: 練字 "practice handwriting", 練球 "practice a ball game". It also stands in 練習 "practice".

column3: Internship, work experience: 实习生 is an intern. 实 ("real") plus 习 ("practice"): practice in real work. It is used as a verb: 在公司实习.
column6: Tā zài yī jiā gōngsī shíxí.
column7: He is doing an internship at a company.
column9: Internship, work experience: 實習生 is an intern. 實 ("real") plus 習 ("practice"): practice in real work. It is used as a verb: 在公司實習.

column3: Grade, year in school: 一年级 "first grade", 三年级 "third grade". 年 ("year") plus 级 ("level"). Put the number before it. 大三 is the short form for the third year of university.
column7: I am in third grade.
column9: Grade, year in school: 一年級 "first grade", 三年級 "third grade". 年 ("year") plus 級 ("level"). Put the number before it. 大三 is the short form for the third year of university.

column3: A verb plus its object, so it splits: 报了名, 还没报名. After it comes what you sign up for: 报名参加比赛, 报名学汉语. 报名表 is the form and 报名费 the fee.
column7: I want to sign up to study Chinese.
column9: A verb plus its object, so it splits: 報了名, 還沒報名. After it comes what you sign up for: 報名參加比賽, 報名學漢語. 報名表 is the form and 報名費 the fee.

column3: Here "learn by heart, recite": 背课文 "recite a text from memory". The same 背 is also "back", read bèi (后背), and "to carry on the back", read bēi (背包). Which one is meant depends on the word it is used in.
column7: I am memorizing the text.
column9: Here "learn by heart, recite": 背課文 "recite a text from memory". The same 背 is also "back", read bèi (後背), and "to carry on the back", read bēi (背包). Which one is meant depends on the word it is used in.

column3: Print with a printer: 打 ("hit") plus 印 ("press, print"). 打印机 is a printer, and 打印 + file or paper: 打印文件. 打 is used for many actions, such as 打电话 and 打球.
column7: I want to print this.
column9: Print with a printer: 打 ("hit") plus 印 ("press, print"). 打印機 is a printer, and 打印 + file or paper: 打印文件. 打 is used for many actions, such as 打電話 and 打球.

column3: Level, standard of ability: 汉语水平 "Chinese level", 水平高 "high level". It also means "horizontal".
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng hěn gāo.
column7: His level of Chinese is very high.
column9: Level, standard of ability: 漢語水平 "Chinese level", 水平高 "high level". It also means "horizontal".

column3: Teacher as a profession: 她是一名教师 "she is a teacher". For addressing a teacher, 老师 is used instead; 教师 describes the job.
column7: She is a teacher.
column9: Teacher as a profession: 她是一名教師 "she is a teacher". For addressing a teacher, 老師 is used instead; 教師 describes the job.

column3: Education: a noun and a verb. 教育孩子 "to educate children", 受教育 "receive an education". 教育对孩子很重要 states the topic. It covers both school and upbringing at home.
column7: Education is very important for children.
column9: Education: a noun and a verb. 教育孩子 "to educate children", 受教育 "receive an education". 教育對孩子很重要 states the topic. It covers both school and upbringing at home.

column3: Teaching, the activity of teachers: 教学方法 "teaching method", 教学楼 "teaching building". 教 is read jiào here. It is the teacher's side of things, and 学习 is the student's.
column6: Tā de jiàoxué hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: His teaching is very interesting.
column9: Teaching, the activity of teachers: 教學方法 "teaching method", 教學樓 "teaching building". 教 is read jiào here. It is the teacher's side of things, and 學習 is the student's.

column3: Campus: 校 ("school") plus 园 ("garden, park"). 校园里 "on campus". 校园生活 is "campus life".
column6: Xiàoyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō shù.
column7: There are many trees on campus.
column9: Campus: 校 ("school") plus 園 ("garden, park"). 校園裡 "on campus". 校園生活 is "campus life".

column3: Also how you address them: 王校长, surname first. The same 长 ends 班长 class monitor, 市长 mayor, 部长 minister and 组长 team leader. 长 is read zhǎng here, meaning chief or head; read cháng it means long.
column7: The principal has come to see us.
column9: Also how you address them: 王校長, surname first. The same 長 ends 班長 class monitor, 市長 mayor, 部長 minister and 組長 team leader. 長 is read zhǎng here, meaning chief or head; read cháng it means long.

column3: Class monitor, class leader: 班 ("class") plus 长 ("head"). The pattern is 班长, 校长, 组长. 他是我们班的班长.
column7: He is our class monitor.
column9: Class monitor, class leader: 班 ("class") plus 長 ("head"). The pattern is 班長, 校長, 組長. 他是我們班的班長.

column3: Small group, team for work in class or at work: 小 ("small") plus 组 ("group"). 分小组 "divide into groups".
column7: We split into three groups.
column9: Small group, team for work in class or at work: 小 ("small") plus 組 ("group"). 分小組 "divide into groups".

column3: Group, team, and a measure word for a set: 一组 "a group" or "a set". 三个人一组 "three people to a group". It is also a verb in 组成 "form".
column6: Tāmen sān ge rén yī zǔ.
column7: They are in groups of three.
column9: Group, team, and a measure word for a set: 一組 "a group" or "a set". 三個人一組 "three people to a group". It is also a verb in 組成 "form".

column3: Group leader: 组 ("group") plus 长 ("head"), as in 班长 and 校长. The head of a work team, a study group or a team in a project.
column7: Who is your group leader?
column9: Group leader: 組 ("group") plus 長 ("head"), as in 班長 and 校長. The head of a work team, a study group or a team in a project.

column3: Be made up of, form: 这个班由二十人组成 "this class is made up of twenty people". 由 introduces what it is made of, and 组成 goes after it. 成 shows the result.
column6: Zhège bān yóu èrshí rén zǔchéng.
column7: This class is made up of twenty people.
column9: Be made up of, form: 這個班由二十人組成 "this class is made up of twenty people". 由 introduces what it is made of, and 組成 goes after it. 成 shows the result.

column3: Primary and secondary schools together: 中小学生 are the pupils. A short way to say 中学 and 小学. 中小学 is the term used in notices.
column7: Primary and secondary schools have a holiday today.
column9: Primary and secondary schools together: 中小學生 are the pupils. A short way to say 中學 and 小學. 中小學 is the term used in notices.

column3: Sits between 初中 and university, with years named 高一, 高二, 高三; 上高中 is to be in it, and a pupil is a 高中生. Read gāozhòng, the same characters mean to pass an exam brilliantly, used in congratulations.
column7: He is in high school.
column9: Sits between 初中 and university, with years named 高一, 高二, 高三; 上高中 is to be in it, and a pupil is a 高中生. Read gāozhòng, the same characters mean to pass an exam brilliantly, used in congratulations.

column3: International student, student abroad: 留 ("stay") plus 学生. 留学 means to study in another country. A 留学生 is someone studying abroad, whether a foreigner in China or a Chinese person elsewhere.
column7: I am an international student.
column9: International student, student abroad: 留 ("stay") plus 學生. 留學 means to study in another country. A 留學生 is someone studying abroad, whether a foreigner in China or a Chinese person elsewhere.

column3: Subject, department, field: in school, a 科 is a subject. 你最喜欢哪一科？ is "which subject do you like best?" It is also a medical department, as in 内科 and 外科. The word often appears inside others, as in 科学.
column6: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan nǎ yī kē?
column7: Which subject do you like best?
column9: Subject, department, field: in school, a 科 is a subject. 你最喜歡哪一科？ is "which subject do you like best?" It is also a medical department, as in 內科 and 外科. The word often appears inside others, as in 科學.

column3: Science, and as an adjective "scientific": 科学家 is a scientist, 科学方法 a scientific method. It combines 科 ("subject") and 学 ("study").
column6: Wǒ duì kēxué hěn yǒu xìngqù.
column7: I am very interested in science.
column9: Science, and as an adjective "scientific": 科學家 is a scientist, 科學方法 a scientific method. It combines 科 ("subject") and 學 ("study").

column3: Physical education, sports as a school subject or a field: 体育课 is the PE class. It is the subject and activity, not a particular sport. 体 is "body" and 育 "raise, nurture".
column7: We have PE in the afternoon.
column9: Physical education, sports as a school subject or a field: 體育課 is the PE class. It is the subject and activity, not a particular sport. 體 is "body" and 育 "raise, nurture".

column3: Stadium, an open-air sports ground: 体育 ("sports") plus 场 ("field, place"). 场 turns up in other places for gathering: 广场 "square", 机场 "airport".
column6: Tǐyùchǎng lǐ yǒu hěn duō rén.
column7: There are many people in the stadium.
column9: Stadium, an open-air sports ground: 體育 ("sports") plus 場 ("field, place"). 場 turns up in other places for gathering: 廣場 "square", 機場 "airport".

column3: Gym, indoor sports hall: 体育 ("sports") plus 馆 ("hall"). 馆 is a building for a public purpose: 图书馆 "library", 饭馆 "restaurant".
column7: The match is in the sports hall.
column9: Gym, indoor sports hall: 體育 ("sports") plus 館 ("hall"). 館 is a building for a public purpose: 圖書館 "library", 飯館 "restaurant".

column3: A level in a ranked scale: 初级, 中级, 高级 run from beginner to advanced, 年级 is the school year, and HSK is counted in it (三级). After a number it is a measure word: 三级台阶 "three steps". An old dictionary gives 级 the original meaning of a "sequence" related to silk.
column7: Which level is this exam?
column9: A level in a ranked scale: 初級, 中級, 高級 run from beginner to advanced, 年級 is the school year, and HSK is counted in it (三級). After a number it is a measure word: 三級臺階 "three steps". An old dictionary gives 級 the original meaning of a "sequence" related to silk.

column3: Intermediate level: 中 ("middle") plus 级 ("level"). The usual series is 初级, 中级, 高级: beginner, intermediate, advanced. Courses and exams use it: 中级汉语.
column6: Wǒ xué de shì zhōngjí Hànyǔ.
column7: I am studying intermediate Chinese.
column9: Intermediate level: 中 ("middle") plus 級 ("level"). The usual series is 初級, 中級, 高級: beginner, intermediate, advanced. Courses and exams use it: 中級漢語.

column3: Advanced in level, and "high-end, high-class": 高级酒店 "a high-class hotel", 高级班 "advanced class". 高 ("high") plus 级 ("level").
column6: Zhè shì yī jiā gāojí fàndiàn.
column7: This is a high-class hotel.
column9: Advanced in level, and "high-end, high-class": 高級酒店 "a high-class hotel", 高級班 "advanced class". 高 ("high") plus 級 ("level").

column3: Yard on its own: 院里 "in the yard". It is mostly part of other words: 医院 "hospital", 学院 "college", 电影院 "cinema", and also 院子. Used alone it points to a courtyard.
column6: Yuàn lǐ yǒu yī kē shù.
column7: There is a tree in the yard.
column9: Yard on its own: 院裡 "in the yard". It is mostly part of other words: 醫院 "hospital", 學院 "college", 電影院 "cinema", and also 院子. Used alone it points to a courtyard.

column3: Head of an institution such as a hospital, college or research institute: 院 ("institution") plus 长 ("head"). Same pattern as 校长 and 班长.
column7: She is the head of the hospital.
column9: Head of an institution such as a hospital, college or research institute: 院 ("institution") plus 長 ("head"). Same pattern as 校長 and 班長.

column3: Word, a unit of language that can have one or more characters: 词 is a word, 字 is a character. 生词 is a new word, and 词典 a dictionary. 这个词的意思 is "the meaning of this word".
column7: What does this word mean?
column9: Word, a unit of language that can have one or more characters: 詞 is a word, 字 is a character. 生詞 is a new word, and 詞典 a dictionary. 這個詞的意思 is "the meaning of this word".

column3: Words and expressions, a general term for vocabulary: 学习词语 "learn vocabulary". It covers words and short set phrases, but it is the name for the group, not a single item.
column6: Wǒmen xué le hěn duō xīn cíyǔ.
column7: We learned a lot of new words.
column9: Words and expressions, a general term for vocabulary: 學習詞語 "learn vocabulary". It covers words and short set phrases, but it is the name for the group, not a single item.

column3: Dictionary for words, which are often more than one character. 查词典 "look up in a dictionary". A 字典 is for single characters. In everyday talk the two are often used for either.
column6: Wǒ yòng cídiǎn chá zhège cí.
column7: I look this word up in a dictionary.
column9: Dictionary for words, which are often more than one character. 查詞典 "look up in a dictionary". A 字典 is for single characters. In everyday talk the two are often used for either.

column3: Lists single characters with their readings, strokes and meaning; 词典 lists words. In speech 字典 is also loosely any dictionary, and 查字典 is the phrase for looking something up. 字 first meant to give birth to or nurture, a sense that has essentially become obsolete.
column6: Zhège zì wǒ yào chá zìdiǎn.
column7: I need to look this character up in the dictionary.
column9: Lists single characters with their readings, strokes and meaning; 詞典 lists words. In speech 字典 is also loosely any dictionary, and 查字典 is the phrase for looking something up. 字 first meant to give birth to or nurture, a sense that has essentially become obsolete.

column3: New word in vocabulary you have not yet learned: 生 ("raw, unfamiliar") plus 词. The list of new words at the end of a lesson is 生词表.
column6: Kèwén lǐ yǒu hěn duō shēngcí.
column7: There are many new words in the text.
column9: New word in vocabulary you have not yet learned: 生 ("raw, unfamiliar") plus 詞. The list of new words at the end of a lesson is 生詞表.

column3: The measure word for sentences and lines of speech: 一句话 "one sentence", 说一句 "say a sentence". For the sentence as a unit of grammar, the word is 句子. The 口 ("mouth") inside it points to speech.
column7: Please say one more sentence.
column9: The measure word for sentences and lines of speech: 一句話 "one sentence", 說一句 "say a sentence". For the sentence as a unit of grammar, the word is 句子. The 口 ("mouth") inside it points to speech.

column3: Sentence as a unit of language: 造句 "make a sentence", 写句子 "write sentences". Counted with 个 or 句: 一个句子. The 子 is light: jùzi.
column7: This sentence is very long.
column9: Sentence as a unit of language: 造句 "make a sentence", 寫句子 "write sentences". Counted with 個 or 句: 一個句子. The 子 is light: jùzi.

column3: Pronunciation of a character or word: 读 ("read aloud") plus 音 ("sound"). 这个字的读音 asks how to say that character.
column6: Zhège zì de dúyīn shì shénme?
column7: How is this character pronounced?
column9: Pronunciation of a character or word: 讀 ("read aloud") plus 音 ("sound"). 這個字的讀音 asks how to say that character.

column3: Syllable: 音 ("sound") plus 节 ("section"). In Chinese almost every character is one syllable, so 你好 has two syllables.
column6: Zhège cí yǒu sān ge yīnjié.
column7: This word has three syllables.
column9: Syllable: 音 ("sound") plus 節 ("section"). In Chinese almost every character is one syllable, so 你好 has two syllables.

column3: English the language, with 文 ("writing") that stresses the written form: 写英文 "write English". 英语 is more the spoken language, though the two overlap a lot. The 英 is for England.
column7: Can you write English?
column9: English the language, with 文 ("writing") that stresses the written form: 寫英文 "write English". 英語 is more the spoken language, though the two overlap a lot. The 英 is for England.

column3: Country syllable plus 语 makes a language name: 汉语, 日语, 法语, 德语, 西班牙语. 英语 is the language and school subject (说英语, 英语课); 英文 leans toward the written form (英文名字, 英文书).
column6: Tā shuō Yīngyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo.
column7: She speaks English very well.
column9: Country syllable plus 語 makes a language name: 漢語, 日語, 法語, 德語, 西班牙語. 英語 is the language and school subject (說英語, 英語課); 英文 leans toward the written form (英文名字, 英文書).

column3: Standard Mandarin: 说普通话 "speak Mandarin". The name literally means "common speech". In Taiwan people usually just say 中文; the official name there, 国语, sounds formal or old-fashioned.
column7: He can speak Mandarin.
column9: Standard Mandarin: 說普通話 "speak Mandarin". The name literally means "common speech". In Taiwan people usually just say 中文; the official name there, 國語, sounds formal or old-fashioned.

column3: Language: 学语言 "study languages", 语言学 "linguistics". 语 ("speech") plus 言 ("words"). Specific languages have their own names, such as 汉语 and 英语.
column7: I like learning languages.
column9: Language: 學語言 "study languages", 語言學 "linguistics". 語 ("speech") plus 言 ("words"). Specific languages have their own names, such as 漢語 and 英語.

column3: Dialogue, conversation: a text of two speakers in a language book (读对话 "read the dialogue"), or a talk between sides. 对 ("facing") plus 话 ("speech").
column7: Please read this dialogue.
column9: Dialogue, conversation: a text of two speakers in a language book (讀對話 "read the dialogue"), or a talk between sides. 對 ("facing") plus 話 ("speech").

column3: Speak, tell, explain: 讲故事 "tell a story", 讲课 "give a lesson", 讲道理 "reason with someone". It puts weight on telling or explaining, where 说 is simply "say".
column7: The teacher is telling a story.
column9: Speak, tell, explain: 講故事 "tell a story", 講課 "give a lesson", 講道理 "reason with someone". It puts weight on telling or explaining, where 說 is simply "say".

column3: Speak, give a talk: a verb and its object, 讲 ("speak") plus 话. 他在讲话 "he is speaking" in front of people. It is also the noun "a speech": 重要讲话.
column7: He is speaking on the stage.
column9: Speak, give a talk: a verb and its object, 講 ("speak") plus 話. 他在講話 "he is speaking" in front of people. It is also the noun "a speech": 重要講話.

column3: Listen to a lecture, pay attention in class: 听 ("listen") plus 讲 ("lecture"). A teacher says 认真听讲 "listen carefully".
column7: Everyone, please listen carefully.
column9: Listen to a lecture, pay attention in class: 聽 ("listen") plus 講 ("lecture"). A teacher says 認真聽講 "listen carefully".

column3: I hear that…, "it is said that…": 听说 + the news: 听说他回国了. It starts a sentence. The same two characters also appear as "listening and speaking" in 听说读写.
column7: I hear it will snow tomorrow.
column9: I hear that…, "it is said that…": 聽說 + the news: 聽說他回國了. It starts a sentence. The same two characters also appear as "listening and speaking" in 聽說讀寫.

column3: As a verb it explains a matter or gives directions, and also shows or proves: 这说明他很努力 "this shows he works hard". As a noun it is instructions, in 说明书 "manual" and 使用说明. 解释 explains a reason or meaning.
column7: Please explain it.
column9: As a verb it explains a matter or gives directions, and also shows or proves: 這說明他很努力 "this shows he works hard". As a noun it is instructions, in 說明書 "manual" and 使用說明. 解釋 explains a reason or meaning.

column3: Meaning: 什么意思 "what does it mean?" It has a second sense, "a gesture, a small token": 一点意思 "a little something". Said yìsi with a light 思. 意思 also appears in 不好意思 and 有意思.
column6: Nǐ shuō de shì shénme yìsi?
column7: What do you mean by that?
column9: Meaning: 什麼意思 "what does it mean?" It has a second sense, "a gesture, a small token": 一點意思 "a little something". Said yìsi with a light 思. 意思 also appears in 不好意思 and 有意思.

column3: Interesting, fun: 有 ("have") plus 意思. 很有意思 says a book, film or person is interesting. The opposite is 没意思 "boring, dull".
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: This book is very interesting.
column9: Interesting, fun: 有 ("have") plus 意思. 很有意思 says a book, film or person is interesting. The opposite is 沒意思 "boring, dull".

column3: Opinion, view, and "objection" in 有意见. 你有什么意见？ asks for an opinion. 提意见 is to give suggestions or complaints. 见 is read jiàn.
column7: What is your opinion?
column9: Opinion, view, and "objection" in 有意見. 你有什麼意見？ asks for an opinion. 提意見 is to give suggestions or complaints. 見 is read jiàn.

column3: Express, show, and "indicate": 表示感谢 "express thanks", 表示同意 "show agreement". It is somewhat formal. 表 ("outer") plus 示 ("show").
column7: He said he agrees.
column9: Express, show, and "indicate": 表示感謝 "express thanks", 表示同意 "show agreement". It is somewhat formal. 表 ("outer") plus 示 ("show").

column3: Table, form, chart: 填表 "fill in a form", 时间表 "timetable". 课程表 is a class schedule, and 价格表 a price list.
column7: Please fill in this form.
column9: Table, form, chart: 填表 "fill in a form", 時間表 "timetable". 課程表 is a class schedule, and 價格表 a price list.

column3: Lamp, light: 开灯 "turn on the light", 关灯 "turn it off". Also in 红绿灯 "traffic light". 灯 has 火 ("fire") and 丁 (dīng).
column7: Please turn off the light.
column9: Lamp, light: 開燈 "turn on the light", 關燈 "turn it off". Also in 紅綠燈 "traffic light". 燈 has 火 ("fire") and 登 as the sound part, which gives dēng.

column3: Chair: 一把椅子. Measure word 把, which is also used for things with a handle. The 子 is light: yǐzi. 椅 has 木 ("wood") on the left and 奇 as the sound part.
column7: Please sit on the chair.
column9: Chair: 一把椅子. Measure word 把, which is also used for things with a handle. The 子 is light: yǐzi. 椅 has 木 ("wood") on the left and 奇 as the sound part.

column3: The wall of a house, courtyard or city (城墙). 墙壁 adds 壁 and stresses the wall as a surface inside. Online, 翻墙 is slang for getting past the Great Firewall, from climbing over a wall.
column6: Qiáng shang yǒu yī zhāng dìtú.
column7: There is a map on the wall.
column9: The wall of a house, courtyard or city (城牆). 牆壁 adds 壁 and stresses the wall as a surface inside. Online, 翻牆 is slang for getting past the Great Firewall, from climbing over a wall.

column3: Main gate, front door: 大 ("big") plus 门. It is the gate of a school, a compound or a building. The door of a room is just 门.
column7: The school gate is closed.
column9: Main gate, front door: 大 ("big") plus 門. It is the gate of a school, a compound or a building. The door of a room is just 門.

column3: Washing machine: 洗衣 ("wash clothes") plus 机 ("machine"). The pattern 洗衣机 is the same as 打印机 "printer" and 手机 "mobile phone". 机 is "machine".
column7: The washing machine is broken.
column9: Washing machine: 洗衣 ("wash clothes") plus 機 ("machine"). The pattern 洗衣機 is the same as 打印機 "printer" and 手機 "mobile phone". 機 is "machine".

column3: Paper: 一张纸 "a sheet of paper". 张 is the measure word. 纸 has 纟 ("silk") on the left. 纸 appears in 报纸 "newspaper" too.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī zhāng zhǐ.
column7: Please give me a sheet of paper.
column9: Paper: 一張紙 "a sheet of paper". 張 is the measure word. 紙 has 糹 ("silk") on the left. 紙 appears in 報紙 "newspaper" too.

column3: Wristwatch: 手 ("hand") plus 表 ("watch"). Measure word: 块 or 只. 戴手表 "wear a watch". A clock is 钟, as in 闹钟 "alarm clock".
column7: His watch is expensive.
column9: Wristwatch: 手 ("hand") plus 錶 ("watch"). Measure word: 塊 or 隻. 戴手錶 "wear a watch". A clock is 鐘, as in 鬧鐘 "alarm clock".

column3: Shoe, shoes: 一双鞋 "a pair of shoes", with 双 as the measure word. The 革 ("leather") on the left shows the material. 穿鞋 "put on shoes", 脱鞋 "take off shoes".
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī shuāng xīn xié.
column7: I'd like to buy a new pair of shoes.
column9: Shoe, shoes: 一雙鞋 "a pair of shoes", with 雙 as the measure word. The 革 ("leather") on the left shows the material. 穿鞋 "put on shoes", 脫鞋 "take off shoes".

column3: Overcoat: 大 ("big") plus 衣 ("clothing"), a long, warm coat. 穿大衣 "wear a coat". Measure word: 件.
column7: It's cold outside, put on a coat.
column9: Overcoat: 大 ("big") plus 衣 ("clothing"), a long, warm coat. 穿大衣 "wear a coat". Measure word: 件.

column3: Comes with 送 (give) or 收到 (receive), and the occasion goes first: 生日礼物, 圣诞礼物. Count with 个 or 份, or 件 for one item. 送礼 without 物 is gift-giving as a custom, often for favors or business.
column6: Zhè shì gěi nǐ de lǐwù.
column7: This is a present for you.
column9: Comes with 送 (give) or 收到 (receive), and the occasion goes first: 生日禮物, 聖誕禮物. Count with 個 or 份, or 件 for one item. 送禮 without 物 is gift-giving as a custom, often for favors or business.

column3: Computer, the formal name, from 计算 ("calculate") plus 机 ("machine"). In daily talk 电脑 is the usual word. 计算机 also names the subject: 计算机专业.
column7: He is studying computer science.
column9: Computer, the formal name, from 計算 ("calculate") plus 機 ("machine"). In daily talk 電腦 is the usual word. 計算機 also names the subject: 計算機專業.

column3: Camera: 相机 is short for 照相机. 用相机照相 "take pictures with a camera". 机 is "machine". The 相 is read xiàng here, "image", and xiāng in 相信.
column7: I take photos with a camera.
column9: Camera: 相機 is short for 照相機. 用相機照相 "take pictures with a camera". 機 is "machine". The 相 is read xiàng here, "image", and xiāng in 相信.

column3: Housing, living space: 住 ("live") plus 房 ("house"). It is the dwelling as a thing: 住房问题 "the housing problem". 房子 is the building itself.
column7: Their living space is very small.
column9: Housing, living space: 住 ("live") plus 房 ("house"). It is the dwelling as a thing: 住房問題 "the housing problem". 房子 is the building itself.

column3: Card: 银行卡 "bank card", 信用卡 "credit card", 电话卡 "phone card". Counted with 张.
column7: I forgot to bring my bank card.
column9: Card: 銀行卡 "bank card", 信用卡 "credit card", 電話卡 "phone card". Counted with 張.

column3: Pack, load, put into: 装进包里 "put in the bag", 装满 "fill up". It also means "install" and "dress up" in some words. 衣 ("clothes") is the meaning part at the bottom.
column6: Tā bǎ shū zhuāng jìn bāo lǐ.
column7: She put the books into her bag.
column9: Pack, load, put into: 裝進包裡 "put in the bag", 裝滿 "fill up". It also means "install" and "dress up" in some words. 衣 ("clothes") is the meaning part at the bottom.

column3: Bring, take along, for things and people: 带手机 "bring a phone", 带孩子 "take the child". It carries along with you; with a direction, 带来 and 带去. Also "belt, zone".
column7: Don't forget to bring your phone.
column9: Bring, take along, for things and people: 帶手機 "bring a phone", 帶孩子 "take the child". It carries along with you; with a direction, 帶來 and 帶去. Also "belt, zone".

column3: Bring (here): 带 plus 来 gives direction toward the speaker. 带来礼物 "bring a gift". It can also mean "bring about, lead to": 带来快乐.
column7: Thank you for the gift you brought.
column9: Bring (here): 帶 plus 來 gives direction toward the speaker. 帶來禮物 "bring a gift". It can also mean "bring about, lead to": 帶來快樂.

column3: A specific seat on a bus, in a classroom or at a table: 占座位 "save a seat", 座位号 the seat number, 给老人让座 "give up your seat". 位子 is the spoken near-synonym. 座 is literally "that which is sat on", from 坐.
column7: Is there a seat here?
column9: A specific seat on a bus, in a classroom or at a table: 佔座位 "save a seat", 座位號 the seat number, 給老人讓座 "give up your seat". 位子 is the spoken near-synonym. 座 is literally "that which is sat on", from 坐.

column3: Vehicles, as a group: 车 ("vehicle") plus 辆, the measure word for vehicles. 辆 follows the number: 一辆车.
column7: There are many vehicles on the road.
column9: Vehicles, as a group: 車 ("vehicle") plus 輛, the measure word for vehicles. 輛 follows the number: 一輛車.

column3: Bus: 公共 ("public") plus 汽车 ("car"). 坐公共汽车 "take a bus". The short form is 公交车.
column7: I take the bus to school.
column9: Bus: 公共 ("public") plus 汽車 ("car"). 坐公共汽車 "take a bus". The short form is 公交車.

column3: Bus, the shorter word, from 公交 ("public transport") plus 车. 坐公交车 "take a bus". Both 公共汽车 and 公交车 are common.
column7: I take the bus to work every day.
column9: Bus, the shorter word, from 公交 ("public transport") plus 車. 坐公交車 "take a bus". Both 公共汽車 and 公交車 are common.

column3: Bicycle: 自行 ("by itself") plus 车. You ride it with 骑: 骑自行车. Measure word: 辆.
column7: I ride a bike to school.
column9: Bicycle: 自行 ("by itself") plus 車. You ride it with 騎: 騎自行車. Measure word: 輛.

column3: Taxi: 出租 ("rent out") plus 车. 坐出租车 "take a taxi". The spoken way to say it is 打车.
column7: Let's take a taxi.
column9: Taxi: 出租 ("rent out") plus 車. 坐出租車 "take a taxi". The spoken way to say it is 打車.

column3: Rent out (to others): 出 ("out") plus 租. The sign 出租 means "for rent". To rent something yourself, say 租: 租房子.
column7: This apartment is for rent.
column9: Rent out (to others): 出 ("out") plus 租. The sign 出租 means "for rent". To rent something yourself, say 租: 租房子.

column3: Take it with 坐: 坐地铁. Around it are 地铁站 the station and 地铁二号线 line two. 铁 is the iron of railways: 铁路, 高铁 "high-speed rail". The city system in Taiwan is called 捷运.
column7: Taking the subway is faster.
column9: Take it with 坐: 坐地鐵. Around it are 地鐵站 the station and 地鐵二號線 line two. 鐵 is the iron of railways: 鐵路, 高鐵 "high-speed rail". The city system in Taiwan is called 捷運.

column3: Subway station: 地铁 plus 站 ("station, stop"). 站 means "stand" and "station". 站 is also in 车站.
column7: Where is the subway station?
column9: Subway station: 地鐵 plus 站 ("station, stop"). 站 means "stand" and "station". 站 is also in 車站.

column3: Boat, ship: 坐船 "go by boat". Measure word: 条 or 艘. The 舟 ("boat") on the left is the meaning part.
column7: We cross the river by boat.
column9: Boat, ship: 坐船 "go by boat". Measure word: 條 or 艘. The 舟 ("boat") on the left is the meaning part.

column3: Ride something you sit astride: a bicycle, a horse or a motorbike: 骑马, 骑车. For a bus or a train, use 坐, and for driving a car, use 开.
column7: He can ride a horse.
column9: Ride something you sit astride: a bicycle, a horse or a motorbike: 騎馬, 騎車. For a bus or a train, use 坐, and for driving a car, use 開.

column3: Ride a bicycle: 骑 ("ride") plus 车, a verb and its object. It is used for bicycles and motorbikes. 骑车去上班 "ride to work".
column7: I ride to work.
column9: Ride a bicycle: 騎 ("ride") plus 車, a verb and its object. It is used for bicycles and motorbikes. 騎車去上班 "ride to work".

column3: Stop: 雨停了 "the rain has stopped", and "park". It can be used for things that move: 车停了. With 在 it gives a place: 停在门口 "park at the door". 亻 ("person") is on the left.
column7: The rain has already stopped.
column9: Stop: 雨停了 "the rain has stopped", and "park". It can be used for things that move: 車停了. With 在 it gives a place: 停在門口 "park at the door". 亻 ("person") is on the left.

column3: Park a car, or "stop the vehicle": verb and object, 停 plus 车. 停车场 is a car park. A sign says 禁止停车 "no parking".
column7: You can't park here.
column9: Park a car, or "stop the vehicle": verb and object, 停 plus 車. 停車場 is a car park. A sign says 禁止停車 "no parking".

column3: Parking lot, car park: 停车 ("park") plus 场 ("place, field"). 场 turns up in other open places: 体育场, 机场. 停车场 may be outdoors or underground.
column7: Where is the parking lot?
column9: Parking lot, car park: 停車 ("park") plus 場 ("place, field"). 場 turns up in other open places: 體育場, 機場. 停車場 may be outdoors or underground.

column3: Someone who drives for a living: 出租车司机, 公交车司机, 卡车司机, and the hired driver of a private car. On the mainland a taxi driver is also called 师傅 to his face. 机 is the "machine" syllable: 飞机, 手机, 洗衣机.
column7: The driver is waiting for us.
column9: Someone who drives for a living: 出租車司機, 公交車司機, 卡車司機, and the hired driver of a private car. On the mainland a taxi driver is also called 師傅 to his face. 機 is the "machine" syllable: 飛機, 手機, 洗衣機.

column3: Traffic, transport: 交通很方便 "transport is convenient", 交通事故 "traffic accident". It covers roads, buses, trains and so on, as a system. Here 交 means "cross, link".
column7: Transport is very convenient here.
column9: Traffic, transport: 交通很方便 "transport is convenient", 交通事故 "traffic accident". It covers roads, buses, trains and so on, as a system. Here 交 means "cross, link".

column3: Highway, road for vehicles, especially between towns: 公 ("public") plus 路. 高速公路 is an expressway.
column7: This road is very long.
column9: Highway, road for vehicles, especially between towns: 公 ("public") plus 路. 高速公路 is an expressway.

column3: Road, path: a more formal and general word than 路. 道路 can be a real road and also a figurative path: 人生的道路 "the path of life". Counted with 条.
column7: There are trees on both sides of the road.
column9: Road, path: a more formal and general word than 路. 道路 can be a real road and also a figurative path: 人生的道路 "the path of life". Counted with 條.

column3: Roadside: 路 ("road") plus 边 ("side"). 在路边 "at the roadside", 路边的店 "a roadside shop".
column6: Tā bǎ chē tíng zài lùbiān.
column7: He parked the car by the roadside.
column9: Roadside: 路 ("road") plus 邊 ("side"). 在路邊 "at the roadside", 路邊的店 "a roadside shop".

column3: Ask the way, a verb and its object: 问 ("ask") plus 路 ("road"). 向…问路 "ask someone the way". You can also say 问一下路.
column7: He asked me the way.
column9: Ask the way, a verb and its object: 問 ("ask") plus 路 ("road"). 向…問路 "ask someone the way". You can also say 問一下路.

column3: Take off of a plane: 起 ("rise") plus 飞 ("fly"). Its opposite is 降落 "land". The subject is the plane: 飞机起飞. Times go before it.
column7: The plane takes off at ten.
column9: Take off of a plane: 起 ("rise") plus 飛 ("fly"). Its opposite is 降落 "land". The subject is the plane: 飛機起飛. Times go before it.

column3: The north, and "the northern part" of a country: 北方人 "a northerner". 北 ("north") plus 方 ("direction, region").
column7: Winter in the north is cold.
column9: The north, and "the northern part" of a country: 北方人 "a northerner". 北 ("north") plus 方 ("direction, region").

column3: The south, and "the southern part" of a country: 南方人 "a southerner". 南方 is a region, while 南边 is the south side of something, near or not: 我家南边有一个超市.
column7: I am from the south.
column9: The south, and "the southern part" of a country: 南方人 "a southerner". 南方 is a region, while 南邊 is the south side of something, near or not: 我家南邊有一個超市.

column3: The East as a region, culture or people, against 西方: 东方文化, 东方人. For a plain direction in daily talk use 东边, as in 学校在东边. 东 also means the host, who sits on the east side of the guest, and a landlord.
column7: I like Eastern culture.
column9: The East as a region, culture or people, against 西方: 東方文化, 東方人. For a plain direction in daily talk use 東邊, as in 學校在東邊. 東 also means the host, who sits on the east side of the guest, and a landlord.

column3: The West, meaning Western countries, as against 东方: 西方国家 "Western countries". It is also the direction "west". Compare 西边, "the west side".
column6: Tā qù guo hěn duō xīfāng guójiā.
column7: He has been to many Western countries.
column9: The West, meaning Western countries, as against 東方: 西方國家 "Western countries". It is also the direction "west". Compare 西邊, "the west side".

column3: Northeast, and the Northeast of China (东北). In Chinese the combined direction puts 东 or 西 first, then 北 or 南: 东北, 东南, 西北, 西南, the reverse of English "north-east".
column7: Winters in the northeast are cold.
column9: Northeast, and the Northeast of China (東北). In Chinese the combined direction puts 東 or 西 first, then 北 or 南: 東北, 東南, 西北, 西南, the reverse of English "north-east".

column3: Southeast: 东 first, then 南, the reverse of the English order "south-east". Same pattern as 东北. Used for directions and areas: 城市的东南.
column7: The school is in the southeast of the city.
column9: Southeast: 東 first, then 南, the reverse of the English order "south-east". Same pattern as 東北. Used for directions and areas: 城市的東南.

column3: Northwest: 西 first, then 北. Mind the order, which is the reverse of the English: 西北, not 北西. 西北 also names a region of China.
column7: The weather in the northwest is very dry.
column9: Northwest: 西 first, then 北. Mind the order, which is the reverse of the English: 西北, not 北西. 西北 also names a region of China.

column3: Southwest: 西 first, then 南, like 西北. 西南 also names a region of China. 中国的西南 "southwest China".
column6: Zhōngguó de xīnán yǒu hěn duō shān.
column7: There are many mountains in southwest China.
column9: Southwest: 西 first, then 南, like 西北. 西南 also names a region of China. 中國的西南 "southwest China".

column3: Direction: 方 ("direction") plus 向 ("toward"). 走错方向 "go the wrong way". It is also a figurative aim: 努力的方向 "direction of effort". 方向 is the thing, and 往 or 向 the preposition.
column7: You went the wrong way.
column9: Direction: 方 ("direction") plus 向 ("toward"). 走錯方向 "go the wrong way". It is also a figurative aim: 努力的方向 "direction of effort". 方向 is the thing, and 往 or 向 the preposition.

column3: The side facing you across a gap, a street, a table or a room: 马路对面 "across the street", 对面的人 "the person opposite". The related 面对面 means face to face.
column7: The bank is opposite the school.
column9: The side facing you across a gap, a street, a table or a room: 馬路對面 "across the street", 對面的人 "the person opposite". The related 面對面 means face to face.

column3: In front of, mostly with a person: 在他面前 "in front of him". 面前 describes what is before someone's eyes, and not a place far off. Used for figurative situations too: 困难面前 "in the face of difficulty".
column7: He stands in front of me.
column9: In front of, mostly with a person: 在他面前 "in front of him". 面前 describes what is before someone's eyes, and not a place far off. Used for figurative situations too: 困難面前 "in the face of difficulty".

column3: Inside, the spoken word: 里 ("inside") plus a light 头, lǐtou. 里头 is like 里面 and often a bit more colloquial.
column7: There is somebody inside the room.
column9: Inside, the spoken word: 裡 ("inside") plus a light 頭, lǐtou. 裡頭 is like 裡面 and often a bit more colloquial.

column3: A light suffix on words of direction and place: 前头 "in front", 里头 "inside", 上头 "above". Said tou, light and with no tone. It is the same character as 头 "head" in 头发 (tóu), but a different, light use.
column7: There is a bank up ahead.
column9: A light suffix on words of direction and place: 前頭 "in front", 裡頭 "inside", 上頭 "above". Said tou, light and with no tone. It is the same character as 頭 "head" in 頭髮 (tóu), but a different, light use.

column3: A word-ending of direction words, as in 东边 "east side", 左边 "left side" and 旁边 "next to". Here 边 is read with the first tone, biān, in this entry. It may also stand on its own: 边…边… "while…".
column7: The book is to the left of the table.
column9: A word-ending of direction words, as in 東邊 "east side", 左邊 "left side" and 旁邊 "next to". Here 邊 is read with the first tone, biān, in this entry. It may also stand on its own: 邊…邊… "while…".

column3: Side, surface in 上面 and 外面, and a measure word for meetings: 见一面 "meet once". 前面 is "in front", 后面 is "behind" and 里面 is "inside".
column6: Wǒ jiàn guo tā yī miàn.
column7: I have met him once.
column9: Side, surface in 上面 and 外面, and a measure word for meetings: 見一面 "meet once". 前面 is "in front", 後面 is "behind" and 裡面 is "inside".

column3: Toward, to, before a verb of movement: 往前走 "go forward", 往左拐 "turn left". The direction goes after 往. It shows where you head. Compare 向, which can also be followed by a person.
column7: Please go straight ahead.
column9: Toward, to, before a verb of movement: 往前走 "go forward", 往左拐 "turn left". The direction goes after 往. It shows where you head. Compare 向, which can also be followed by a person.

column3: Toward and "from": 向前走 is "go forward", and 向你学习 "learn from you". With a person it means "to, from", as in 向他问好. Unlike 往, it can lead to a person. Another sense of 向 is "direction", as in 方向.
column7: I want to learn from you.
column9: Toward and "from": 向前走 is "go forward", and 向你學習 "learn from you". With a person it means "to, from", as in 向他問好. Unlike 往, it can lead to a person. Another sense of 向 is "direction", as in 方向.

column3: An adverb, so it sits before the verb or 都是: 到处找 "search everywhere", 到处都是人. It suits searching, wandering and spreading about in many places. 处 is read chù here, meaning place.
column7: There are people everywhere here.
column9: An adverb, so it sits before the verb or 都是: 到處找 "search everywhere", 到處都是人. It suits searching, wandering and spreading about in many places. 處 is read chù here, meaning place.

column3: Walk past, walk by: 走 plus 过. 他从我身边走过 "he walked past me". In this word 过 is read guò with its full tone. The place passed follows 从: 从…走过.
column7: He walked past me.
column9: Walk past, walk by: 走 plus 過. 他從我身邊走過 "he walked past me". In this word 過 is read guò with its full tone. The place passed follows 從: 從…走過.

column3: Walk into: 走 plus 进. 走进教室 "walk into the classroom". The place follows directly, with no 到. The opposite is 走出.
column7: The teacher walks into the classroom.
column9: Walk into: 走 plus 進. 走進教室 "walk into the classroom". The place follows directly, with no 到. The opposite is 走出.

column3: Go away, move aside: 走 plus 开. As a command it is blunt, like "go away": 走开！ Used with 请 it asks someone to step aside.
column7: Please step aside for a moment.
column9: Go away, move aside: 走 plus 開. As a command it is blunt, like "go away": 走開！ Used with 請 it asks someone to step aside.

column3: Stop! or "stand still": 站 plus 住. 住 shows holding firm. 站住！ is what you shout to someone who is running.
column7: Stop! Don't move!
column9: Stop! or "stand still": 站 plus 住. 住 shows holding firm. 站住！ is what you shout to someone who is running.

column3: Put down: 放 plus 下, 把书放下 "put the book down". It can also mean "give up": 放下工作 "put one's work aside".
column7: Please put the book down.
column9: Put down: 放 plus 下, 把書放下 "put the book down". It can also mean "give up": 放下工作 "put one's work aside".

column3: Beside oneself, around one: 身 ("body") plus 边 ("side"). 在我身边 "by my side".
column7: The child is by my side.
column9: Beside oneself, around one: 身 ("body") plus 邊 ("side"). 在我身邊 "by my side".

column3: Travel as a journey of any length: 去旅行, 一个人旅行, and a 旅行社 is a travel agency, a 旅行箱 a suitcase. 旅游 is the pleasure trip and tourism; a business trip is 出差. 旅 shows a flag over two people, meaning a brigade of troops; it also carries the sense of guest and lodging.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan yī ge rén lǚxíng.
column7: I like traveling alone.
column9: Travel as a journey of any length: 去旅行, 一個人旅行, and a 旅行社 is a travel agency, a 旅行箱 a suitcase. 旅遊 is the pleasure trip and tourism; a business trip is 出差. 旅 shows a flag over two people, meaning a brigade of troops; it also carries the sense of guest and lodging.

column3: Travel for pleasure, tourism: 去北京旅游. 旅 ("travel") plus 游 ("tour"). A tour group is 旅游团, and a tourist spot is 旅游景点.
column7: We are going to Beijing on a trip.
column9: Travel for pleasure, tourism: 去北京旅遊. 旅 ("travel") plus 遊 ("tour"). A tour group is 旅遊團, and a tourist spot is 旅遊景點.

column3: Traveler, passenger in the written style of stations and notices: 各位旅客 "dear passengers". 旅 ("travel") plus 客 ("guest"). The 游客 is a tourist.
column7: Attention, all passengers.
column9: Traveler, passenger in the written style of stations and notices: 各位旅客 "dear passengers". 旅 ("travel") plus 客 ("guest"). The 遊客 is a tourist.

column3: Tourist: 游 ("tour") plus 客 ("guest"). 游客很多 "there are many tourists". It names someone on a pleasure trip, as against 旅客, who is simply traveling.
column7: There are many tourists here.
column9: Tourist: 遊 ("tour") plus 客 ("guest"). 遊客很多 "there are many tourists". It names someone on a pleasure trip, as against 旅客, who is simply traveling.

column3: Passport: 护 ("protect") plus 照 ("certificate"). 办护照 "apply for a passport". 出国要带护照 states the rule.
column7: You need a passport to go abroad.
column9: Passport: 護 ("protect") plus 照 ("certificate"). 辦護照 "apply for a passport". 出國要帶護照 states the rule.

column3: Go abroad: 出 ("go out of") plus 国 ("country"), a verb and its object. 出国留学 "go abroad to study". The opposite is 回国 "return to one's country". 出 began as a foot 止 stepping out of a cave 凵.
column7: I want to go abroad to study.
column9: Go abroad: 出 ("go out of") plus 國 ("country"), a verb and its object. 出國留學 "go abroad to study". The opposite is 回國 "return to one's country". 出 began as a foot 止 stepping out of a cave 凵.

column3: Return to one's own country: 回 ("return") plus 国. 他下个月回国 "he goes home next month".
column7: He goes back to his country next month.
column9: Return to one's own country: 回 ("return") plus 國. 他下個月回國 "he goes home next month".

column3: Starts a journey; the origin takes 从 (从北京出发) and the goal 去 or 到. Figuratively 从…出发 is "starting from a standpoint": 从学生的角度出发. Simply leaving the house is 出门. 出 shows a foot stepping out of a cave. The 发 in it began as a picture of a bow firing an arrow.
column7: We set off tomorrow morning.
column9: Starts a journey; the origin takes 從 (從北京出發) and the goal 去 or 到. Figuratively 從…出發 is "starting from a standpoint": 從學生的角度出發. Simply leaving the house is 出門. 出 shows a foot stepping out of a cave. The 發 in it began as a picture of a bow firing an arrow.

column3: Go out of the house: a verb and its object, 出 ("out") plus 门 ("door"). 她已经出门了 "she has already gone out". It can also mean "go on a trip": 出门在外 "away from home".
column7: She has already gone out.
column9: Go out of the house: a verb and its object, 出 ("out") plus 門 ("door"). 她已經出門了 "she has already gone out". It can also mean "go on a trip": 出門在外 "away from home".

column3: International: 国 ("country") plus 际 ("between"). It sits before the noun: 国际机场, 国际电话.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge guójì jīchǎng.
column7: This is an international airport.
column9: International: 國 ("country") plus 際 ("between"). It sits before the noun: 國際機場, 國際電話.

column3: Another place, outside the local area: 外地人 is someone not from here. 外 ("outside") plus 地 ("place"). It means somewhere else in the country, not abroad.
column7: He comes from out of town.
column9: Another place, outside the local area: 外地人 is someone not from here. 外 ("outside") plus 地 ("place"). It means somewhere else in the country, not abroad.

column3: Come from, for origin: 我来自北京 "I come from Beijing". The place follows directly. It is formal; in speech people say 我是北京人 or 我是北京的.
column7: I come from Beijing.
column9: Come from, for origin: 我來自北京 "I come from Beijing". The place follows directly. It is formal; in speech people say 我是北京人 or 我是北京的.

column3: Visit, tour a place to look around, such as a museum or a factory: 参观博物馆. 参 is read cān here. It is not used for visiting a person.
column7: We go to visit the school.
column9: Visit, tour a place to look around, such as a museum or a factory: 參觀博物館. 參 is read cān here. It is not used for visiting a person.

column3: Come over, toward the speaker: 你过来 "come here". 过来 is also a complement showing a direction: 走过来.
column7: Come over here for a moment.
column9: Come over, toward the speaker: 你過來 "come here". 過來 is also a complement showing a direction: 走過來.

column3: Go over to another place, away from the speaker: 我过去看看. The same word can also mean "the past": 过去的事 "past matters". Compare 过来, which is toward the speaker.
column7: I'll go over and take a look.
column9: Go over to another place, away from the speaker: 我過去看看. The same word can also mean "the past": 過去的事 "past matters". Compare 過來, which is toward the speaker.

column3: Gives the distance between two fixed points, in space or time: 学校离家很近, 离春节还有三天. Leaving is 离开, and 从 names where a movement starts. 离 comes from a character that was first a bird, the black-naped oriole, and was borrowed by sound for "depart".
column7: The park isn't far from here.
column9: Gives the distance between two fixed points, in space or time: 學校離家很近, 離春節還有三天. Leaving is 離開, and 從 names where a movement starts. 離 was first a bird, the black-naped oriole, and was borrowed by sound for "depart".

column3: Leave, depart from: 离开北京 "leave Beijing". The place or person left follows. It is a verb of movement, unlike 离, which gives a distance: 北京离天津很近.
column7: He left Beijing yesterday.
column9: Leave, depart from: 離開北京 "leave Beijing". The place or person left follows. It is a verb of movement, unlike 離, which gives a distance: 北京離天津很近.

column3: Exit: 出 ("out") plus 口 ("opening"). Signs say 出口 and the opposite 入口. It can also mean "export", but the first sense is the exit. 口 is "mouth" and "opening".
column7: The exit is over there.
column9: Exit: 出 ("out") plus 口 ("opening"). Signs say 出口 and the opposite 入口. It can also mean "export", but the first sense is the exit. 口 is "mouth" and "opening".

column3: Entrance: 入 ("enter") plus 口 ("opening"). The sign is 入口, opposite 出口. 入 looks like 人 ("person"), but the two are different characters.
column7: The entrance is on this side.
column9: Entrance: 入 ("enter") plus 口 ("opening"). The sign is 入口, opposite 出口. 入 looks like 人 ("person"), but the two are different characters.

column3: Enter, the formal word, taking a place directly: 进入教室 "enter the classroom". 进入 also fits abstract things: 进入新年 "enter the new year". 进 alone is the plain everyday word.
column7: Please enter from here.
column9: Enter, the formal word, taking a place directly: 進入教室 "enter the classroom". 進入 also fits abstract things: 進入新年 "enter the new year". 進 alone is the plain everyday word.

column3: Exceed, overtake: 超过 + number or person. 他超过了我 "he overtook me". 超过十个人 "more than ten people".
column6: Tā de chéngjì chāoguò le wǒ.
column7: His grades are better than mine.
column9: Exceed, overtake: 超過 + number or person. 他超過了我 "he overtook me". 超過十個人 "more than ten people".

column3: Pass through, go past, and "go through" an experience: 经过公园 "pass the park", 经过考试 "go through an exam". The place passed follows it directly. 经 has 纟 ("thread") and means "pass through" in many words.
column6: Wǒ měitiān jīngguò zhè jiā diàn.
column7: I pass this shop every day.
column9: Pass through, go past, and "go through" an experience: 經過公園 "pass the park", 經過考試 "go through an exam". The place passed follows it directly. 經 has 糹 ("thread") and means "pass through" in many words.

column3: Pass through: 火车通过大桥. "Pass" a test or a vote: 通过考试. And "by means of", before a method: 我们是通过网络认识的 "we met through the internet".
column7: He passed the exam.
column9: Pass through: 火車通過大橋. "Pass" a test or a vote: 通過考試. And "by means of", before a method: 我們是通過網絡認識的 "we met through the internet".

column3: Supermarket: 超 ("super") plus 市 ("market"), short for 超级市场. 去超市买菜 "go to the supermarket to buy groceries". 市 on its own is "city" or "market".
column7: I go to the supermarket to buy groceries.
column9: Supermarket: 超 ("super") plus 市 ("market"), short for 超級市場. 去超市買菜 "go to the supermarket to buy groceries". 市 on its own is "city" or "market".

column3: Shop, store: the measure word is 家: 一家店. 店 also ends many words for kinds of shops: 书店 "bookshop", 商店 "store", 饭店. 店 has 广 ("building") on the outside.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn shí diǎn kāimén.
column7: This shop opens at ten.
column9: Shop, store: the measure word is 家: 一家店. 店 also ends many words for kinds of shops: 書店 "bookshop", 商店 "store", 飯店. 店 has 广 ("building") on the outside.

column3: Hotel, although the characters mean "liquor shop": 酒 ("alcohol") plus 店 ("shop"). 住酒店 "stay at a hotel". A 酒店 is usually more upscale than a 宾馆 or a 旅馆.
column6: Wǒmen zhù zài zhè jiā jiǔdiàn.
column7: We are staying at this hotel.
column9: Hotel, although the characters mean "liquor shop": 酒 ("alcohol") plus 店 ("shop"). 住酒店 "stay at a hotel". A 酒店 is usually more upscale than a 賓館 or a 旅館.

column3: Where you 存钱, 取钱 or 开户; a bank card is 银行卡. 去银行办业务 is the phrase for handling business at the counter, and 网上银行 is online banking. 行 is read háng here, meaning a commercial firm; read xíng it means to walk.
column7: What time does the bank open?
column9: Where you 存錢, 取錢 or 開戶; a bank card is 銀行卡. 去銀行辦業務 is the phrase for handling business at the counter, and 網上銀行 is online banking. 行 is read háng here, meaning a commercial firm; read xíng it means to walk.

column3: Bank card, with 卡 ("card"): 银行 plus 卡. Measure word 张: 一张银行卡.
column7: Do you have a bank card?
column9: Bank card, with 卡 ("card"): 銀行 plus 卡. Measure word 張: 一張銀行卡.

column3: Credit card: 信用 ("credit, trust") plus 卡. 可以用信用卡吗？ is a question to ask a shop.
column7: Can I use a credit card?
column9: Credit card: 信用 ("credit, trust") plus 卡. 可以用信用卡嗎？ is a question to ask a shop.

column3: Customer: 顾 ("look after") plus 客 ("guest"). 顾客 is the word used by shops and services. 客 is the same as in 客人.
column6: Diàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō gùkè.
column7: There are many customers in the shop.
column9: Customer: 顧 ("look after") plus 客 ("guest"). 顧客 is the word used by shops and services. 客 is the same as in 客人.

column3: Service, and "serve": 服务员 is a waiter or attendant. 服务很好 "the service is good". 为客人服务 "serve guests".
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de fúwù hěn hǎo.
column7: The service in this shop is very good.
column9: Service, and "serve": 服務員 is a waiter or attendant. 服務很好 "the service is good". 為客人服務 "serve guests".

column3: Cheap, inexpensive: the second syllable is light, piányi. 便 is read pián here, but biàn in 方便. The opposite is 贵. 便宜一点 "a bit cheaper" is what you ask when bargaining.
column7: This piece of clothing is cheap.
column9: Cheap, inexpensive: the second syllable is light, piányi. 便 is read pián here, but biàn in 方便. The opposite is 貴. 便宜一點 "a bit cheaper" is what you ask when bargaining.

column3: Sell. 卖 is 买 ("buy") with 十 on top, so the tone is also different: mài against mǎi. 卖 + thing: 卖水果. 在卖 "selling".
column7: Do they sell fruit here?
column9: Sell. The tone is different from 買 ("buy"): mài against mǎi. 賣 + thing: 賣水果. 在賣 "selling".

column3: It works from either side: a tenant 租 a place, and a landlord can 租 it out too. On a sign, 出租 means 'for rent', and the rent paid is 房租 or 租金.
column4: 我想在学校附近租房子。
column5: 我想在學校附近租房子。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng zài xuéxiào fùjìn zū fángzi.
column7: I want to rent a place near the school.
column9: It works from either side: a tenant 租 a place, and a landlord can 租 it out too. On a sign, 出租 means 'for rent', and the rent paid is 房租 or 租金.

column3: Income: 收 ("take in") plus 入 ("enter"). 他的收入不高 "his income is not high". 月收入 is monthly income. 收入 can also be a verb, "to take in".
column7: His income is not high.
column9: Income: 收 ("take in") plus 入 ("enter"). 他的收入不高 "his income is not high". 月收入 is monthly income. 收入 can also be a verb, "to take in".

column3: Take, fetch, withdraw: 取钱 "withdraw money", 取包裹 "pick up a parcel". The thing taken follows it.
column7: I'm going to the bank to withdraw money.
column9: Take, fetch, withdraw: 取錢 "withdraw money", 取包裹 "pick up a parcel". The thing taken follows it.

column3: Change, exchange: 换钱 "exchange money", 换衣服 "change clothes", 换一个 "swap for another".
column6: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yī jiàn dà de.
column7: I'd like to change it for a bigger one.
column9: Change, exchange: 換錢 "exchange money", 換衣服 "change clothes", 換一個 "swap for another".

column3: Enough: 钱够了 "there is enough money". 够 + adjective gives "enough": 够大 "big enough". 够了 can mean "that's enough!"
column7: Is this money enough?
column9: Enough: 錢夠了 "there is enough money". 夠 + adjective gives "enough": 夠大 "big enough". 夠了 can mean "that's enough!"

column3: Not enough: 不 plus 够. 钱不够 "the money is not enough". After an adjective: 不够大 "not big enough". The tone of 不 is bù in dictionaries.
column7: The money isn't enough, what shall I do?
column9: Not enough: 不 plus 夠. 錢不夠 "the money is not enough". After an adjective: 不夠大 "not big enough". The tone of 不 is bù in dictionaries.

column3: Businessperson, merchant: 商 ("trade") plus 人. 商人 is a person who does business, often one who sells goods. 商 is also in 商店.
column7: He is a businessman.
column9: Businessperson, merchant: 商 ("trade") plus 人. 商人 is a person who does business, often one who sells goods. 商 is also in 商店.

column3: A job title that goes after the surname, so people are addressed as 王经理. It covers the head of a shop, a hotel or a department; 总经理 is the top manager of the whole company.
column7: The manager is not in today.
column9: A job title that goes after the surname, so people are addressed as 王經理. It covers the head of a shop, a hotel or a department; 總經理 is the top manager of the whole company.
