column3: Receive, accept, collect: 收到 "receive", 收钱 "take payment", 收东西 "put things away". 收到 is the most common: 收到信 "got the letter".
column6: Nǐ shōudào wǒ de xìn le ma?
column7: Did you get my letter?
column9: Receive, accept, collect: 收到 "receive", 收錢 "take payment", 收東西 "put things away". 收到 is the most common: 收到信 "got the letter".

column3: Borrow and also "lend". 借你的书 is "borrow your book". To lend, add 给: 借给我 "lend to me". 向 or 跟 introduces the person you borrow from. The context makes clear which.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng jiè nǐ de shū.
column7: I'd like to borrow your book.
column9: Borrow and also "lend". 借你的書 is "borrow your book". To lend, add 給: 借給我 "lend to me". 向 or 跟 introduces the person you borrow from. The context makes clear which.

column3: Square, plaza: 广 ("wide") plus 场 ("place"). 天安门广场 is a well-known one. You are 在广场上, and 广场舞 is the group dancing done in squares.
column6: Guǎngchǎng shang yǒu hěn duō rén.
column7: There are many people on the square.
column9: Square, plaza: 廣 ("wide") plus 場 ("place"). 天安門廣場 is a well-known one. You are 在廣場上, and 廣場舞 is the group dancing done in squares.

column3: Street: a city street, the road with its shops: 大街 "main street", 上街 "go out on the street". 街上 "on the street". 路 is the broader word for a road.
column7: Let's take a walk on the street.
column9: Street: a city street, the road with its shops: 大街 "main street", 上街 "go out on the street". 街上 "on the street". 路 is the broader word for a road.

column3: City as an administrative unit and a place name ending: 北京市, 上海市. 市 also means "market": 超市. 城市 is the general word for a city. 市 is also "municipal": 市中心 "city center".
column7: My home is in Shanghai.
column9: City as an administrative unit and a place name ending: 北京市, 上海市. 市 also means "market": 超市. 城市 is the general word for a city. 市 is also "municipal": 市中心 "city center".

column3: Mayor: 市 ("city") plus 长 ("head"). Read zhǎng. The pattern is the same as 校长, 班长 and 院长.
column7: The mayor is coming to the school today.
column9: Mayor: 市 ("city") plus 長 ("head"). Read zhǎng. The pattern is the same as 校長, 班長 and 院長.

column3: Before, in the past: 以前我住在这里 "I used to live here". After a time, "ago": 三年以前. 以前 can start a sentence. Its opposite is 以后.
column7: I used to live here.
column9: Before, in the past: 以前我住在這裡 "I used to live here". After a time, "ago": 三年以前. 以前 can start a sentence. Its opposite is 以後.

column3: It comes after the event or time it counts from (下课以后, 三年以后), or stands alone for 'later, from now on' (以后再说). Unlike 后来, which only tells a story in the past, 以后 can look ahead; its opposite is 以前. Besides standing for 'after', 后 is an old character of its own, meaning an empress or ruler.
column7: After class we go to eat.
column9: It comes after the event or time it counts from (下課以後, 三年以後), or stands alone for 'later, from now on' (以後再說). Unlike 後來, which only tells a story in the past, 以後 can look ahead; its opposite is 以前. Besides standing for 'after', 後 is an old character of its own, meaning an empress or ruler.

column3: Above, more than: 十岁以上 "ten years and over". 以上 counts the number itself: 十岁以上 includes ten-year-olds. It can also mean "the above". The opposite is 以下.
column6: Shí suì yǐshàng de rén kěyǐ lái.
column7: People aged ten and over can come.
column9: Above, more than: 十歲以上 "ten years and over". 以上 counts the number itself: 十歲以上 includes ten-year-olds. It can also mean "the above". The opposite is 以下.

column3: Below, under: 十度以下 "below ten degrees". 以下 counts the number itself. It can also mean "the following": 以下是… "what follows is…". Its opposite is 以上.
column7: Today it is ten degrees or below.
column9: Below, under: 十度以下 "below ten degrees". 以下 counts the number itself. It can also mean "the following": 以下是… "what follows is…". Its opposite is 以上.

column3: Outside of, apart from: 除了…以外 "apart from…". Often with 都 or 还. It can also mean "beyond" in a place: 城市以外.
column4: 除了我以外，大家都去了。
column5: 除了我以外，大家都去了。
column6: Chúle wǒ yǐwài, dàjiā dōu qù le.
column7: Everyone went except me.
column9: Outside of, apart from: 除了…以外 "apart from…". Often with 都 or 還. It can also mean "beyond" in a place: 城市以外.

column3: From now on, in future: 今 ("now") plus 后 ("after"). Starts a clause about the future. It is more formal than 以后.
column7: From now on I'll come every day.
column9: From now on, in future: 今 ("now") plus 後 ("after"). Starts a clause about the future. It is more formal than 以後.

column3: Afterwards, later: what came after a past event, so only about the past: 后来他去了北京. 以后 is "after" a point in time, past or future: 毕业以后我去了德国, 明年毕业以后我去德国工作.
column7: Later he went to Beijing.
column9: Afterwards, later: what came after a past event, so only about the past: 後來他去了北京. 以後 is "after" a point in time, past or future: 畢業以後我去了德國, 明年畢業以後我去德國工作.

column3: Then, after that, in a sequence of actions: 先…，然后… "first…, then…". 然后 goes at the start of the second step.
column7: First we eat, then we see a film.
column9: Then, after that, in a sequence of actions: 先…，然後… "first…, then…". 然後 goes at the start of the second step.

column3: At that time in the past: 当时我才十岁 "I was only ten then". 当 is read dāng here.
column7: At that time I was only ten.
column9: At that time in the past: 當時我才十歲 "I was only ten then". 當 is read dāng here.

column3: Besides 'at the same time' for two actions (边…边… is the lighter spoken way), it opens a sentence as a link meaning 'also, and moreover': 同时，我们还要注意安全.
column6: Tā tóngshí xué liǎng zhǒng yǔyán.
column7: He studies two languages at the same time.
column9: Besides 'at the same time' for two actions (邊…邊… is the lighter spoken way), it opens a sentence as a link meaning 'also, and moreover': 同時，我們還要注意安全.

column3: Usually, in ordinary times, as against special days or the present moment: 我平时七点起床. It goes before the verb.
column7: Normally I get up at seven.
column9: Usually, in ordinary times, as against special days or the present moment: 我平時七點起床. It goes before the verb.

column3: At that time: 那 ("that") plus 时. Shorter and more written than 那时候. It sets up a past time: 那时我还小.
column7: I was still little then.
column9: At that time: 那 ("that") plus 時. Shorter and more written than 那時候. It sets up a past time: 那時我還小.

column3: At that time, the fuller, spoken form: 那时候我住在上海. Like 那时 but with 候. The light 候 gives nàshíhou.
column7: At that time I lived in Shanghai.
column9: At that time, the fuller, spoken form: 那時候我住在上海. Like 那時 but with 候. The light 候 gives nàshíhou.

column3: At that time, the spoken form with the ending 儿: nàhuìr. 那会儿我还没上学. It is the same as 那时候.
column7: At that time I was not yet in school.
column9: At that time, the spoken form with the ending 兒: nàhuìr. 那會兒我還沒上學. It is the same as 那時候.

column3: At this moment, just then: 这 ("this") plus 时. Often starts a sentence in a story: 这时，电话响了.
column7: Just then, the phone rang.
column9: At this moment, just then: 這 ("this") plus 時. Often starts a sentence in a story: 這時，電話響了.

column3: At this time, the spoken form with 候: 这时候你在做什么？ Same meaning as 这时.
column7: What are you doing at this time?
column9: At this time, the spoken form with 候: 這時候你在做什麼？ Same meaning as 這時.

column3: Links one step to the one just done: 吃完饭，他接着写作业. Before a verb it also means 'go on', as in 接着说 'keep talking', and it can mean 'catch and hold': 接着球. The last syllable is light. 着 began as a corrupted variant of 著, recorded as a popular form (俗字) in the Tang dynasty.
column6: Tā shuō wán, jiēzhe chàng gē.
column7: After he spoke, he went on to sing.
column9: Links one step to the one just done: 吃完飯，他接著寫作業. Before a verb it also means 'go on', as in 接著說 'keep talking', and it can mean 'catch and hold': 接著球. The last syllable is light. 著 began as a corrupted variant of 著, recorded as a popular form (俗字) in the Tang dynasty.

column3: Next, what comes next: 接下来我们做什么？ It starts a sentence and refers to what follows. 接 ("connect") plus 下来 ("on down").
column7: What shall we do next?
column9: Next, what comes next: 接下來我們做什麼？ It starts a sentence and refers to what follows. 接 ("connect") plus 下來 ("on down").

column3: What to do?: the question for a problem. 怎么办？ stands alone as a full sentence. 办 is "handle".
column6: Wǒ wàng le dài qián, zěnmebàn?
column7: I forgot my money, what shall I do?
column9: What to do?: the question for a problem. 怎麼辦？ stands alone as a full sentence. 辦 is "handle".

column3: How about…?, "how is it?": 你的新家怎么样？ Used to ask for an opinion or state. Also 怎么样 at the end of a suggestion: 我们去看电影，怎么样？
column7: How is your new home?
column9: How about…?, "how is it?": 你的新家怎麼樣？ Used to ask for an opinion or state. Also 怎麼樣 at the end of a suggestion: 我們去看電影，怎麼樣？

column3: How, more written than 怎么样: 怎样写 "how to write". It asks the way something is done.
column7: How is this character written?
column9: How, more written than 怎麼樣: 怎樣寫 "how to write". It asks the way something is done.

column3: What kind of: 什么样的人 "what kind of person". It asks for a description. 样 means "kind, shape".
column7: What kind of person do you like?
column9: What kind of: 什麼樣的人 "what kind of person". It asks for a description. 樣 means "kind, shape".

column3: Why: it goes before the verb, in the position of the reason: 你为什么不去？ The answer starts with 因为. 为 is read wèi.
column7: Why aren't you going?
column9: Why: it goes before the verb, in the position of the reason: 你為什麼不去？ The answer starts with 因為. 為 is read wèi.

column3: Used before a person or a purpose (为你高兴, 为了健康), and as 'be, become' in 成为, 认为 and 以为. It is also in 为什么 and 因为. 为 is wèi when it means 'because of, for', and wéi when it means 'to become, to be'.
column7: I'm happy for you.
column9: Used before a person or a purpose (為你高興, 為了健康), and as 'be, become' in 成為, 認為 and 以為. It is also in 為什麼 and 因為. 為 is wèi when it means 'because of, for', and wéi when it means 'to become, to be'.

column3: Like this, so: 这样做 "do it like this", 这样的人 "this kind of person". 就这样吧 "let's leave it at that".
column7: That's it then, goodbye.
column9: Like this, so: 這樣做 "do it like this", 這樣的人 "this kind of person". 就這樣吧 "let's leave it at that".

column3: Like that: 那样做 "do it like that", opposite of 这样. 不要那样做 is "don't do that".
column7: Don't do it like that.
column9: Like that: 那樣做 "do it like that", opposite of 這樣. 不要那樣做 is "don't do that".

column3: The same, equally: 同样的问题 "the same problem", and before a verb or adjective, 同样重要 "just as important". 同 ("same") plus 样 ("kind, appearance").
column7: We have the same problem.
column9: The same, equally: 同樣的問題 "the same problem", and before a verb or adjective, 同樣重要 "just as important". 同 ("same") plus 樣 ("kind, appearance").

column3: It seems, as if: 好像 + clause: 好像要下雨了 "it looks like rain". It states an impression. It is related to 像, "be like".
column7: It looks like it's going to rain.
column9: It seems, as if: 好像 + clause: 好像要下雨了 "it looks like rain". It states an impression. It is related to 像, "be like".

column3: Be like, resemble: 他很像他爸爸 "he looks like his father". It also lists examples: 像苹果、香蕉这样的水果.亻 ("person") is the meaning part and 象 the sound part, and 象 also means "elephant".
column7: He looks a lot like his father.
column9: Be like, resemble: 他很像他爸爸 "he looks like his father". It also lists examples: 像蘋果、香蕉這樣的水果.亻 ("person") is the meaning part and 象 the sound part, and 象 also means "elephant".

column3: Appearance, look, manner: 他笑的样子 "the way he smiles". 看样子 means "by the look of it". The 子 is light: yàngzi. 样 is "kind, shape".
column6: Tā xiào de yàngzi hěn kě'ài.
column7: The way he smiles is very cute.
column9: Appearance, look, manner: 他笑的樣子 "the way he smiles". 看樣子 means "by the look of it". The 子 is light: yàngzi. 樣 is "kind, shape".

column3: Young person, youth in the sense of a young adult, as against 少年: 青年人. 青 means "green, young" here.
column6: Hěn duō qīngnián xǐhuan zhè shǒu gē.
column7: Many young people like this song.
column9: Young person, youth in the sense of a young adult, as against 少年: 青年人. 青 means "green, young" here.

column3: A boy or young person of roughly 12 to 18, a little more literary than 男孩. 青少年 is the wider group of teens and young people in news and policy talk; a 青年 is older. 少 is shào when it means 'young', and shǎo for 'few'.
column4: 那个少年每天早上跑步。
column5: 那個少年每天早上跑步。
column6: Nà ge shàonián měitiān zǎoshang pǎobù.
column7: That boy runs every morning.
column9: A boy or young person of roughly 12 to 18, a little more literary than 男孩. 青少年 is the wider group of teens and young people in news and policy talk; a 青年 is older. 少 is shào when it means 'young', and shǎo for 'few'.

column3: Teenagers, young people: 青年 plus 少年 joined. 青少年 as a group: 青少年要多运动.
column7: Teenagers should exercise more.
column9: Teenagers, young people: 青年 plus 少年 joined. 青少年 as a group: 青少年要多運動.

column3: Middle age: 中 ("middle") plus 年. 中年人 "a middle-aged person". The stages are 少年, 青年, 中年, 老年.
column7: He is a middle-aged man.
column9: Middle age: 中 ("middle") plus 年. 中年人 "a middle-aged person". The stages are 少年, 青年, 中年, 老年.

column3: Old age, the elderly: 老年人 "old people". The last of 少年, 青年, 中年, 老年.
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō lǎonián rén.
column7: There are many old people in the park.
column9: Old age, the elderly: 老年人 "old people". The last of 少年, 青年, 中年, 老年.

column3: Young, for people: 她看起来很年轻 "she looks young". 年轻人 means "young people". It is said of teenagers and adults; for a small child, use 小: 他还小. 年 ("year") plus 轻 ("light").
column7: She looks very young.
column9: Young, for people: 她看起來很年輕 "she looks young". 年輕人 means "young people". It is said of teenagers and adults; for a small child, use 小: 他還小. 年 ("year") plus 輕 ("light").

column3: Be born: 我出生在北京 "I was born in Beijing". 出 ("out") plus 生 ("birth"). It names the event, and the place or year follows. 出生日期 is "date of birth".
column7: I was born in Beijing.
column9: Be born: 我出生在北京 "I was born in Beijing". 出 ("out") plus 生 ("birth"). It names the event, and the place or year follows. 出生日期 is "date of birth".

column3: Give birth to, "be born", "raw", "student" and more. As a verb: 生孩子 "have a baby", 生病 "fall ill", 生气 "get angry". In 学生 it means "student". In 生词 "new word" and 生菜 "lettuce" it means "raw, unfamiliar".
column6: Tā shēng le yī ge nǚ'ér.
column7: She had a daughter.
column9: Give birth to, "be born", "raw", "student" and more. As a verb: 生孩子 "have a baby", 生病 "fall ill", 生氣 "get angry". In 學生 it means "student". In 生詞 "new word" and 生菜 "lettuce" it means "raw, unfamiliar".

column3: Grow and "senior, head", read zhǎng: 孩子长得真快 "the child grows fast". 校长 "principal" and 家长 "parent" use the same 长, meaning "chief, elder". As "long", the same character is read cháng.
column7: The child is growing so fast.
column9: Grow and "senior, head", read zhǎng: 孩子長得真快 "the child grows fast". 校長 "principal" and 家長 "parent" use the same 長, meaning "chief, elder". As "long", the same character is read cháng.

column3: Grow up: 长 ("grow") plus 大. 长大后 "after growing up". 我长大要当医生 "when I grow up I want to be a doctor".
column7: When I grow up I want to be a doctor.
column9: Grow up: 長 ("grow") plus 大. 長大後 "after growing up". 我長大要當醫生 "when I grow up I want to be a doctor".

column3: A whole life: 一 ("one") plus 生 ("life"). 他一生 or 一生都 "all his life".
column6: Tā yīshēng dōu zài xuéxiào gōngzuò.
column7: He worked at the school all his life.
column9: A whole life: 一 ("one") plus 生 ("life"). 他一生 or 一生都 "all his life".

column3: Life in the sense of everyday living, and "to live": 生活很好 "life is good", 在北京生活 "live in Beijing". 住 is only about where you live; 生活 is the whole of daily life.
column6: Wǒ zài Běijīng shēnghuó le wǔ nián.
column7: I have lived in Beijing for five years.
column9: Life in the sense of everyday living, and "to live": 生活很好 "life is good", 在北京生活 "live in Beijing". 住 is only about where you live; 生活 is the whole of daily life.

column3: You 养 whatever you feed and look after over time: pets (养狗), plants (养花), a family (养家), even a habit, with 养成好习惯. 养病 is to rest until you recover.
column6: Tā jiā yǎng le liǎng zhī gǒu.
column7: His family keeps two dogs.
column9: You 養 whatever you feed and look after over time: pets (養狗), plants (養花), a family (養家), even a habit, with 養成好習慣. 養病 is to rest until you recover.

column3: Long, read cháng: 这条河很长 "this river is long". The opposite is 短. This is the same character as zhǎng "grow, head", but pronounced differently. In 长江, the Yangtze, it is cháng too.
column7: This river is very long.
column9: Long, read cháng: 這條河很長 "this river is long". The opposite is 短. This is the same character as zhǎng "grow, head", but pronounced differently. In 長江, the Yangtze, it is cháng too.

column3: Thousand: 三千 "three thousand". With a single thousand, add 一: 一千 "one thousand", not 千 alone. 千 is also in 千克 "kilogram".
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī qiān kuài qián.
column7: I have a thousand yuan.
column9: Thousand: 三千 "three thousand". With a single thousand, add 一: 一千 "one thousand", not 千 alone. 千 is also in 千克 "kilogram".

column3: Ten thousand. Chinese counts in units of 万, not thousands: 十万 is 100,000 and 五十万 is 500,000. So "two million" is 二百万. The next unit up is 亿, a hundred million.
column6: Zhège chéngshì yǒu wǔshí wàn rén.
column7: This city has five hundred thousand people.
column9: Ten thousand. Chinese counts in units of 萬, not thousands: 十萬 is 100,000 and 五十萬 is 500,000. So "two million" is 二百萬. The next unit up is 億, a hundred million.

column3: Hundred million: 一亿 is 100,000,000. Chinese counts 万 (10,000) and 亿 (100,000,000), so ten 亿 is a billion.
column7: China has over a billion people.
column9: Hundred million: 一億 is 100,000,000. Chinese counts 萬 (10,000) and 億 (100,000,000), so ten 億 is a billion.

column3: Kilometer: 公 ("public, metric") plus 里. 里 itself is an old Chinese mile. 三公里 "three kilometers".
column7: The school is three kilometers from here.
column9: Kilometer: 公 ("public, metric") plus 里. 里 itself is an old Chinese mile. 三公里 "three kilometers".

column3: Kilogram: 公 plus 斤. 两公斤 "two kilograms". A 公斤 is two 斤. The form 千克 is the scientific name.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi liǎng gōngjīn píngguǒ.
column7: I'd like to buy two kilos of apples.
column9: Kilogram: 公 plus 斤. 兩公斤 "two kilograms". A 公斤 is two 斤. The form 千克 is the scientific name.

column3: The weight of everyday shopping: fruit, meat and vegetables are priced and asked for by the 斤 (苹果多少钱一斤?), and 半斤 is half of one. 公斤 is the formal kilogram on labels and in news. 斤 began as a picture of an axe.
column7: How much is a jin of apples?
column9: The weight of everyday shopping: fruit, meat and vegetables are priced and asked for by the 斤 (蘋果多少錢一斤?), and 半斤 is half of one. 公斤 is the formal kilogram on labels and in news. 斤 began as a picture of an axe.

column3: Gram: 五百克 "500 grams". 克 follows the number. A 斤 is 500 克.
column7: Please give me 500 grams.
column9: Gram: 五百克 "500 grams". 克 follows the number. A 斤 is 500 克.

column3: Kilogram, the official name of the unit: 千 ("thousand") plus 克 ("gram"). 公斤 is the everyday word. 千克 appears on labels and in science.
column7: This bag weighs five kilograms.
column9: Kilogram, the official name of the unit: 千 ("thousand") plus 克 ("gram"). 公斤 is the everyday word. 千克 appears on labels and in science.

column3: Corner, "horn", and a unit of money, a tenth of a yuan: 五块三角 "5.30 yuan". 角 also means "angle". A tenth of a 块 is a 角, and a tenth of a 角 is a 分. It is read jiǎo in all these. It began as a picture of an animal horn.
column7: This costs 5.30 yuan.
column9: Corner, "horn", and a unit of money, a tenth of a yuan: 五塊三角 "5.30 yuan". 角 also means "angle". A tenth of a 塊 is a 角, and a tenth of a 角 is a 分. It is read jiǎo in all these. It began as a picture of an animal horn.

column3: Degree for temperature and angles: 三十度 "thirty degrees". It follows the number. Read dù.
column7: It is thirty degrees today.
column9: Degree for temperature and angles: 三十度 "thirty degrees". It follows the number. Read dù.

column3: Count, read shǔ: 数一数 "count it up". The same character is read shù in 数字 "number".
column6: Nǐ shǔ yi shǔ yǒu jǐ ge.
column7: Count how many there are.
column9: Count, read shǔ: 數一數 "count it up". The same character is read shù in 數字 "number".

column3: Number, figure: 数 ("number") plus 字 ("character"). 数字 appears in statistics and prices, and means "digital" in 数字化. Here 数 is read shù.
column7: This figure is correct.
column9: Number, figure: 數 ("number") plus 字 ("character"). 數字 appears in statistics and prices, and means "digital" in 數字化. Here 數 is read shù.

column3: Number of people: 人 plus 数. 人数很多 "there are many people".
column6: Jīntiān lái de rénshù hěn duō.
column7: A lot of people came today.
column9: Number of people: 人 plus 數. 人數很多 "there are many people".

column3: For the population of a country, city or village: 人口增加, 人口很多. To count the people at a meeting, in a class or at an event, use 人数 instead.
column6: Zhège chéngshì de rénkǒu hěn duō.
column7: This city has a large population.
column9: For the population of a country, city or village: 人口增加, 人口很多. To count the people at a meeting, in a class or at an event, use 人數 instead.

column3: Altogether, in total: 一共多少钱？ is the question for a total price. It goes before the verb and states a sum: 一共五个人. Dictionaries write yīgòng.
column7: How much is it altogether?
column9: Altogether, in total: 一共多少錢？ is the question for a total price. It goes before the verb and states a sum: 一共五個人. Dictionaries write yīgòng.

column3: Quarter of an hour: 三点一刻 "3:15" and 三点三刻 "3:45". It also means "carve". 刻 is a clock word used with 点. The 刂 ("knife") is the meaning part, and 亥 the sound part.
column6: Xiànzài shì sān diǎn yī kè.
column7: It is a quarter past three.
column9: Quarter of an hour: 三點一刻 "3:15" and 三點三刻 "3:45". It also means "carve". 刻 is a clock word used with 點. The 刂 ("knife") is the meaning part, and 亥 the sound part.

column3: Measure word for portions, copies and jobs: 一份报纸 "a newspaper", 一份工作 "a job", 一份饭 "a meal set". 份 also means "share".
column6: Wǒ zhǎodào le yī fèn gōngzuò.
column7: I found a job.
column9: Measure word for portions, copies and jobs: 一份報紙 "a newspaper", 一份工作 "a job", 一份飯 "a meal set". 份 also means "share".

column3: Measure word for letters: 一封信 "a letter". It also means "to seal": 封上.
column6: Wǒ xiě le yī fēng xìn.
column7: I wrote a letter.
column9: Measure word for letters: 一封信 "a letter". It also means "to seal": 封上.

column3: Measure word for clothes on the upper body, for matters, and for pieces of luggage: 一件衣服, 一件事, 一件行李. For trousers use 条, and for shoes 双.
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī jiàn shì yào shuō.
column7: I have something to say.
column9: Measure word for clothes on the upper body, for matters, and for pieces of luggage: 一件衣服, 一件事, 一件行李. For trousers use 條, and for shoes 雙.

column3: Floor, story and "layer": 五层 "the fifth floor". 一层 is the ground floor in Chinese counting. It follows the number. A building is 楼, and 三层楼 is a three-story building.
column7: I live on the fifth floor.
column9: Floor, story and "layer": 五層 "the fifth floor". 一層 is the ground floor in Chinese counting. It follows the number. A building is 樓, and 三層樓 is a three-story building.

column3: Counts shows and contests: 一场电影, 一场比赛, 一场考试. It is also the 'place' in 机场, 市场 and 操场. 场 is chǎng for a large place or for sporting activities, and cháng for a spell or episode of something.
column4: 我们昨天看了一场电影。
column5: 我們昨天看了一場電影。
column6: Wǒmen zuótiān kàn le yī chǎng diànyǐng.
column7: We watched a movie yesterday.
column9: Counts shows and contests: 一場電影, 一場比賽, 一場考試. It is also the 'place' in 機場, 市場 and 操場. 場 is chǎng for a large place or for sporting activities, and cháng for a spell or episode of something.

column3: Measure word for vehicles: 一辆车 "a car", 两辆自行车 "two bicycles".
column7: There is a car at the door.
column9: Measure word for vehicles: 一輛車 "a car", 兩輛自行車 "two bicycles".

column3: Measure word for long, thin things: 一条路, 一条河, 一条鱼, 一条裤子. Dogs take 条 as well as 只.
column6: Wǒ yǎng le yī tiáo gǒu.
column7: I keep a dog.
column9: Measure word for long, thin things: 一條路, 一條河, 一條魚, 一條褲子. Dogs take 條 as well as 隻.

column3: Measure word for a set or a suit: 一套房子 "an apartment", 一套衣服 "an outfit". 套 also means "cover".
column6: Wǒmen zū le yī tào fángzi.
column7: We rented an apartment.
column9: Measure word for a set or a suit: 一套房子 "an apartment", 一套衣服 "an outfit". 套 also means "cover".

column3: Measure word for large, fixed things: 一座山 "a mountain", 一座桥 "a bridge", 一座城市 "a city". The same character is in 座位 "seat".
column7: That mountain is very high.
column9: Measure word for large, fixed things: 一座山 "a mountain", 一座橋 "a bridge", 一座城市 "a city". The same character is in 座位 "seat".

column3: The polite measure word for people: 这位是我的老师 "this is my teacher". 一位客人 "a guest". 您几位？ is what a waiter says. It also appears in 座位 and 位子.
column6: Zhè wèi shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
column7: This is my teacher.
column9: The polite measure word for people: 這位是我的老師 "this is my teacher". 一位客人 "a guest". 您幾位？ is what a waiter says. It also appears in 座位 and 位子.

column3: Measure word for a stretch or a section: 一段路 "a stretch of road", 一段时间 "a period of time", 一段话 "a passage".
column6: Wǒmen zǒu le yī duàn lù.
column7: We walked for a stretch.
column9: Measure word for a stretch or a section: 一段路 "a stretch of road", 一段時間 "a period of time", 一段話 "a passage".

column3: Counts an action done through from start to finish: 读一遍, 看一遍. 次 only counts how many times, so 再说一遍 asks for the whole thing again. Before 'a place' it means all over: 走遍中国. It goes back to a root meaning to spread wide and stretch out.
column7: Please say it once more.
column9: Counts an action done through from start to finish: 讀一遍, 看一遍. 次 only counts how many times, so 再說一遍 asks for the whole thing again. Before 'a place' it means all over: 走遍中國. It goes back to a root meaning to spread wide and stretch out.

column3: Measure word for written pieces: 一篇文章 "an article", 一篇作文 "an essay". 篇 has 竹 ("bamboo") on top.
column6: Wǒ xiě le yī piān zuòwén.
column7: I wrote an essay.
column9: Measure word for written pieces: 一篇文章 "an article", 一篇作文 "an essay". 篇 has 竹 ("bamboo") on top.

column3: Slice, flake and a measure word for flat pieces: 一片面包 "a slice of bread", 一片云 "a cloud". 片 also means "film".
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī piàn miànbāo.
column7: Please give me a slice of bread.
column9: Slice, flake and a measure word for flat pieces: 一片面包 "a slice of bread", 一片雲 "a cloud". 片 also means "film".

column3: Name and a measure word for people in a profession: 一名学生 "a student", 一名医生 "a doctor". It is also in 名字 and 姓名.
column7: He is a doctor.
column9: Name and a measure word for people in a profession: 一名學生 "a student", 一名醫生 "a doctor". It is also in 名字 and 姓名.

column3: Row, line, and a measure word for rows: 第一排 "the first row". It is also a verb: 排队 "line up". 扌 ("hand") is the meaning part.
column7: I sit in the first row.
column9: Row, line, and a measure word for rows: 第一排 "the first row". It is also a verb: 排隊 "line up". 扌 ("hand") is the meaning part.

column3: Measure word for questions, dishes, doors and orders: 一道题 "a question", 一道菜 "a dish". Also "way, road", as in 道路.
column7: This dish is delicious.
column9: Measure word for questions, dishes, doors and orders: 一道題 "a question", 一道菜 "a dish". Also "way, road", as in 道路.

column3: Team, line: 他是我们队的 "he is on our team". It is also in 排队 "line up". Also 球队 "ball team" and 队长 "team captain".
column7: He belongs to our team.
column9: Team, line: 他是我們隊的 "he is on our team". It is also in 排隊 "line up". Also 球隊 "ball team" and 隊長 "team captain".

column3: A written, formal 'many' that goes straight before the noun (许多人, 许多问题); speech prefers 很多 or 好多. 许许多多 stresses the quantity even more. One scholar suggests 多 was once two pieces of meat, which meant a lot when meat was scarce.
column7: There are many people in the park.
column9: A written, formal 'many' that goes straight before the noun (許多人, 許多問題); speech prefers 很多 or 好多. 許許多多 stresses the quantity even more. One scholar suggests 多 was once two pieces of meat, which meant a lot when meat was scarce.

column3: Many, lots of, the spoken word: 好多人 "lots of people". With 了 it means "much better": 好多了.
column7: Lots of people came today.
column9: Many, lots of, the spoken word: 好多人 "lots of people". With 了 it means "much better": 好多了.

column3: The majority, most: 大多数人 "most people". 大 ("big") plus 多数 ("the greater number"). It goes before the noun and is followed by 都 or 是.
column7: Most students like this.
column9: The majority, most: 大多數人 "most people". 大 ("big") plus 多數 ("the greater number"). It goes before the noun and is followed by 都 or 是.

column3: The majority, most: 多 ("many") plus 数 ("number"). 多数人 "most people". The opposite is 少数. It is used before a noun: 多数人都同意.
column7: Most people agree.
column9: The majority, most: 多 ("many") plus 數 ("number"). 多數人 "most people". The opposite is 少數. It is used before a noun: 多數人都同意.

column3: A minority, a few: 少 is read shǎo here. 少数民族 are the ethnic minorities of China. 只有少数人 "only a few people". It is the opposite of 多数.
column7: Only a few people know.
column9: A minority, a few: 少 is read shǎo here. 少數民族 are the ethnic minorities of China. 只有少數人 "only a few people". It is the opposite of 多數.

column3: Most of, the greater part: 大部分学生 "most of the students", 大部分时间 "most of the time". The 分 is light: dàbùfen.
column7: Most of the students have come.
column9: Most of, the greater part: 大部分學生 "most of the students", 大部分時間 "most of the time". The 分 is light: dàbùfen.

column3: Part, portion: 这部分 "this part", 一部分 "a part". Said bùfen, with a light 分. It can be a part of a whole, a section of a book, or a share of people.
column7: This part is hard.
column9: Part, portion: 這部分 "this part", 一部分 "a part". Said bùfen, with a light 分. It can be a part of a whole, a section of a book, or a share of people.

column3: A part, some: 一部分人 "some of the people". It names a share that is not the majority. Compare 大部分, which is most. Said yībùfen.
column7: Some people disagree.
column9: A part, some: 一部分人 "some of the people". It names a share that is not the majority. Compare 大部分, which is most. Said yībùfen.

column3: A large amount: 大量的时间 "a large amount of time". It goes before nouns and verbs and sounds formal: 大量生产. 大 plus 量 ("quantity").
column6: Tā kàn le dàliàng de shū.
column7: He has read a large number of books.
column9: A large amount: 大量的時間 "a large amount of time". It goes before nouns and verbs and sounds formal: 大量生產. 大 plus 量 ("quantity").

column3: Says 'a good many' by denying 'few'. It sits before the noun (不少人) or ends a sentence (他买了不少). Do not take it for 'few': 不多 is 'not much, not many'. 不 began as a picture of the calyx of a flower; its meaning 'no' spread back to it from 否.
column7: Quite a lot of people came.
column9: Says 'a good many' by denying 'few'. It sits before the noun (不少人) or ends a sentence (他買了不少). Do not take it for 'few': 不多 is 'not much, not many'. 不 began as a picture of the calyx of a flower; its meaning 'no' spread back to it from 否.

column3: All, the whole: 我全部都买了 "I bought all of it". 全部 is a noun and an adverb.
column7: I bought all of it.
column9: All, the whole: 我全部都買了 "I bought all of it". 全部 is a noun and an adverb.

column3: All the members, the whole body: 全体同学 "all the students". It is a formal word used in announcements.
column7: All students, please stand up.
column9: All the members, the whole body: 全體同學 "all the students". It is a formal word used in announcements.

column3: Whole, all, before a noun: 全班 "the whole class", 全家, 全国, 全年. It can also be an adverb, "completely": 全对 "all correct".
column6: Quán bān tóngxué dōu lái le.
column7: The whole class has come.
column9: Whole, all, before a noun: 全班 "the whole class", 全家, 全國, 全年. It can also be an adverb, "completely": 全對 "all correct".

column3: The whole country, with 全 and 国. 全国各地 "all over the country".
column7: It is snowing all over the country.
column9: The whole country, with 全 and 國. 全國各地 "all over the country".

column3: A tiny bit: 一点 doubled. 我会说一点点 "I can speak a very little". It softens or reduces: 只有一点点.
column7: I can only speak a tiny bit.
column9: A tiny bit: 一點 doubled. 我會說一點點 "I can speak a very little". It softens or reduces: 只有一點點.

column3: All, every: 所有的人 "everyone". It is followed by a noun and often by 都: 所有的人都笑了.
column6: Suǒyǒu de rén dōu xiào le.
column7: Everyone laughed.
column9: All, every: 所有的人 "everyone". It is followed by a noun and often by 都: 所有的人都笑了.

column3: Points back into a group just named: 班上有二十个学生，其中十个是女生. It needs that group in the sentence before, and often leads to 一个, 一些 or 包括. 其 does the same pointing in 其他, 其实 and 其次. 其 began as a picture of a basket, and was later borrowed for a pronoun.
column4: 我有三只猫，其中一只是白色的。
column5: 我有三隻貓，其中一隻是白色的。
column6: Wǒ yǒu sān zhī māo, qízhōng yī zhī shì báisè de.
column7: I have three cats, and one of them is white.
column9: Points back into a group just named: 班上有二十個學生，其中十個是女生. It needs that group in the sentence before, and often leads to 一個, 一些 or 包括. 其 does the same pointing in 其他, 其實 and 其次. 其 began as a picture of a basket, and was later borrowed for a pronoun.

column3: Other, others: 其他人 "the other people", 其他的 "the rest". It is for things and people left out of the group already mentioned. 其 plus 他.
column7: The others have all left.
column9: Other, others: 其他人 "the other people", 其他的 "the rest". It is for things and people left out of the group already mentioned. 其 plus 他.

column3: Almost, about the same: 我们差不多大 "we are about the same age". As an answer to "how is it?", it means "so-so, about right". 差 is read chà here. Said chàbuduō.
column7: We are about the same age.
column9: Almost, about the same: 我們差不多大 "we are about the same age". As an answer to "how is it?", it means "so-so, about right". 差 is read chà here. Said chàbuduō.

column3: Basketball: 篮 ("basket") plus 球 ("ball"). 打篮球 "play basketball". 篮 has 竹 ("bamboo") on top.
column7: He likes playing basketball.
column9: Basketball: 籃 ("basket") plus 球 ("ball"). 打籃球 "play basketball". 籃 has 竹 ("bamboo") on top.

column3: Volleyball: 排 ("row") plus 球. 打排球 "play volleyball". With a hand ball sport you use 打.
column7: Let's play volleyball.
column9: Volleyball: 排 ("row") plus 球. 打排球 "play volleyball". With a hand ball sport you use 打.

column3: Tennis: 网 ("net") plus 球. 打网球 "play tennis". Many ball sports take 打. A tennis court is 网球场, and a racket is 网球拍.
column7: She plays tennis every week.
column9: Tennis: 網 ("net") plus 球. 打網球 "play tennis". Many ball sports take 打. A tennis court is 網球場, and a racket is 網球拍.

column3: Court, field for ball games: 球 ("ball") plus 场 ("field"). 球场上 "on the court".
column6: Qiúchǎng shang yǒu hěn duō rén.
column7: There are many people on the court.
column9: Court, field for ball games: 球 ("ball") plus 場 ("field"). 球場上 "on the court".

column3: A team in a ball sport, like 足球队 or 篮球队; its members, 队员 or 球员, are led by the 队长, and the national team is 国家队.
column6: Wǒmen de qiúduì zuótiān yíng le.
column7: Our team won yesterday.
column9: A team in a ball sport, like 足球隊 or 籃球隊; its members, 隊員 or 球員, are led by the 隊長, and the national team is 國家隊.

column3: Sports shoes, sneakers: 球 plus 鞋. They are shoes for sports. Measure word: 双. 穿球鞋 "wear sneakers".
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī shuāng qiúxié.
column7: I want to buy a pair of sneakers.
column9: Sports shoes, sneakers: 球 plus 鞋. They are shoes for sports. Measure word: 雙. 穿球鞋 "wear sneakers".

column3: Team captain: 队 ("team") plus 长 ("head"), read zhǎng. The same pattern is in 班长 and 组长.
column7: He is our captain.
column9: Team captain: 隊 ("team") plus 長 ("head"), read zhǎng. The same pattern is in 班長 and 組長.

column3: Stand in line, queue: a verb and its object, 排 ("arrange") plus 队 ("line"). 请排队 is what staff say.
column7: Everyone, please line up.
column9: Stand in line, queue: a verb and its object, 排 ("arrange") plus 隊 ("line"). 請排隊 is what staff say.

column3: Exercise, sport, and "to exercise": 多运动 "get more exercise". 运动员 is an athlete.
column7: I exercise every morning.
column9: Exercise, sport, and "to exercise": 多運動 "get more exercise". 運動員 is an athlete.

column3: Activity, event: 一个活动 "an event". 参加活动 "take part in an event". It can also mean "to move about, stretch": 活动活动.
column7: There is an event tomorrow.
column9: Activity, event: 一個活動 "an event". 參加活動 "take part in an event". It can also mean "to move about, stretch": 活動活動.

column3: Take part in, join: 参加比赛 "take part in a match", 参加会议 "attend a meeting". What you join is an event or a group. 参 here is read cān.
column7: Are you taking part in this event?
column9: Take part in, join: 參加比賽 "take part in a match", 參加會議 "attend a meeting". What you join is an event or a group. 參 here is read cān.

column3: Hold an event, formal: 比赛在明天举行 "the match takes place tomorrow". 举 ("lift") plus 行 ("carry out").
column7: The match will be held tomorrow.
column9: Hold an event, formal: 比賽在明天舉行 "the match takes place tomorrow". 舉 ("lift") plus 行 ("carry out").

column3: Raise something up (举手), or bring up as proof (举例子). 举行 holds a ceremony, meeting or match, and 举办 is much the same but stresses the organizer: 学校举办比赛.
column6: Yǒu wèntí de tóngxué qǐng jǔ shǒu.
column7: Students with a question, please raise your hand.
column9: Raise something up (舉手), or bring up as proof (舉例子). 舉行 holds a ceremony, meeting or match, and 舉辦 is much the same but stresses the organizer: 學校舉辦比賽.

column3: Novel, fiction: 看小说 "read novels", 写小说 "write a novel". 小 ("small") plus 说 ("talk"), a "minor talk".
column7: I like reading novels.
column9: Novel, fiction: 看小說 "read novels", 寫小說 "write a novel". 小 ("small") plus 說 ("talk"), a "minor talk".

column3: Story: 讲故事 "tell a story". The 事 is light: gùshi.
column7: He tells the child a story.
column9: Story: 講故事 "tell a story". The 事 is light: gùshi.

column3: Joke: 讲笑话 "tell a joke". 笑话 can also be a verb, "to laugh at someone": 别笑话我. The 话 is light: xiàohua.
column6: Tā jiǎng le yī ge xiàohua.
column7: He told a joke.
column9: Joke: 講笑話 "tell a joke". 笑話 can also be a verb, "to laugh at someone": 別笑話我. The 話 is light: xiàohua.

column3: Joke with the spoken ending 儿: xiàohuar. 讲笑话儿 or 说笑话儿 "tell a joke". It is the same as 笑话.
column6: Nǐ tīng guo zhège xiàohuar ma?
column7: Have you heard this joke?
column9: Joke with the spoken ending 兒: xiàohuar. 講笑話兒 or 說笑話兒 "tell a joke". It is the same as 笑話.

column3: Program, show on television, radio or on stage: 电视节目 "TV program". 节目 can also be an item of a show.
column7: This program is very interesting.
column9: Program, show on television, radio or on stage: 電視節目 "TV program". 節目 can also be an item of a show.

column3: Film, movie: 影 ("shadow, image") plus 片 ("film"). It is more formal than 电影 and fits a particular film. 看影片 "watch a film".
column7: This film is very long.
column9: Film, movie: 影 ("shadow, image") plus 片 ("film"). It is more formal than 電影 and fits a particular film. 看影片 "watch a film".

column3: Goes with 听 and 放 (放音乐 plays it), and builds 音乐会 'concert' and 音乐家 'musician'. 乐 is yuè when it means 'music', and lè when it means 'happy'.
column6: Tā biān zuò zuòyè biān tīng yīnyuè.
column7: He listens to music while doing homework.
column9: Goes with 聽 and 放 (放音樂 plays it), and builds 音樂會 'concert' and 音樂家 'musician'. 樂 is yuè when it means 'music', and lè when it means 'happy'.

column3: Concert: 音乐 plus 会 ("gathering"). 听音乐会 "go to a concert". Counted with 场: 一场音乐会.
column7: Let's go to a concert.
column9: Concert: 音樂 plus 會 ("gathering"). 聽音樂會 "go to a concert". Counted with 場: 一場音樂會.

column3: Photo: 照 ("shine, picture") plus 片. 一张照片 "a photo". 照片 is the picture itself. The act of taking it is 照相 or 拍照.
column7: This photo looks nice.
column9: Photo: 照 ("shine, picture") plus 片. 一張照片 "a photo". 照片 is the picture itself. The act of taking it is 照相 or 拍照.

column3: Take a photo: a verb and its object, 照 plus 相 ("picture"). 照相 splits: 照了一张相. 拍照 means about the same. 相 here is read xiàng.
column7: Let's take a photo together.
column9: Take a photo: a verb and its object, 照 plus 相 ("picture"). 照相 splits: 照了一張相. 拍照 means about the same. 相 here is read xiàng.

column3: Draw, paint, and "a picture": 画画 "draw". 画家 is "painter".
column6: Tā huà le yī zhī māo.
column7: He drew a cat.
column9: Draw, paint, and "a picture": 畫畫 "draw". 畫家 is "painter".

column3: Picture, painting with the spoken ending 儿: 一张画儿. It sounds colloquial.
column6: Qiáng shang yǒu yī zhāng huàr.
column7: There is a painting on the wall.
column9: Picture, painting with the spoken ending 兒: 一張畫兒. It sounds colloquial.

column3: Painter: 画 plus 家 ("expert"). The 家 ending names a skilled person: 作家 "writer", 画家, 科学家.
column7: His father is a painter.
column9: Painter: 畫 plus 家 ("expert"). The 家 ending names a skilled person: 作家 "writer", 畫家, 科學家.

column3: A writer by profession or reputation: novelists, essayists, poets. The author of one given book is the 作者. 家 after a field names an expert: 画家, 科学家, 音乐家. Stories built on the pig in 家 are folk etymologies: the original sound part was a male pig, 𢑓, whose form was later corrupted to 豕.
column7: She wants to become a writer.
column9: A writer by profession or reputation: novelists, essayists, poets. The author of one given book is the 作者. 家 after a field names an expert: 畫家, 科學家, 音樂家. Stories built on the pig in 家 are folk etymologies: the original sound part was a male pig, 𢑓, whose form was later corrupted to 豕.

column3: Picture, image, often one on a screen: 图片 plus a measure like 张. It is the word for pictures in a document or website. Compare 照片 for photos.
column7: Please look at this picture.
column9: Picture, image, often one on a screen: 圖片 plus a measure like 張. It is the word for pictures in a document or website. Compare 照片 for photos.

column3: Letter, and "trust, believe": 写信 "write a letter", 信他 "believe him". 信 as a verb is used for believing a person or his words: 我不信他的话. Counted with 封.
column6: Wǒ bù xìn tā de huà.
column7: I don't believe what he says.
column9: Letter, and "trust, believe": 寫信 "write a letter", 信他 "believe him". 信 as a verb is used for believing a person or his words: 我不信他的話. Counted with 封.

column3: Text message: 短 ("short") plus 信 ("message"). 发短信 "send a text". Measure word: 条.
column6: Wǒ gěi nǐ fā le yī tiáo duǎnxìn.
column7: I sent you a text message.
column9: Text message: 短 ("short") plus 信 ("message"). 發短信 "send a text". Measure word: 條.

column3: Information, message: 收到信息 "get a message". It covers data and also messages in an app.
column6: Wǒ shōudào le tā de xìnxī.
column7: I received his message.
column9: Information, message: 收到信息 "get a message". It covers data and also messages in an app.

column3: Signal: 手机没有信号 "no signal on the phone". 信 plus 号 ("number, mark"). 号 here is read hào.
column7: There is no signal here.
column9: Signal: 手機沒有信號 "no signal on the phone". 信 plus 號 ("number, mark"). 號 here is read hào.

column3: Newspaper: 报 ("report") plus 纸 ("paper"). 看报纸 "read the newspaper". Measure word: 份 or 张.
column7: Dad is reading the newspaper.
column9: Newspaper: 報 ("report") plus 紙 ("paper"). 看報紙 "read the newspaper". Measure word: 份 or 張.

column3: Daily newspaper: 日 ("day") plus 报. It is often part of a newspaper's name.
column7: This is today's daily paper.
column9: Daily newspaper: 日 ("day") plus 報. It is often part of a newspaper's name.

column3: Many city papers carry it in their name (新民晚报). 报 ends names of papers by when they come out: 日报 daily, 早报 morning, 晚报 evening; the paper you hold is 报纸.
column7: Grandpa reads the evening paper every day.
column9: Many city papers carry it in their name (新民晚報). 報 ends names of papers by when they come out: 日報 daily, 早報 morning, 晚報 evening; the paper you hold is 報紙.

column3: News: 看新闻 "watch the news". 新 ("new") plus 闻 ("hear, news"). 新闻 is the news of the media. A single item is 一条新闻.
column7: I watch the news every day.
column9: News: 看新聞 "watch the news". 新 ("new") plus 聞 ("hear, news"). 新聞 is the news of the media. A single item is 一條新聞.

column3: Advertisement: 广 ("wide") plus 告 ("announce"). 电视广告 is a TV advertisement.
column6: Diànshì shang yǒu hěn duō guǎnggào.
column7: There are many ads on TV.
column9: Advertisement: 廣 ("wide") plus 告 ("announce"). 電視廣告 is a TV advertisement.

column3: List of names: 名 ("name") plus 单 ("list"). 在名单上 "on the list".
column6: Wǒ de míngzi zài míngdān shang.
column7: My name is on the list.
column9: List of names: 名 ("name") plus 單 ("list"). 在名單上 "on the list".

column3: Name of a thing, an organization or a place: 名称. It is more formal than 名字, which is used for people and things alike.
column6: Zhège diàn de míngchēng shì shénme?
column7: What is the name of this shop?
column9: Name of a thing, an organization or a place: 名稱. It is more formal than 名字, which is used for people and things alike.

column3: Star in the sense of a famous person: 明星, 电影明星 "film star". 明 ("bright") plus 星 ("star"). The star in the sky is 星星.
column7: He is a film star.
column9: Star in the sense of a famous person: 明星, 電影明星 "film star". 明 ("bright") plus 星 ("star"). The star in the sky is 星星.

column3: Net, web and the internet: 上网 "go online", 网上 "on the internet". 网 began as a picture of a fishing net.
column6: Wǒ zài wǎng shang mǎi dōngxi.
column7: I shop on the internet.
column9: Net, web and the internet: 上網 "go online", 網上 "on the internet". 網 began as a picture of a fishing net.

column3: Website: 网 ("net") plus 站 ("station"). 这个网站 "this website". 站 means "stop, station", and here it is a "site".
column7: This website is very useful.
column9: Website: 網 ("net") plus 站 ("station"). 這個網站 "this website". 站 means "stop, station", and here it is a "site".

column3: For a phone, computer or other device; lights, doors and taps are just 关 (关灯, 关门). The opposite is 开机, and 机 is the same 'machine' as in 手机 and 飞机. 关 comes from a character that began as a door locked with two wooden sticks.
column7: Please switch your phone off.
column9: For a phone, computer or other device; lights, doors and taps are just 關 (關燈, 關門). The opposite is 開機, and 機 is the same 'machine' as in 手機 and 飛機. 關 began as a door locked with two wooden sticks.

column3: Switch on, boot up: 开 ("open") plus 机 ("machine"). The opposite is 关机. 电脑开机 "the computer starts".
column7: The computer is slow to start up.
column9: Switch on, boot up: 開 ("open") plus 機 ("machine"). The opposite is 關機. 電腦開機 "the computer starts".

column3: Healthy, health: 身体健康 "good health", often used in wishes. As an adjective: 健康的生活.
column7: I wish you good health.
column9: Healthy, health: 身體健康 "good health", often used in wishes. As an adjective: 健康的生活.

column3: Medicine: 吃药 "take medicine". 药 has 艹 ("plant") on top. 中药 is Chinese medicine and 西药 is Western medicine.
column7: Have you taken your medicine?
column9: Medicine: 吃藥 "take medicine". 藥 has 艹 ("plant") on top. 中藥 is Chinese medicine and 西藥 is Western medicine.

column3: Pharmacy, drugstore: 药 ("medicine") plus 店 ("shop"). 去药店买药 "go to the pharmacy to buy medicine". Measure word: 家.
column7: The pharmacy is open in the evening too.
column9: Pharmacy, drugstore: 藥 ("medicine") plus 店 ("shop"). 去藥店買藥 "go to the pharmacy to buy medicine". Measure word: 家.

column3: Pill, tablet: 药 ("medicine") plus 片 ("flat piece"). 一片药片 or 两片 "two pills". 药片 is solid and flat, as against 药水.
column6: Zhè zhǒng yàopiàn yī tiān chī liǎng cì.
column7: Take this pill twice a day.
column9: Pill, tablet: 藥 ("medicine") plus 片 ("flat piece"). 一片藥片 or 兩片 "two pills". 藥片 is solid and flat, as against 藥水.

column3: Liquid medicine: 药 ("medicine") plus 水 ("water"), as against 药片. Cough syrup is a typical case. 喝药水 "drink liquid medicine".
column7: The child drank the liquid medicine.
column9: Liquid medicine: 藥 ("medicine") plus 水 ("water"), as against 藥片. Cough syrup is a typical case. 喝藥水 "drink liquid medicine".

column3: It means the kind of medicine and the doctor, and has nothing to do with the doctor's nationality. The pair is 中医 against 西医, and drugs split the same way: 中药 and 西药.
column6: Wǒ gǎnmào le, xiǎng qù kàn xīyī.
column7: I have a cold and want to see a Western-medicine doctor.
column9: It means the kind of medicine and the doctor, and has nothing to do with the doctor's nationality. The pair is 中醫 against 西醫, and drugs split the same way: 中藥 and 西藥.

column3: Traditional Chinese medicine, and its doctor: 中 ("Chinese") plus 医. 看中医 "see a TCM doctor". It is the opposite of 西医.
column7: He is seeing a TCM doctor.
column9: Traditional Chinese medicine, and its doctor: 中 ("Chinese") plus 醫. 看中醫 "see a TCM doctor". It is the opposite of 西醫.

column3: Be admitted to hospital: 住 ("stay") plus 院 ("hospital"), a verb and its object. 他住院了 "he is in hospital". Opposite: 出院.
column7: He fell ill and is in hospital.
column9: Be admitted to hospital: 住 ("stay") plus 院 ("hospital"), a verb and its object. 他住院了 "he is in hospital". Opposite: 出院.

column3: Leave hospital, be discharged: 出 ("out") plus 院. The opposite of 住院. 明天可以出院 "can go home tomorrow".
column7: He can leave the hospital tomorrow.
column9: Leave hospital, be discharged: 出 ("out") plus 院. The opposite of 住院. 明天可以出院 "can go home tomorrow".

column3: Check, examine: 检查身体 "have a physical". 检查作业 "check homework". 检 has 木 ("wood") on the left.
column7: The doctor gives me a check-up.
column9: Check, examine: 檢查身體 "have a physical". 檢查作業 "check homework". 檢 has 木 ("wood") on the left.

column3: Look up, check: 查词典 "look in a dictionary", 查一下 "check quickly". Compare 检查, which examines a thing carefully.
column7: I'll check the map.
column9: Look up, check: 查詞典 "look in a dictionary", 查一下 "check quickly". Compare 檢查, which examines a thing carefully.

column3: Safe, safety: 注意安全 "mind your safety". 这里很安全 "it's safe here". 安 ("peaceful") plus 全 ("whole").
column7: It's safe here.
column9: Safe, safety: 注意安全 "mind your safety". 這裡很安全 "it's safe here". 安 ("peaceful") plus 全 ("whole").

column3: Safe in the sense that no harm came, mostly about a trip or a person: 平安到家, 一路平安, and 报平安 'send word you are fine'. For safe against danger, as in a safe place or food, use 安全. 平安夜 is Christmas Eve.
column7: We got home safe and sound.
column9: Safe in the sense that no harm came, mostly about a trip or a person: 平安到家, 一路平安, and 報平安 'send word you are fine'. For safe against danger, as in a safe place or food, use 安全. 平安夜 is Christmas Eve.

column3: Help, assistance: a verb (帮助别人) and a noun (谢谢你的帮助). More formal than 帮忙.
column7: He often helps me.
column9: Help, assistance: a verb (幫助別人) and a noun (謝謝你的幫助). More formal than 幫忙.

column3: Look after, take care of: 照顾孩子 "look after a child", 照顾病人 "care for a patient". The 顾 is light: zhàogu.
column7: She looks after the child at home.
column9: Look after, take care of: 照顧孩子 "look after a child", 照顧病人 "care for a patient". The 顧 is light: zhàogu.

column3: Pretty, beautiful: 漂亮 is for people, clothes and things. It can also mean "well done", as in 干得漂亮. The 亮 is light: piàoliang. 漂 is read piào here, and piāo in "to float".
column6: Tā de xīn yīfu hěn piàoliang.
column7: Her new clothes are pretty.
column9: Pretty, beautiful: 漂亮 is for people, clothes and things. It can also mean "well done", as in 幹得漂亮. The 亮 is light: piàoliang. 漂 is read piào here, and piāo in "to float".

column3: Low: 气温很低 "the temperature is low". The opposite is 高. For a person's height use 矮.
column7: The temperature is low today.
column9: Low: 氣溫很低 "the temperature is low". The opposite is 高. For a person's height use 矮.

column3: Short, for length and time: 头发很短 "short hair", 时间很短 "a short time". The opposite is 长. For a person's height use 矮.
column7: Her hair is very short.
column9: Short, for length and time: 頭髮很短 "short hair", 時間很短 "a short time". The opposite is 長. For a person's height use 矮.

column3: Light in weight, and "gentle": 这个包很轻. The opposite is 重. 轻轻地 is "softly". 轻松 means "relaxed, easy": 轻松的工作 "an easy job".
column7: This bag is light.
column9: Light in weight, and "gentle": 這個包很輕. The opposite is 重. 輕輕地 is "softly". 輕鬆 means "relaxed, easy": 輕鬆的工作 "an easy job". 輕 began as a light carriage 車.

column3: Bright: 灯很亮 "the light is bright". 天亮了 "it's daylight". It is also in 漂亮 and 月亮.
column7: It is light, time to get up.
column9: Bright: 燈很亮 "the light is bright". 天亮了 "it's daylight". It is also in 漂亮 and 月亮.

column3: The pattern is A 离 B 很近: 离 gives the 'from', and 近 is the adjective. It opens up 附近 'nearby' and 最近 'lately, recently'. Its opposite is 远.
column6: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
column7: My home is close to the school.
column9: The pattern is A 離 B 很近: 離 gives the 'from', and 近 is the adjective. It opens up 附近 'nearby' and 最近 'lately, recently'. Its opposite is 遠.

column3: Flat, level: 这条路很平 "this road is flat". It also means "calm" and "equal": 平等.
column7: This road is flat.
column9: Flat, level: 這條路很平 "this road is flat". It also means "calm" and "equal": 平等.

column3: Full: 车上坐满了人 "the bus is full of people". 满 + 了 follows a verb: 坐满, 装满. Compare 饱, which is "full" from eating. 满 has 氵 ("water").
column6: Chē shang zuò mǎn le rén.
column7: The bus is full of people.
column9: Full: 車上坐滿了人 "the bus is full of people". 滿 + 了 follows a verb: 坐滿, 裝滿. Compare 飽, which is "full" from eating. 滿 has 氵 ("water").

column3: Quiet: 请安静 "please be quiet". 安 ("peaceful") plus 静 ("still").
column7: Please be quiet for a moment.
column9: Quiet: 請安靜 "please be quiet". 安 ("peaceful") plus 靜 ("still").

column3: Convenient: 很方便 "very convenient". It goes with transport and shops: 交通很方便. 方便 can also be a polite way to say "go to the toilet". 方便面 is instant noodles.
column7: It is very convenient to live here.
column9: Convenient: 很方便 "very convenient". It goes with transport and shops: 交通很方便. 方便 can also be a polite way to say "go to the toilet". 方便麵 is instant noodles.

column3: Not bad, pretty good: 不 plus 错 ("wrong"). It is a modest compliment: 这个菜不错. The tone of 不 is bù in dictionaries.
column7: This dish is not bad.
column9: Not bad, pretty good: 不 plus 錯 ("wrong"). It is a modest compliment: 這個菜不錯. The tone of 不 is bù in dictionaries.

column3: Clear, and "to know clearly": 听不清楚 "can't hear clearly", 我不清楚 "I'm not sure". The 楚 is light: qīngchu.
column7: I can't hear clearly.
column9: Clear, and "to know clearly": 聽不清楚 "can't hear clearly", 我不清楚 "I'm not sure". The 楚 is light: qīngchu.

column3: A neutral 'ordinary, regular', said of people and things: 普通人, 普通朋友, 普通票. It is also the 普 of 普通话, the mainland name for Mandarin; in Taiwan people usually say 中文, and 国语 is the official name.
column4: 我只是一个普通的学生。
column5: 我只是一個普通的學生。
column6: Wǒ zhǐ shì yī ge pǔtōng de xuésheng.
column7: I'm just an ordinary student.
column9: A neutral 'ordinary, regular', said of people and things: 普通人, 普通朋友, 普通票. It is also the 普 of 普通話, the mainland name for Mandarin; in Taiwan people usually say 中文, and 國語 is the official name.

column3: Ordinary, and "usually, normally": 我平常不喝咖啡 "I normally don't drink coffee". As an adverb it goes before the verb. 平 plus 常 ("often"). Compare 平时.
column7: I don't normally drink coffee.
column9: Ordinary, and "usually, normally": 我平常不喝咖啡 "I normally don't drink coffee". As an adverb it goes before the verb. 平 plus 常 ("often"). Compare 平時.

column3: Size: 大小 ("big and small") as one noun, as in 大小合适 "the size fits". Two opposites together give a noun for the quality, as in 多少.
column6: Zhè liǎng shuāng xié dàxiǎo yīyàng.
column7: These two pairs of shoes are the same size.
column9: Size: 大小 ("big and small") as one noun, as in 大小合適 "the size fits". Two opposites together give a noun for the quality, as in 多少.

column3: Loudly: 大声 ("big sound") before the verb: 大声说话 "speak loudly". The opposite is 小声. 请大声一点 asks someone to speak up.
column7: Please speak up a bit.
column9: Loudly: 大聲 ("big sound") before the verb: 大聲說話 "speak loudly". The opposite is 小聲. 請大聲一點 asks someone to speak up.

column3: Quietly, in a low voice: 小声 before the verb: 小声说话 "speak softly". The opposite is 大声.
column7: Please speak quietly.
column9: Quietly, in a low voice: 小聲 before the verb: 小聲說話 "speak softly". The opposite is 大聲.

column3: Sound, voice: 声 ("sound") plus 音 ("sound"). 他的声音很好听 "his voice is nice".
column7: His voice is very pleasant.
column9: Sound, voice: 聲 ("sound") plus 音 ("sound"). 他的聲音很好聽 "his voice is nice".

column3: Sound, ring, be loud: 电话响了 "the phone rang". It is also an adjective, "loud". 响 has 口 ("mouth") on the left.
column7: The phone rang.
column9: Sound, ring, be loud: 電話響了 "the phone rang". It is also an adjective, "loud". 響 has 口 ("mouth") on the left.

column3: The loud kind of calling: shouting (喊口号 'chant slogans') or calling someone from a distance, 喊他吃饭. 叫 is the general word for 'call'; 喊 adds volume.
column6: Māma zài lóuxià hǎn nǐ chīfàn.
column7: Mom is calling you from downstairs to eat.
column9: The loud kind of calling: shouting (喊口號 'chant slogans') or calling someone from a distance, 喊他吃飯. 叫 is the general word for 'call'; 喊 adds volume.

column3: Fake, false, read jiǎ: 假的 "a fake". In 假期 "holiday" it is read jià. The opposite of 假 "fake" is 真.
column7: This bag is fake.
column9: Fake, false, read jiǎ: 假的 "a fake". In 假期 "holiday" it is read jià. The opposite of 假 "fake" is 真.

column3: Flow: 河水向东流 "the river flows east". 氵 ("water") is on the left.
column7: The river flows east.
column9: Flow: 河水向東流 "the river flows east". 氵 ("water") is on the left.

column3: Popular, fashionable: 流 ("flow") plus 行 ("go"). 这首歌很流行 "this song is popular".
column6: Zhè shǒu gē xiànzài hěn liúxíng.
column7: This song is popular now.
column9: Popular, fashionable: 流 ("flow") plus 行 ("go"). 這首歌很流行 "this song is popular".

column3: Even more: 今天比昨天更冷 "today is even colder than yesterday". 更 + adjective. It goes with 比 comparisons and also stands alone: 更好. Read gèng here. In 更新 it is read gēng.
column7: Today is even colder than yesterday.
column9: Even more: 今天比昨天更冷 "today is even colder than yesterday". 更 + adjective. It goes with 比 comparisons and also stands alone: 更好. Read gèng here. In 更新 it is read gēng.

column3: Quite, rather, spoken: 挺好的 "quite good". The pattern is 挺 + adjective + 的, with 的 often at the end. It is informal.
column7: This place is quite good.
column9: Quite, rather, spoken: 挺好的 "quite good". The pattern is 挺 + adjective + 的, with 的 often at the end. It is informal.

column3: Pretty good, quite fine: 挺 ("quite") plus 好. As a reply to "how is it?": 挺好 "pretty good". Add 的 for a warm tone: 挺好的.
column7: This way is quite good.
column9: Pretty good, quite fine: 挺 ("quite") plus 好. As a reply to "how is it?": 挺好 "pretty good". Add 的 for a warm tone: 挺好的.

column3: Especially, particularly: 特别冷 "especially cold". It goes before an adjective. It also means "special": 特别的礼物. 特 plus 别.
column7: Today is particularly cold.
column9: Especially, particularly: 特別冷 "especially cold". It goes before an adjective. It also means "special": 特別的禮物. 特 plus 別.

column3: A degree word before an adjective or a feeling verb, a notch stronger and more formal than 很: 十分重要, 十分感谢 'many thanks'. 不十分 softens a negative to 'not quite'.
column7: Many thanks for your help.
column9: A degree word before an adjective or a feeling verb, a notch stronger and more formal than 很: 十分重要, 十分感謝 'many thanks'. 不十分 softens a negative to 'not quite'.

column3: Really, truly: 实在太累了 "I'm really too tired". It goes before the adjective or verb and is stronger than 真. As an adjective it means "honest, solid".
column7: I'm really too tired.
column9: Really, truly: 實在太累了 "I'm really too tired". It goes before the adjective or verb and is stronger than 真. As an adjective it means "honest, solid".

column3: Actual, real: 实际情况 "the actual situation", and 实际上 "in fact, actually".
column6: Tā shíjì shang bù huì kāichē.
column7: In fact, he can't drive.
column9: Actual, real: 實際情況 "the actual situation", and 實際上 "in fact, actually".

column3: Completely, entirely: 完全同意 "completely agree". It goes before the verb.
column7: I fully agree.
column9: Completely, entirely: 完全同意 "completely agree". It goes before the verb.

column3: Greatly: 大 doubled to give an adverb before the verb: 大大提高 "greatly improve". It comes before a verb of change.
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ dàdà tígāo le.
column7: His Chinese has improved a great deal.
column9: Greatly: 大 doubled to give an adverb before the verb: 大大提高 "greatly improve". It comes before a verb of change.

column3: How…! in exclamations: 多么好看啊！ "how beautiful!" It goes before an adjective, usually with 啊 at the end.
column7: How quiet it is here!
column9: How…! in exclamations: 多麼好看啊！ "how beautiful!" It goes before an adjective, usually with 啊 at the end.

column3: So, this much, for something near: 这么大 "this big", 这么早 "so early". It goes before an adjective or verb.
column7: Why are you so early?
column9: So, this much, for something near: 這麼大 "this big", 這麼早 "so early". It goes before an adjective or verb.

column3: So, that much, for something far or earlier: 那么多 "that many". At the start of a clause it means "in that case": 那么我们走吧.
column6: Nàme duō rén, wǒ bù xiǎng qù.
column7: With that many people, I don't want to go.
column9: So, that much, for something far or earlier: 那麼多 "that many". At the start of a clause it means "in that case": 那麼我們走吧.

column3: The more… the more…: 越…越… in a pair. 越吃越多 "the more you eat, the more it is". The pattern joins two verbs or adjectives: 雨越下越大 "the rain gets heavier and heavier". 越 alone only appears in this pattern, most often as 越来越 "more and more" before an adjective: 天气越来越冷.
column7: The rain gets heavier and heavier.
column9: The more… the more…: 越…越… in a pair. 越吃越多 "the more you eat, the more it is". The pattern joins two verbs or adjectives: 雨越下越大 "the rain gets heavier and heavier". 越 alone only appears in this pattern, most often as 越來越 "more and more" before an adjective: 天氣越來越冷.

column3: Describes a change that keeps growing as time passes: 越来越贵, with 了 often at the end. Do not add 很 or 更. For 'the more X, the more Y' use 越…越…: 越多越好.
column7: The weather is getting colder and colder.
column9: Describes a change that keeps growing as time passes: 越來越貴, with 了 often at the end. Do not add 很 or 更. For 'the more X, the more Y' use 越…越…: 越多越好.

column3: A bit, somewhat: 有点儿冷 "a bit cold". It goes before an adjective and is often used for a complaint or something unwanted. After the adjective use 一点儿: 冷一点儿. Said diǎnr.
column7: It is a bit cold today.
column9: A bit, somewhat: 有點兒冷 "a bit cold". It goes before an adjective and is often used for a complaint or something unwanted. After the adjective use 一點兒: 冷一點兒. Said diǎnr.

column3: A bit, the longer form of 有点儿, with 一 inserted. The two mean the same. It goes before an adjective: 有一点儿累. After the adjective, 一点儿 stands alone.
column7: I'm a bit tired.
column9: A bit, the longer form of 有點兒, with 一 inserted. The two mean the same. It goes before an adjective: 有一點兒累. After the adjective, 一點兒 stands alone.

column3: Anew, start again: 重新开始 "start over". 重 is read chóng here, "again", not zhòng "heavy". It goes before the verb. 重新 + verb means doing something over.
column7: I want to start again.
column9: Anew, start again: 重新開始 "start over". 重 is read chóng here, "again", not zhòng "heavy". It goes before the verb. 重新 + verb means doing something over.

column3: Repeat: 请重复一遍 "please repeat". 重 is read chóng. 复 means "again". It fits mistakes and steps too: 重复同样的错误 "repeat the same mistake".
column7: Please repeat it once.
column9: Repeat: 請重複一遍 "please repeat". 重 is read chóng. 複 means "again". It fits mistakes and steps too: 重複同樣的錯誤 "repeat the same mistake".

column3: A long time: 好久不见 "long time no see". 好 here intensifies it. 好久 comes after the verb as a duration: 等了好久 "waited a long time".
column6: Hǎojiǔ bù jiàn, nǐ hǎo ma?
column7: Long time no see, how are you?
column9: A long time: 好久不見 "long time no see". 好 here intensifies it. 好久 comes after the verb as a duration: 等了好久 "waited a long time".

column3: How long: the question for duration. It goes after the verb: 学了多久 "studied for how long".
column7: How long have you studied Chinese?
column9: How long: the question for duration. It goes after the verb: 學了多久 "studied for how long".

column3: Looks at time from a point in a story: 不久以后 'soon after', 不久以前 'not long ago', 不久就 + verb. To say you are coming soon in speech, use 马上 or 很快.
column7: He came back soon after.
column9: Looks at time from a point in a story: 不久以後 'soon after', 不久以前 'not long ago', 不久就 + verb. To say you are coming soon in speech, use 馬上 or 很快.

column3: After a moment, soon: 一会儿 negated, "not even a moment". Often followed by 就: 不一会儿，他就来了.
column7: A moment later he came.
column9: After a moment, soon: 一會兒 negated, "not even a moment". Often followed by 就: 不一會兒，他就來了.

column3: Just (a moment ago): 我刚到家 "I just got home". It goes before the verb. It cannot start the sentence as 刚才 can. 刚 also means "exactly" in 刚好.
column7: I just got home.
column9: Just (a moment ago): 我剛到家 "I just got home". It goes before the verb. It cannot start the sentence as 剛才 can. 剛 also means "exactly" in 剛好.

column3: Just now: 刚才 is a time word, so it can start the sentence or follow the subject. 刚才谁给你打电话？ is a natural question.
column6: Gāngcái shéi gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà?
column7: Who called you just now?
column9: Just now: 剛才 is a time word, so it can start the sentence or follow the subject. 剛才誰給你打電話？ is a natural question.

column3: Just, doubled from 刚, and used in the same way before a verb. 他刚刚走 "he has just left". The second 刚 is light: gānggang.
column7: He has just left.
column9: Just, doubled from 剛, and used in the same way before a verb. 他剛剛走 "he has just left". The second 剛 is light: gānggang.

column3: Long ago, a long time already: 早 ("early") plus 就. 我早就知道了 "I have known it for ages". It shows that something is earlier than expected.
column7: I knew that long ago.
column9: Long ago, a long time already: 早 ("early") plus 就. 我早就知道了 "I have known it for ages". It shows that something is earlier than expected.

column3: Already: 已经 + verb + 了. 我已经吃过了 "I have already eaten". It goes before the verb. 已 differs from 己 (jǐ) only in how the last stroke ends.
column7: I have already eaten.
column9: Already: 已經 + verb + 了. 我已經吃過了 "I have already eaten". It goes before the verb. 已 differs from 己 (jǐ) only in how the last stroke ends.

column3: Does the same job as 常常 and 常, a little more formal; it goes before the verb. 不常 or 不经常 says 'not often', while 常 alone is the shortest: 常去. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment, and was borrowed for 'frequently'.
column6: Wǒ jīngcháng qù nà jiā diàn.
column7: I often go to that shop.
column9: Does the same job as 常常 and 常, a little more formal; it goes before the verb. 不常 or 不經常 says 'not often', while 常 alone is the shortest: 常去. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment, and was borrowed for 'frequently'.

column3: At any time, whenever: 随时 + verb. 你可以随时来 "you can come any time". It goes before the verb.
column6: Yǒu wèntí kěyǐ suíshí wèn wǒ.
column7: If you have a question, ask me any time.
column9: At any time, whenever: 隨時 + verb. 你可以隨時來 "you can come any time". It goes before the verb.

column3: Straight on, "continuously" and "all along": 一直走 "go straight", 一直往前走; 昨天夜里一直下雨 "it rained all last night"; 我一直喜欢中国文化 "I have always liked Chinese culture".
column7: Keep going straight ahead.
column9: Straight on, "continuously" and "all along": 一直走 "go straight", 一直往前走; 昨天夜裡一直下雨 "it rained all last night"; 我一直喜歡中國文化 "I have always liked Chinese culture".

column3: Forever, always: 我永远爱你 "I will always love you". 永 began as a picture of a long river.
column7: I will love you forever.
column9: Forever, always: 我永遠愛你 "I will always love you". 永 began as a picture of a long river.

column3: Always, with a complaint: 老是迟到 "always late". The 是 is light: lǎoshi.
column6: Tā lǎoshi wàng le dài shǒujī.
column7: He always forgets to bring his phone.
column9: Always, with a complaint: 老是遲到 "always late". The 是 is light: lǎoshi.

column3: Again, for a repeat that has already happened: 他昨天又来了 "he came again yesterday". For a repeat in the future, use 再. 又 usually comes with 了, and 再 does not. It can show annoyance: 你又迟到了 "you're late again!" It can also mean "also", as in 又大又好 "both big and good".
column7: He came again yesterday.
column9: Again, for a repeat that has already happened: 他昨天又來了 "he came again yesterday". For a repeat in the future, use 再. 又 usually comes with 了, and 再 does not. It can show annoyance: 你又遲到了 "you're late again!" It can also mean "also", as in 又大又好 "both big and good".

column3: Only then, not until: 他十点才起床 "he doesn't get up until ten". It points to something late or less than expected. 就 shows early or easy, and 才 shows late or hard. 就 usually comes with 了, and 才 does not: 他八点才来. It goes before the verb.
column7: He doesn't get up until ten.
column9: Only then, not until: 他十點才起床 "he doesn't get up until ten". It points to something late or less than expected. 就 shows early or easy, and 才 shows late or hard. 就 usually comes with 了, and 才 does not: 他八點才來. It goes before the verb.

column3: Suddenly: 天忽然下雨了 "it suddenly rained". It goes before the verb.
column7: It suddenly started to rain.
column9: Suddenly: 天忽然下雨了 "it suddenly rained". It goes before the verb.

column3: Recently, lately: 最近你忙吗？ It can start a sentence or follow the subject.
column7: Have you been busy lately?
column9: Recently, lately: 最近你忙嗎？ It can start a sentence or follow the subject.

column3: About to: 快要…了, as in 火车快要开了. It cannot be used with a specific time word. For that use 就要. In speech it is common for being close to a limit: 我快要饿死了 "I'm starving".
column7: The train is about to leave.
column9: About to: 快要…了, as in 火車快要開了. It cannot be used with a specific time word. For that use 就要. In speech it is common for being close to a limit: 我快要餓死了 "I'm starving".

column3: About to, and it can be used with a specific time: 我们明天就要走了 "we leave tomorrow". 就要…了 is the form that works with a time word: 我下个星期就要回国了. It also sounds more urgent than 快要.
column7: We are leaving tomorrow.
column9: About to, and it can be used with a specific time: 我們明天就要走了 "we leave tomorrow". 就要…了 is the form that works with a time word: 我下個星期就要回國了. It also sounds more urgent than 快要.

column3: Hurry up: 快点儿! The 点儿 is a small amount, so literally "a bit faster". It also follows a verb: 走快点儿.
column7: Hurry up, we'll be late.
column9: Hurry up: 快點兒! The 點兒 is a small amount, so literally "a bit faster". It also follows a verb: 走快點兒.

column3: Common, often seen: 常见的鸟 "a common bird". 常 ("often") plus 见 ("see").
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng chángjiàn de niǎo.
column7: This is a common kind of bird.
column9: Common, often seen: 常見的鳥 "a common bird". 常 ("often") plus 見 ("see").

column3: Describes what people reach for often: 常用字, 常用词, 常用语 'everyday phrases'. 常见 is the neighbor for what you often come across, not use. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment, and was borrowed for 'frequently'.
column6: Zhèxiē shì zuì chángyòng de Hànzì.
column7: These are the most commonly used characters.
column9: Describes what people reach for often: 常用字, 常用詞, 常用語 'everyday phrases'. 常見 is the neighbor for what you often come across, not use. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment, and was borrowed for 'frequently'.

column3: Can, may: permission or possibility. 我可以进来吗？ asks permission. It can also mean "not bad": 还可以. Its negative is 不可以 for "not allowed".
column7: May I come in?
column9: Can, may: permission or possibility. 我可以進來嗎？ asks permission. It can also mean "not bad": 還可以. Its negative is 不可以 for "not allowed".

column3: Maybe, possible: 他可能不来 "he may not come". It is an adverb (可能不来), and 有可能 means "it is possible".
column7: He may not come.
column9: Maybe, possible: 他可能不來 "he may not come". It is an adverb (可能不來), and 有可能 means "it is possible".

column3: Be able to, a bit more formal than 能: 能够看懂 "be able to understand". 能够 stresses having the means or the chance.
column6: Wǒ nénggòu kàn dǒng zhè běn shū.
column7: I am able to understand this book.
column9: Be able to, a bit more formal than 能: 能夠看懂 "be able to understand". 能夠 stresses having the means or the chance.

column3: Should, ought to: 你应该多休息 "you should rest more". Its negative is 不应该. 应 is read yīng here.
column7: You should rest more.
column9: Should, ought to: 你應該多休息 "you should rest more". Its negative is 不應該. 應 is read yīng here.

column3: Should, and "it is one's turn": 该你了 "it's your turn". 该 is shorter than 应该: 该走了 "it's time to go".
column7: It's your turn.
column9: Should, and "it is one's turn": 該你了 "it's your turn". 該 is shorter than 應該: 該走了 "it's time to go".

column3: Must, have to: 你必须来 "you must come". Its negative is 不必 or 不用 "need not", not 不必须.
column7: You must come.
column9: Must, have to: 你必須來 "you must come". Its negative is 不必 or 不用 "need not", not 不必須.

column3: Definitely, must: 明天我一定来 "I will definitely come tomorrow". It goes before the verb, and 一 here is read yī in dictionaries, though people say yí before 定.
column7: I will definitely come tomorrow.
column9: Definitely, must: 明天我一定來 "I will definitely come tomorrow". It goes before the verb, and 一 here is read yī in dictionaries, though people say yí before 定.

column3: A partial denial: 'not always, maybe not'. Alone it is a hedged reply (你去吗？不一定). Mind the order: 不一定 is 'not necessarily', but 一定不 is a firm 'definitely not'.
column7: Expensive is not necessarily good.
column9: A partial denial: 'not always, maybe not'. Alone it is a hedged reply (你去嗎？不一定). Mind the order: 不一定 is 'not necessarily', but 一定不 is a firm 'definitely not'.

column3: Perhaps: 也许他还在睡觉 "perhaps he is still sleeping". It can start a sentence.
column7: Perhaps he is still asleep.
column9: Perhaps: 也許他還在睡覺 "perhaps he is still sleeping". It can start a sentence.

column3: Can only, have no choice but: 我只能等 "I can only wait".
column7: Today I can only wait.
column9: Can only, have no choice but: 我只能等 "I can only wait".

column3: Not OK, won't do: 这样不行 "this won't do". It can also mean "not working". 行 is read xíng. The positive answer is 行.
column7: This won't do.
column9: Not OK, won't do: 這樣不行 "this won't do". It can also mean "not working". 行 is read xíng. The positive answer is 行.

column3: Don't…, and "do not want": 不要说话 "don't talk". 不要 is also "I don't want it": 我不要.
column7: Don't talk.
column9: Don't…, and "do not want": 不要說話 "don't talk". 不要 is also "I don't want it": 我不要.

column3: Not as good as, and "had better": A 不如 B means "A is not as good as B". 走路不如骑车快 "walking is slower than cycling".
column7: Walking is not as fast as cycling.
column9: Not as good as, and "had better": A 不如 B means "A is not as good as B". 走路不如騎車快 "walking is slower than cycling".

column3: Not very: 我不太饿 "I'm not very hungry". It goes before an adjective and softens the denial. 不太好 is a polite way to say "not good".
column7: I'm not very hungry.
column9: Not very: 我不太餓 "I'm not very hungry". It goes before an adjective and softens the denial. 不太好 is a polite way to say "not good".

column3: Doing something on purpose, often something you should not do: 故意迟到, 故意不说话. For a deliberate kind act, say 特意. To apologize, 我不是故意的 'I didn't mean to'. The top of 意 looks like 音 but is etymologically unrelated to it.
column4: 他故意迟到，老师很生气。
column5: 他故意遲到，老師很生氣。
column6: Tā gùyì chídào, lǎoshī hěn shēngqì.
column7: He was late on purpose, and the teacher was angry.
column9: Doing something on purpose, often something you should not do: 故意遲到, 故意不說話. For a deliberate kind act, say 特意. To apologize, 我不是故意的 'I didn't mean to'. The top of 意 looks like 音 but is etymologically unrelated to it.

column3: Take out: 拿 ("take") plus 出 ("out"). 拿出一本书 "take out a book".
column7: He took out a book.
column9: Take out: 拿 ("take") plus 出 ("out"). 拿出一本書 "take out a book".

column3: Get, receive something in hand: 拿到 plus a result: 拿到钱, 拿到手机.
column7: I got my new phone.
column9: Get, receive something in hand: 拿到 plus a result: 拿到錢, 拿到手機.

column3: Obtain, achieve: 取得成绩 "achieve results". It is used for abstract things such as results and success.
column7: He got good results.
column9: Obtain, achieve: 取得成績 "achieve results". It is used for abstract things such as results and success.

column3: Receive, pick up, connect: 接电话 "answer the phone", 接人 "pick someone up".
column7: I'm going to the airport to pick up a friend.
column9: Receive, pick up, connect: 接電話 "answer the phone", 接人 "pick someone up".

column3: Receive, for calls and letters: 接到电话 "get a call". Compare 收到.
column6: Wǒ jiēdào le tā de diànhuà.
column7: I received a call from him.
column9: Receive, for calls and letters: 接到電話 "get a call". Compare 收到.

column3: Accept: 接受礼物, 接受意见 "accept advice". It can also mean "undergo": 接受检查.
column7: I accept your opinion.
column9: Accept: 接受禮物, 接受意見 "accept advice". It can also mean "undergo": 接受檢查.

column3: Receive, something that comes to you: 收到信, 收到礼物. 收 ("take in") plus 到. It is used for mail, messages and gifts.
column6: Nǐ shōudào wǒ de duǎnxìn le ma?
column7: Did you get my text?
column9: Receive, something that comes to you: 收到信, 收到禮物. 收 ("take in") plus 到. It is used for mail, messages and gifts.

column3: The verb plus 到 'arriving at' marks where it ends up: 送到家, 送到机场. It fits a parcel or takeout delivered to your door, and also a person you see to a place: 我送你到门口.
column7: The takeout has been delivered.
column9: The verb plus 到 'arriving at' marks where it ends up: 送到家, 送到機場. It fits a parcel or takeout delivered to your door, and also a person you see to a place: 我送你到門口.

column3: Give as a present: 送 ("give") plus 给 ("to"). 这个送给你 "this is a gift for you". The receiver follows.
column7: This is for you.
column9: Give as a present: 送 ("give") plus 給 ("to"). 這個送給你 "this is a gift for you". The receiver follows.

column3: Hand in, hand over, pay: 交作业 "hand in homework", 交钱 "pay money", 交朋友 "make friends".
column7: Please hand in your homework.
column9: Hand in, hand over, pay: 交作業 "hand in homework", 交錢 "pay money", 交朋友 "make friends".

column3: Hand over to: 交给老师 "hand it to the teacher". 把 often comes before: 把作业交给老师.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zuòyè jiāo gěi lǎoshī.
column7: Please hand your homework to the teacher.
column9: Hand over to: 交給老師 "hand it to the teacher". 把 often comes before: 把作業交給老師.

column3: Raise, bring up, and "carry in the hand": 提问题 "ask a question", 提意见 "make a suggestion", 提前 "in advance". 扌 ("hand") is the meaning part. In daily speech the object is something said or put forward.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng tí yī ge wèntí.
column7: I want to raise a question.
column9: Raise, bring up, and "carry in the hand": 提問題 "ask a question", 提意見 "make a suggestion", 提前 "in advance". 扌 ("hand") is the meaning part. In daily speech the object is something said or put forward.

column3: Put forward a question, suggestion or demand: 提 ("raise") plus 出 ("out"). 提出意见 "make a suggestion". The thing put forward is abstract.
column6: Tā tíchū le yī ge hǎo yìjiàn.
column7: He put forward a good suggestion.
column9: Put forward a question, suggestion or demand: 提 ("raise") plus 出 ("out"). 提出意見 "make a suggestion". The thing put forward is abstract.

column3: Mention, refer to: 提 plus 到. 他提到了你 "he mentioned you". It goes with a person or a topic.
column6: Tā tídào le nǐ de míngzi.
column7: He mentioned your name.
column9: Mention, refer to: 提 plus 到. 他提到了你 "he mentioned you". It goes with a person or a topic.

column3: Covers 'keep for later' (留一点) and 'stay behind' (留在家里), and with 下 it is 留下. It builds 留学 'study abroad', 留言 'leave a message' and 留意 'pay attention'.
column4: 菜很多，给爸爸留一点吧。
column5: 菜很多，給爸爸留一點吧。
column6: Cài hěn duō, gěi bàba liú yīdiǎn ba.
column7: There's a lot of food, so let's leave some for Dad.
